And I've been to most of the area pizza joints, if only just to explore and compare. The only thing stopping me from eating this every meal until I turn into a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle is my own conscience, keeping me at bay. THE SERVICE: OK, this is what keeps my review from the full 5-stars-- and it's not even really the employees and their handling of customers. It's the process, and it's f---ed up. I write about it in my reviews all the time, if a place has to resort to calling out a customers' order ten times before they realize it and go to pick it up, something's wrong. Maybe it's the physical layout of the place-- narrow and uncomfortable where the ordering/pickup takes place, maybe it's the half-wit customers who will stand there and WATCH these guys call out their food, maybe it's me, the easily-irritated ignoramus of a reviewer. I think if they separated the eat-in's from the take-out's and gave the eat-in's a number and had their food brought to them, it would make things go smoother. THE PRICE: Totally worth it, worth the wait, worth the epic battle through a gauntlet of gluttons and gangstas, worth the mind-bending riddle of how/when you can give your $10 for 2 specialty slices and a snapple, you may finally emerge triumphantly with your food, like Harold & Kumar and White Castle...savor the spoils of victory my friend...savor them, you've earned it. text: I'm a little surprised at the previous reviews. I'm an avid yelper, and usually trust the reviews I read ESPECIALLY regarding the Philly restaurant scene because i take my food seriously. did i mention that i love food? I made an 8:00 reservation on a Saturday night and we got there early and the restaurant was bumpin'. That was understandable because its fairly new. Figured we'd wait a good 15 min, half hour tops. But nobody was moving... shouldn't tables be turned faster when you only serve small tapas style plates? We waited over an hour dropping mad loot at the bar til we got seated. Were drinks comped? No... they caught on after our last round and decided to send us a couple complimentary apps to make up for it... Edamame dumplings (tasty, but heavy on the butter) and a philly cheesesteak roll (could they have done something more original? so many other philly eateries serve this app!) So did I mention how much I love food? Well my fellow diners in my crew love it JUST as much. We frequent many of Philly's finest restaurants all across the board...up to NY and even international spots where we sample dishes we wanna see back home. Now, our main reason for going to Sampan was to get our much anticipated Ramen dish and the Chili crab, ( which prior to dining at Sampan,, I could only partake of these two dishes in NYC). We ordered a few other dishes and they just didn't leave the greatest taste in our mouth... I can't fault everything..a few were decent. But here's the thing, the decent dishes were just NOT memorable. Those that were memorable were the really bad ones. The brussel sprouts and bacon were burnt... and super duper salty along with the chili crab. Which was ridiculously drowned in some sort of oyster sauce and where was the crab? It was like diggin for gold. Here we were, waiting for some whole crabs in their shell simmering in a red spicy chili sauce, because wasn't there chili in the description? Well, all we saw were some dried noodles over a salty mess with itty bitty bits of crabmeat which was not fresh... Another downer was the ramen...oooh the ramen. Did you really have to serve it lukewarm? And did you really have to serve the instant pack of noodles? Only those who've had REAL Japanese ramen know that the noodles are fresh and totally cannot be bought in your local grocery store was another salty disappointment. I have no idea how much water we wound up drinking. The wait staff was receptive to our feedback and disappointment... gave us a couple comped dessert options, but to our dismay could not make the disappointments disappear. While they did comp the dishes that were not to our liking, we got the bill and SERIOUSLY? how do you spend that much money on tapas dishes that weren't worth it? Especially when we waited so long at the bar and already dropped mad loot to begin with. Sampan, there are SO many better restaurants out there, so you better step up your game and take the feedback to heart. You will thank us later...and maybe we can give it another shot if you're around in the next 6 months. If you want to know what real ramen tastes like go to: Ippudo in NYC www.ippudo.com/ny/ - If you want some real chili crab goodness go to: Fatty Crab in NYC www.fattycrab.com

text: We had dinner at Meridian last night and it was quite good. The atmosphere was cool. The building is a 2 story log cabin that, according to their website, was built in 1880. It has an upscale but down home feel. For dinner we split the tuna poke appetizer and the house salad. The poke was very good. Pretty standard as tuna poke goes. I really liked the house salad. It was made with mixed greens, tomatoes, dried fruit and a maple vinaigrette that was so tasty. For our main entrees, I had the pumpkin swordfish that was delicious. It was grilled and on top of a hash made of sweet potatoes, brussel sprout leaves, pearl onions & bacon and surrounded by a romesco sauce. So so good. Allegedly pumpkin swordfish is a rare version of swordfish that has an orange tinge to it & is supposedly sweeter than regular swordfish. Whatever it was, it was tasty. My bfriend had the lamb loin. It was prepared in a mediterraean style with tzatziki & eggplant puree and a chickpea cake on the side. I thought the lamb was a bit chewy but had great flavor overall. We also had a side of mac & cheese which was yummy. We were too stuffed for dessert but next time I go, I'm getting one (or more). They had quite a few options and the ones I saw other people order looked really good. The wine list had a nice selection in a range of prices with wines from all over the world. Our server was very friendly, well versed in the menu and wine list and attentive.

text: Hype, Hype, Hype. This was my first trip to the land of "Brotherly Love". I had a mission: to get all the cheese steaks I could in a week, then make my decision who (to me) was the best of four. This over hyped place came in last. I had never heard of this place and I wish I never had. The people who recommended Geno's saw it on TV. I read some reviews, paid attention to the bad ones, and wanted to try The Tourist Trap". My GF, her BFF and I had of all intentions of making this our first stop. We landed on Saturday morning, unpacked and headed right to the area. We were gonna do the Geno's/Pat's spit and get both, but the lines were outrageous. Pat's went around the building and Geno's was on the other block. Eh, well come later on in the week. During that time we sneaked in two places, so I did have a gauge to work of off. The next time we went, the line was considerably smaller. Pat's line was also smaller so we did the split. I go to Geno's and they go to Pat's. During this time I was told about the owner's (who is obviously of an immigrant decent) rants about being "American" and the importance of speaking English while ordering. I was even thinking of making up some weird accent, like Borat, to see what would happen. In my heart I wanted to have fun, but I really wanted to eat the "cheese steak" with out any fuss. Plus in the back of my head, I could hear my GF giving me crap for even thinking it. While in line noticed all of the Star F**ker's pictures all spread out like, well, like cheese. Pictures of "famous" and people I had never heard of, all of which had signatures. Who cares? Way too much Hollywood fluff going on for me. On the sidewalk was a memorial for some of the police officers who have died in the line of duty, interesting. I'm looking for the famous sticker, but not at the order window. Apparently, there are two order windows. One for the cheese steak, the other for the drinks and fries. Both counter people were rude, I have an idea why, and were very short. At the window for the cheese steak, I told the behemoth of a man, which one I wanted (Provolone), before I got my change back, the sandwich was being given to me. Interesting. Not sure if they were pre-made or just fast. Like cattle, you walk to the next window. There I had to tell the behemoth of a woman what I wanted to drink. Before I could utter a word, a guy comes from behind me and states he didn't get one of his sodas. She replies, "You didn't get it". This clever meeting of the minds lasted for 5 min. The witty exchange between the two ended by the man finally getting his soda. Walking away I finally notice the sticker. I really won't repeat it. I still feel nauseous thinking about the meaning and the history of signs like that. "Whites Only", "No Mexicans" so on. Armed with my "famous" Geno's cheese steak, a drink, and fries. I notice that grease is seeping though the bag. Are you serious?! The last two sandwiches had little to no grease. Walking to Pat's I find my BF and her buddy. They grab a seat to wait for me. Sitting there, I pull out the Geno's sandwich and my GF made her famous "eeewwww" face. We had to rush to Independence Hall cause we had tickets for a tour. So my GF BFF decides to drive while we sit in the back seat to sample our food. Let me put it this way; It sucked. If you decide to make public rant about your own controversial political views, you had better have the best Philly Cheese Steak in the world, the universe, to back you up. I could have gotten a better tasting sandwich at one of the Greek places in Montebello. It was bland. No flavor whatsoever. The bread was soggy from being saturated by grease. If I knew the life span on this thing was 10 minutes, we would have eaten it on the way to the car. Please, stay away from the hype. No picture wear taken. It was so shiny, it would have been like taking a pic of the sun.
label: NEG

text: I hate to shoot something down right out of the gate I went on one of two special opening nights just for FaceBook fans but I was not impressed by the food which is after all the main reason you go to a restaurant. I ordered a frozen margarita which was virtually flavorless. The chips and salsa arrived at the table & while the chips were the ones I love, light & crispy, the salsa was missing something, maybe some acid, & too heavy on other things. It was a fresh salsa but it had little tomato flavor & really not even much heat. For our free appetizer we chose the chile con queso. DH ordered the sopapilla chicken & I had the green corn tamale with a chipotle shrimp taco. Our waiter was excellent overall, trying to make up for food not coming out of the kitchen in a timely manner. He brought us the cheese wedges which he had described earlier as a flat bread or sort of pizza with cheeses. The menu said it came with a side of hatch chile peppers if I recall correctly. Well, it was a flour tortilla that was smothered in cheeses with some lettuce in the center & some sour cream. It was lacking flavor. DH, who NEVER salts food, salted it twice & even put black pepper on it. We wound up asking for some chile peppers to go on it & got a little ramekin of chile peppers that seemed to be stewed & had very little flavor or heat but they did add a little to the appetizer. The tortilla was barely cooked & that caused the cheese to make it somewhat soggy. Another minute or two in the fryer/griddle would have made all the difference in the world as would a light sprinkling of salt when it came from the fryer/griddle. Our entrees arrived shortly after that. I will admit that the masa mixture on my tamale was the best I have had in Nashville. However, that being said, it was still disappointing. There really wasn't much filling & while there were some green chiles on it, it wasn't a sauce like I had expected from the menu description & it was smeared with sour cream. The chipotle shrimp taco was surprisingly different than what I had expected. There were four pieces of shrimp, some of which were burned, along with some raw cabbage that could have been sliced finer to make it easier to eat, & a little bacon in a sort of sad looking 'crispy' corn tortilla shell. I wound up picking the shrimp & bacon out. DH was surprised by the shrimp, they were very fresh, cooked well except for the burnt side, and they weren't the smoky hot chipotle flavor that he doesn't like. Instead they were more sweet with very little heat. It needed something to pull it together, a sauce of some sort. I believe I saw a baja sauce on one dish, perhaps something like that would help the taco. But what was really the big disappointment was the 'refried' beans which I hate to even call refried. They were so soupy that they could hardly be refried, it was more like slightly mashed up cooked pinto beans with way to much of their cooking liquid. Again, the seasoning was off with too much cumin. And here's the kicker, with almost all the entrees at $10, the actual entrees are small portions but you get a good half a plate of these beans. DH's sopapilla chicken was a small square pocket with chicken. The flavor there was pretty good but again, I think it could stand a sauce option. And here again, the flour tortilla was barely fried. It really needed a couple of additional minutes in the fryer to give it the crispness that it needed. It was not really what I would call a stuffed sopapilla as from what I saw, it looked like a chimichanga but rather than rolled like most restaurants do it, it was simply a flour tortilla folded around a chicken mixture into a bundle & fried. Our chile con queso arrived after out entrees & was nothing outstanding again lacking flavor. And again, DH added salt & black pepper to it in order to get some flavor going. They also described it as being served fondue style. I am not sure what they think fondue style is but it was just served warm in a bowl sitting in the middle of a dish with more warm tortilla chips around it. Finally, they brought us an order of complimentary sopapillas & here we go again, they were not cooked long enough. They barely had any color to them just like all the other fried dishes. They had little to no crispness to them. They were very light and flaky but as you tried to tear a corner off to fill with honey, they tore into pieces. Overall, our waiter was trying his best. The kitchen is not firing on all cylinders yet. The food was very average, the portions small, & the prices high. I might wait a few months & possibly try it again hoping that these are just kinks that will get worked out.
label: NEG

text: For a special treat, my work took a few of us out to Ruth's Chris for dinner. For many of my colleagues, it was their first time at the establishment. I had been once previously, shortly after it first opened. My memory didn't fail me, we were in for a feast! We were greeted by the owner, who gave us a brief tour of the basement and the vaults. There are two vault rooms, one of which the owners themselves had to jack hammer the ceiling of in order to heighten the roof and put in a lighting fixture. Both vaults still have their original doors, but the doors have been propped open - so no fear about getting locked in! We sat in the first vault room, which fit the 10 of us with ease. The servers were friendly, fun, and eager to explain the menu and make suggestions. My friend and I started with a pair of blue crab cakes, which were moist and flavourful. I got the tenderloin, which is American beef. When Ruth's Chris first opened, many people were upset a restaurant would have the gall to serve American beef when our Alberta beef is so well-known and delicious. They do have two Alberta beef options, but the options are over-shadowed by the USDA options. The corn-fed American tenderloin was delicious and a bit sweeter, but the cooking in butter is a little bit much. It does make a great treat, but I'll stick to Alberta beef. The sides are ordered extra, and come in a large family size order intended for 3-4 people. I tried the mushrooms, asparagus with hollandaise sauce, broiled tomato, and broccoli gratin. The broccoli and asparagus dishes were very tasty, with the asparagus definitely being a must-order for me. The broiled tomato is sweet, and more sugary than I remembers. The mushrooms were not for me. For dessert, creme brulee! Exactly how creme brulee should be. Ruth's Chris is a fantastic date and dinner location in our city. Definitely higher scale, so expect to spend minimum $100 per person. The food is scrumptious, the atmosphere is great, and the staff are amazing. Very out of my price range, but also a place I'd love to return to!

Don't expect to find your fancy ingredients (ie: goat cheese) but if it is part of Southern or West Indian cuisine you should be good. The prepared food selection is piping hot and ready to devour. The poor waitress, who DID write it down and DID tell the Sushi Chef BEFORE he made it, felt so bad that she spoke with the Owner (lady) and they took the roll off of our bill, and then had the Sushi chef make another one for me. But wait, it gets better... He didn't make me a new roll. He simply made a 1/4 roll and simply left out the Avocado on the 2 new pieces that he made, but the original 4 pieces were STILL on the plate WITH the Avocado in them! That action alone is grounds for a lawsuit based on deliberate life endangerment. As if it wasn't bad enough that we had to cut our dinner short so that I could get home and get some medicine so I didn't go into anaphylactic shock (which has happened to me before from avocado), but then the fact that this prick of a Sushi Chef didn't do his job properly and deliberately left the avocado pieces in my food is enough to warrant talking to an attorney and seeking legal actions against him and the restaurant. text: How do you welcome the 200+ people that you helped teach the ways of Yelp to over a weekend? By writing a review for the event that you did it at of course! For better and worse I've followed WXPN for years (shout out to my friend Robert Drake!). But for whatever strange reason I haven't been to a an XPoNential Festival until this year. But I've always made note of how the diversity of the lineup always managed to successfully reflect upon the diversity of the station. And off the bat I'll also add that although I jumped upon the opportunity to be the point man at the Yelp Table with an enthusiastic HELL YES the moment that Monica asked me; They Might Be Giants, Peter Bjorn & John, East Hundred, Illinois and many others would have had me seeing it anyway. I do have to give it up to the dedication XPN puts into setting up the festival, Since I've walked through Wiggins Park as a bare bones park when leaving the Tweeter (whatever it's called) Center before (and will be reviewing now that I know what it's called), I can honestly attest to the fact that NO part of the stages, or any of the booths are there when the festival isn't in session. So that gives you the start of understanding how much they put into it. But when you factor in things like the entire fest being broad-casted on air, how they accommodate it's volunteers and sponsors during the fest, and then some it becomes abundantly clear. and the effort that WXPN puts into shows throughout. In the end I was beyond thrilled with getting to see TMBG and Peter Bjorn & John for the first time ever, and I also enjoyed getting reacquainted with local favorites like East Hundred and Gillian Grassie (swoon). But I also had the chance to discover new favorites like Perkasie and The Hold Steady. I'm not going to lie and pretend that things like the burnt burger with cheese whiz, the random bouts of rain, The Bacon Brothers, and the crowd who came to see Toby Keith play the Center of Evil Ticket Bastard didn't make me want to grab a shovel and bury myself. But over all the festival made for an absolutely AMAZING weekend. And I got to spend it all alongside some pretty awesome yelpers, which made for a priceless occasion.

text: The restaurant is wonderful. The decor is clean and somewhat simple. I liked the high ceilings and the old iron windows are nice. They picked a great old building to open this restaurant. The menu is simple and and clean too, I liked it. Although there are fewer options to choose from it seems like everyone can find something they would like. Somehow I felt as if we were eating healthier, even though my grilled cheese and his burger was just about as fattening as any other we have ever eaten. The ingredients and the presentation of the food give it a healthy feel. Possibly the special thanks on the menu to the local farms that helped contribute did it too :) For me I think it was the fact that my grilled cheese was on a really thick fluffy wheat bread instead of a traditional white or sourdough. It was a really unique grilled cheese like none I have ever eaten in a restaurant or even at home. The salad that came with it (you choose either salad or shoestrings) filled half the plate and was very fresh. I would have liked a little more flavor to the dressing though. I also tried the shoestring fries of the person I was eating with and they are very fluffy and not overly greasy at all. They provide room-temp water in a bottle at your table which is a much better approach than the way Voila does it where it is sitting at all the tables waiting for a customer to drink it. We also tried their (I forget what it is called) vanilla and cranberry desert which was very good and just the right size for the both of us to share at the end of a very filling meal. Service was great as well, they had staff making the rounds at all times (but not bothering the customers, just checking) to make sure everything was running smoothly. The price for the both of us was not bad. Almost $40 - keep in mind we had beers and dessert too. I was a little worried because I had been hearing from other people that they were expensive. I guess it is all a matter of opinion from the people you are hearing things from though! Oh, and they get extra thumbs up from me for carrying Great Basin's Icky!

text: Foodies, I know what you're thinking when you hear this place is in Meadowood mall. UGHHH mall food....greasy fast food, deep-fried overly saucy asian food, and ridiculously outfitted super sweet lemon-aide sellers...but be prepared to enter 775 Gastropub and forget that you're even in the mall. I like beer, a lot, but I am quite indecisive and when you put a huge list of beer in front of me I tend to get baffled and noncommittal about what I want...so I usually ask for a recommendation....the waitress recommended some raspberry beer to me that was just not my kind of drink, it tasted like cough syrup, but I should have known I wouldn't like it considering I'm not a super sweet drink kind of girl. But other than that mishap everything here has been rather excellent... House sangria hit the spot on a hot day, seared duck breast was probably my favorite thing I've had so far, swordfish caesar salad had nice crisp romaine and the burgers are huge and satisfying. I think they still use grain finished beef, so I hope they can step that up to grass finished in the future... This place is still a big step down from Sezmu and 4th St. Bistro for me but it's great that more restaurants supporting local and organic food are opening in Reno...Oh and my roommate was a little put off by their name, gastropub made her think of stomach juices, so don't let that deter you either!
label: POS

text: Great store for wine, they have tons of well organized and categorized wines, good prices and a really cool and helpful staff. text: I have a friend who's been to every "cool/unique/off the beaten path" spot in Philly. So, while I can impress my less in-the-know friends with random urban discoveries, this one buddy keeps me on my toes. I finally one-upped her at Carman's. It was actually the first time I'd been there too. We walked into this diminutive diner (there's bar seating for about 4-6 people -there's no liquor though- and a few tables) and were seated right away. Our server came over, asked for our names and proceeded to rattle off the specials. I can't remember exactly what they were, but I got the feeling that Carman's the type of woman who goes shopping the day before and buys whatever's fresh. Figuring out what to make with it seems like an afterthought. Somehow she manages to pair the most unlikely items together and keep it delicious. There's subtle penis iconography strewn throughout the diner. It doesn't come off as tasteless though. While I was sitting at the table, I remember looking out the window and glancing over a little plush piggie. How darling! Upon closer inspection, his little bits were hanging out. "Carman puts the C U N(ext) T(uesday) back into country." That's what the sign reads, folks. Oh! You can call in advance and have your name put on the waiting list. There never seems to be too long of a wait though.
label: POS

text: This place makes me sad. It has the potential and perhaps the history to make it a landmark of the Philadelphia culinary scene. But it has wronged me so many times with undercooked doughy slices that i have to knock it down two stars and then add another one for being open mad late. It is perfect in so many ways for a late night pizza joint. Quick unfriendly service. No toppings, just a fast slice of pizza to eat on the fly. I love that. And when Lorenzo's is on point, it is one of the best and only classic elephant ear slices in the city. But in order to get a slice of pizza there that represents the full nature of their talents, you need to get a slice at 3 in the afternoon, when they actually bother to cook the pizza. If you are in line at 2:15 with all the other drunk dillholes, you should expect a laughably undercooked slice that when eaten tastes more like a pizza burrito than anything else. And that's just because they know you're drunk and that you probably won't notice or care what you eat. So before you judge this place's pizza, you should hit it up during the off-peak hours, but any criticism anyone gives of this place is well deserved, cause they don't respect their own reputation. I remain a stubborn fan, but they have seriously gone downhill of late.
label: POS

text: SAMBUCA is sultry and has a slow sizzle to it. Dark, romantic, spacious seating, old world sytle, it reminds me of a House of the Blues meets Spainish riviera, with black leather and red satin and velvet, very relaxed and with sexy undertones. Smooth Brazilian jazz was playing and the upstair outdoor areas were full of minglers, mincing about the canopy and curtained seating, that overlooks the busy street corner below. The patio is great for a quiet conversation before going inside for the music. I had the salmon and my friend had a pizza, the salads were great, mine spinach-fresh & tasty. The salmon was very good in a honey terraki glaze over rice, very nice. SAMBUCA has great atmosphere and good food, that will put you into a good mood, at the end of your work day. Prices are reasonable for food and typical for drinks. The menu could be larger and more diversified.On-site Valet parking was helpful. Is it a dinner club I'd do again?, Oh YEAH!

text: Five Guys is a chain which hails from Virginia. They've received many local awards there, and it's easy to taste why once you bite into one of their burgers or dogs. While you wait for your order to be yelled out, fill up your fountain drink and snack on complimentary peanuts at your table. On several occasions I've ordered their hot dogs with the works and I've always left satisfied. Today, I ordered a little bacon cheeseburger with jalapenos, fried onions, and sauteed mushrooms. Note that their meats are always cooked well-done - whether for liability reasons or style, who can say! While Five Guys is a chain, it is not any less for it. As long as their staff follows process, you will get the same gem, each time you order, every time! Recommended for lunch.

text: The food at Modo Mio makes it worth the waiting, frenzied staff, and tight dining area. Everything, down to the simple spaghetti ragu, tasted delicious, albeit a little on the salty side. The portions are small enough and cheap enough to try many dishes...and the menu could definitely be approached in a small plates/tapas way if you wanted. The restaurant itself was very crowded and the wait significant on a friday night, but the atmosphere is generally festive and everyone is offered free sambuca shots before leaving. Especially since their menu changes frequently, it's definitely a place worth going back to.

text: I always have the vague sensation that I'm being mocked when I'm at Plump's. I'm not paranoid; I think there is a bit of a holier-than-thou attitude among the servers here. Once while I was hanging out with a former coworker, he went to the bathroom and the bartender asked me with a smirk if we were on a first date. He said it in such a way that made me think there was some kind of a bet going on down the bar. (I guess this was funny because there was an obvious age difference between my friend and I...?) Still, I would've gone easy on Plump's because of its location and expansive deck, but a recent visit for a pre-prandial beverage finally completely turned me off. The bartender this time looked at me blankly when I tried to order some bourbon drinks that were listed on cards on the table. They do give their cocktails a generous pour, but you get plastic cups on the weekends apparently. I don't know, I guess maybe that's a practical decision for some businesses, but there's something just really tacky about drinking out of plastic cups inside a bar. Finally, as a design choice, I'm not feeling the basketball memorabilia, which is looking a little worn around the edges at this point. The story of Plump's game-winning shot and the last ascension of a small school to a statewide title is neat, but would I build a business around it? No.

text: I've often had talks about how Reno food is OK, but nothing has stood out for me to be like "OMFG, this is IT! I have to drive 4 hours just to eat this!". That was until I met Eclipse Pizza this past Saturday. Hands down the BEST pizza joint I've been to in a long time. We took a cab here from Grand Sierra, so we wouldn't have to worry about DUI's. Total cab fare was $25 one way. When we walked in, the place was pretty tiny. There was only 3 small tables with 2 seats at each, so 6 total. Upstairs they had about 5 more tables. I think the max seated is 25. You order at the counter with "I think", the owner. I always thought these restaurants that come up on the top few pages of Yelp pay to be there, but the owner has never heard of Yelp, and even had to write it down. We ordered the Apple Goat Cheese salad (mixed greens, apples, cherry tomatoes, sun dried tomatoes, dried cranberries, candied pecans, goat cheese, and champagne vinaigrette dressing), the medium Ironman Pizza (pesto, mozzarella, pineapples, jalapenos, sausages), and a bottle of Mia's Playground Old Vine Zinfandel. Total for the bill was under $45. I'm not a veggie person, and I swear, "mixed greens" to me looks like weeds out of someone's front lawn. But the balance in this salad was insane. I had to memorize the ingredients, so I can toss my own salad at home. :) We were so impressed by the salad, that we were afraid the pizza would fail us, but this was the best pizza I've had in a long time. Every ingredient perfectly balanced the next ingredient, and the crust was perfectly crispy, with a chewy center. No cutting up the roof of your mouth here. The amazing thing is it stayed crispy from the first bite, all the way to the last bite (about 1.5 hours later, since we were sipping on wine while we ate). I would recommend this to everyone, and will come back here every time I visit Reno. I want to try all their pizzas and salads! Oh, the wine was a perfect pairing for the pizza as well. The owners here put a lot of thought into their concept, and their personality shines through in the preparation of their pizza. We talked about their pizza the whole way home on Sunday, and hubby even texted me for the ingredients this morning, so he can make the same thing at work.
label: POS

text: We selected this boarding facility and vet based on my cat vet's recommendation. Sadly, I should have asked around more. After our initial vet visit, we decided to use their boarding service. When we went to pick up our dog after boarding, the front desk had to call the boarding facility three times to tell them to bring out our dog. We could tell he lost weight during his stay as soon as we saw him. He was limping as we walked to our car. In the next few days, he developed diarrhea and vomiting. We notified the hospital who told us to bring him in to be evaluated to determine whether his injury and illness was the result of the stay. When we went to our appointment, they did not have any records from our previous vet visit, no record of our phone calls about the dog's injury and illness, and they had not scheduled us to see a vet. They reran tests that they had run previously and charged us for everything. A few days later, a large red cyst appeared on our dog's foot. If the vet had actually looked at our dog's foot, they might have found it. We will not use the boarding service or the vet service again.

I love the toppings combos they offer. We usually split the pizza 50/50 and end up with half BBQ chicken & half potato, makes a strange but great combo. I honestly haven't ever had a bad flavor combo here though, they've got a solid line up of pizza toppings. I've done both take away & eat in here. Eating in is great because it has a nice old house vibe and, now that the endless construction across the street is done, one of the best patios in town. They're also really reliable for take away - you get what you ordered and you can depend on it being cooked properly every time. The staff are great as well, whether you're eating in or taking away. I also think the prices are totally reasonable for the types of pizzas they serve here. This isn't Pizza Hut quality, it's a ton better and yes, you do pay more for it. They do run specials sometimes that can really cut the cost - right now 50% off your entire bill on Fridays from 4-6 pm, dine in only. text: First off their rates increase continually (and only sometimes do they let you know about it). I was signed up as a "young adult" or something like that until I turned 24, at which time I was supposed to receive notification that my rate would increase to the normal adult price. I never received this notification, even though my membership rate increased by $15 a month, yet when the price went up by $1 a month for all members I received a letter. When you finally arrive at the gym you'll note there are barely enough parking spots. Snow removal was mediocre at best and many spots STILL have piles of snow in them, despite the fact there is probably less than 6" of snow covering non-treated surfaces at this point. They do nothing to tow cars that are illegally parked, even if legally parked cars are severely parked in. Coming into the building the locker rooms are either packed and/or filthy. I once saw a used "swimmy" diaper on the floor of the women's locker room. I complained about this, cleanliness was good, then less then a month later I saw piles of empty wrappers and old papers all over the floors of the locker room once again (luckily no swimmy diaper that time). I complained again and have yet to hear anything about it, although once again it appears the locker rooms are clean. So you think, finally, I can forget all this, put my things in a locker, and work out? Nope! Most of the electronic lockers are broken so you can leave your things there but cannot lock the door (probably pretty risky!). Much of the exercise equipment is taken, often by children who are too young (by the YMCA's own rules!) to even be in the gym. The Y staff seems willing to remove them, but only when asked, and they only move them to another machine which will most likely inconvenience the next person looking for that type of machine. The mats are packed as well and often I can't find the free weights I want to use as they only have one or two sets of each for the entire facility. To add insult to injury you'll see tours of prospective members go through constantly while working out! This is crazy considering how over-subscribed the gym currently is! Want to go swimming? Forget about it! The indoor pools are often closed for swim meets (that don't even involve members, these are for h.s. teams!) or at least 50% of lap lanes are taken up by lessons/practices! If you submit a complaint to the complaint box, unless it's as minor as changing a TV channel, you'll most likely never see a response to it posted. The two complaints I made were never responded to. The responses I do see are mostly excuses and offer no concrete ways in which the Y will try to improve itself. It's really a shame, the place was great when I joined about 6 mos ago, but now it's over subscribed and is rapidly going downhill. Unless you like paying $60/mo for broken equipment, a lack of parking, a lack of cleanliness, and generally a lack of customer service, I'd avoid it!

text: I came here on July 2nd with four others. Decor was simple, noise level was unremarkable. Space was a bit small--I was sitting with my back to a wall, and servers kept squeezing past me. Our server was helpful, although he never seemed to make eye contact and seemed to close his eyes whenever talking. Maybe that's how Cypriots are and he was just trying to give us a more authentic experience? We got the Greek salad, dips of the day, bureki, and halloumi for appetizers. The salad was moderately sized and pretty standard. (I think the one at Dmitri's is a better value.) I'm not entirely sure what the dips were, but I believe there was a lentil one, a chickpea/anchovy one, and a pumpkin one. We all disagreed about which one we liked best, but we thought all of them were good. We had to ask for more pita for dipping, which they didn't charge for. The bureki (fillo pastry stuffed with feta and thyme, drizzled with thyme honey, served with roast beets ) had a nice sweet/salty thing going on, and I liked the herbaceousness, but it was a bit small to share 5 ways. It seemed expensive for the size, but maybe that's also because we were splitting it. The beets seemed a bit like an afterthought. The halloumi was interesting--I didn't realize that it doesn't really melt. Again, not the best appetizer to split. Of the apps, dips of the day was the winner. One additional note--they brought out bread with tahini, and I feel like the timing was off--either they brought it just before or at the same time as the rest of the appetizers, or a refill was slow. Also, nobody poured our wine for us, and we wound up pouring our own. Neither really bothered us, but I like to nitpick. For entrees, we got two veal flank steaks, a pork chop, a quail, and a duck leg. I had the veal. All the meat was well-cooked, well-seasoned and amply portioned, and the accompaniments were well-executed also. I'm hesitant to say it, because everyone was happy with their food, but I think most of us agreed that the mains were still somewhat unremarkable; maybe they lacked some defining Greekness that we were expecting. I'd never had quail, so I did enjoy the richness, and people who tried the duck really liked it (the piece I tried was really too small to get much duckiness). For dessert, we got the date and chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream and caramel sauce, the galatoboureko (filo pastry with semolina custard), and the assortment of Cypriot pastries. The chocolate cake was amazing--extremely moist, chocolatey, with a faint trace of date flavor. The vanilla ice cream and caramel sauce weren't the most imaginative things, but they were good and worked well with the cake. I really enjoyed the custard as well--it reminded me of creme brulee, almost, with a thick, rich texture and fairly subtle flavor. The pastries had baklava, which was really good--it had cinnamon in it, which made it stand out from other baklava I've had. There were also almond cookies, which were okay, but not too exciting, and some sort of cake that was sort of dense/dry and not as sweet as I would've liked it. As we were leaving, we were preparing to stuff a bottle of wine we wound up not opening in a purse, and a server (not ours) stopped me and gave me a...fabric wine tote? I don't know what it's called, but he said that people are always leaving them at the restaurant and we could have this so our chilled wine wouldn't warm up on the way home. It was a nice touch. Total came out to about $45/person including tax and tip, and most portions were reasonable/generous. Overall, this was a solid restaurant. I'd been looking forward to it for awhile. Although not everything lived up to my built-up hopes, just about everything was at least good, and a few things really were excellent.

text: I have a major axe to grind with said establishment and how poorly they handled a snafu from way back when. (If only Yelp had existed back in the day!) It was a typically crowded Saturday night, and parking was of course at a premium. So instead of circling around for parking for 30 minutes, I caved and decided to hand my keys over to the valet. Fast-forward to the end of our meal, where our waiter told us to give him my claim check when we were ready to settle the bill so he could give the valet a heads up to bring our car around. We did so, which would have worked fine, except for the fact that it took a good 20 minutes for our waiter to bring my credit card back so I could sign the bill and leave. This triggered a most frustrating chain of events. Under the assumption that we would be out in a few minutes, the valet brought my car around in a timely manner, but when I didn't show up soon after (because the waiter was moving at a snail's pace), he left my car in the middle of the dark street with the keys in the ignition and the driver's door partially open. WOW - you might as well have put a sign on it that said, "Please steal me." Knowing how New Orleans is, I'm frankly shocked that the car didn't get stolen. But it gets worse: not only was my car abandoned and ready to be stolen at any time, but it was also blocking traffic (darn narrow Warehouse District streets), so I got a parking ticket. As I'm finally leaving the restaurant, someone outside informed me of what just happened with my car, and of course, I'm furious. (I was a broke college student at the time, so a parking ticket was certainly not a welcome added expense for the evening's activities.) The brilliant valet who ditched my car resurfaced and made excuses for why he left it. I soon realized that I was going to have to escalate the matter to management to get any sort of resolution and was irritated enough, so decided to go home, regroup and try to get this resolved the next day. I first started with calling the restaurant, who so adroitly played the blame game and said that it's not their fault (even though it was their waiter who delayed me getting out the door) and that the valets are from another company that I would have to contact. I then reached out to the valet company, who pretty much said they couldn't do anything about what happened. Nice. As a last resort, I tried contesting the parking ticket with the city of New Orleans (It's all about the principle of the situation!), which, in their infinite wisdom, they rejected my claim. Being the tenacious one, I decided to go back to square one and approach the restaurant again, but in person this time. I showed up during a quiet afternoon and politely asked to speak to the manager. He showed up soon after, and listened as I calmly explained what happened. After I finished my story, I was appalled by how he responded, talking to me as if he were calming an upset child and using such platitudes as "oh baby" and " sweetie, I'm so sorry." I did not appreciate being talked down to like that, and that was the last straw. (As Ms. Janet says, "No, my name ain't baby!") The smarmy manager said that he would refund my money once I mailed in the documentation, but after being talked to in such a manner, I was done. At that point, I was happy to take a financial hit from the parking ticket just so I wouldn't have to deal with that awful manager again. And, this incident aside, your sushi ain't all that.

text: Cocktails: Inventive, tasty, fun and all come in around $8-9. I had the 'Jazz Club' to start- tasty, but probably wouldn't get it again. My friend started with the 'Miles Davis Fizz'- this one was interesting. I only had a sip, but it was good...wouldn't get a whole on myself though. I then moved on to the 'In A Pickle.' I'm not a huge specialty cocktail drinker, but this one might have converted me. It sounded interesting and the server encouraged me to try it. I'm glad I did! It was a delicious drink that only got better the further I got into it. Can't wait to have another. My friend wanted something coffee-y or chocolaty for her second drink, but nothing was on the menu. We asked the server and a few minutes later he came out with a nice little chocolaty cocktail concoction (they didn't have any coffee at the bar). Food: While nothing will fill you up, the have some tasty snacks. We got the cheese plate which comes with bread and 3 small chunks of different cheeses and ours came with a raisin/grape compote. The white cheddar coupled with the compote was great. We also went for the special: Lambs tongue bruschetta. Sounded a bit weird, but I like lamb, so what the heck. the tongue had a nice smokey flavor and there was a nice tang in there as well from what turned out to be some sort of lemon and something else cabbage. Good Stuff. Service: Our server was excellent - attentive but not overbearing. Would educate us when we asked or looked puzzled about something, but never showed off, and made good suggestions. It is exactly what you want every time you go out to dinner. It was nice going there on a Tuesday as it wasn't as busy as I'm sure it gets on the weekends. We sat outside and only had a couple of other people out there throughout the night. Go and enjoy!
label: POS

text: The Fresh Grocer is my unofficial-official after party. Open 24 hours, if someone with a car wants to drive me to Fresh Grocer at 2:30am when there's nothing else to do I'm all for it. If you think this sounds like a lame way to spend a late Friday or Saturday night, you're wrong. Fresh Grocer is full of and surrounded by entertainment. There are homeless people sleeping up on the cushioned benches by the bathrooms. The bathrooms smell so clean it's hard to breathe over the scent of sanitation. (That doesn't mean they ARE clean.) The aisles are organized so that they only time they make sense is after a night spent imbibing. They have the worst selection of frozen pizza ever. When I was there are 3am on Friday night, I saw a dude who resembled Carrot Top. They sell incense and do rags and kosher dill pickles, rugs, baseball hats and scented oils. The other drunks around the premises are also very amusing. I'd probably never do any real food shopping here, but I rarely do real food shopping anyway. But there's something to be said about having a supermarket basically all to yourself.

Much better, authentic Thai and you can eat in or get take out as well.

text: This is a tale of two reviews. The Gandhi's Birthday special consisted of a center table surrounded by normal steam table selections. The special table selections were nearly all very good. The eggplant selection and the veggie kabobs, were unique and fabulous. It's too bad the table wasn't representative of the rest of the buffet. Dessert consisted of homemade peach and apple pies, cookies and nuts. The pies -- particularly the peach -- were great. But oddly, the ice cream, mentioned in another review, costs extra. The rest of the buffet was truly ho-hum. (Ice cream -- mentioned in one review here, is extra -- nearly unheard of on Chinese buffets.) The sauces on the main buffet were too heavy and tended to be gluey. The hot and sour soup was nearly inedible. Vegetarian restaurants can be a healthy place to eat, not Su Tao where the emphasis is on heavy sauces and fried dishes. The service was very friendly and helpful. I was in Malvern on business, visited Su Tao for dinner based upon recommendations here. Sigh. If this is one of the best vegetarian buffet restaurants in the Philadelphia suburbs, the area must be devoid of decent vegetarian chefs.
label: NEG

text: Dr. Elizabeth McKinstry, the Cat Vet of South Street never bought into the corporate approach to veterinary care like Vca Cat Hospital of Philadelphia and so many other vets have done.The light bulb went off a few years ago to many vets that we will pay anything to see that our cats and dogs are given the very best care. Now, whether or not the animal is robust enough to weather test after test "just to be sure", it has become the standard MO of so many vets that a visit that might have cost about $80.00 not so long ago, will now rip your wallet to the tune of $500, $600 and upwards for "precautionary care". Its criminal; less for what it does to our bank accounts than how it brutalizes our pets. It is easy to believe that Dr. McKinstry's dream as a little girl was to be a vet. I don't know if that is true, but I would bet on it. Leave your pet with her and her caring staff at her Hospital on South street and be assured that it will be given the very best care with thorough and insightful diagnoses of any hospital in the city. Be assured there wont be a charge on the bill for a test that wasn't absolutely necessary. And if your pet is a patient and like my orange tabby does die, expect a heartfelt hand written sympathy card from Dr. McKinstry herself. Not something the venal corporate quacks are wont to do. She cares and it shows. Bonus? Its next door to Ants Pants.
label: POS

text: I went in Mike Duffy's last week while continuing my search for a great tasting burger. I had found some old reviews on the internet stating they had good burgers, or at least they did at some point in time. I ordered a medium cheeseburger with American cheese and fries. The menu shows the burger as 8oz and also touts it as "the best burger in St. Louis" and for $8.75 it better be. The burger was cooked to order but had several flaws, first it was cooked over heat that was too high, so the outside was very charred, there was also zero seasoning which made for a tasteless burger. The worst of the flaws was the quality of meat, it was bite after bite of gristle, in fact I can't remember ever eating a burger that has this much gristle. Needless to say I was unimpressed by "The best burger in St. Louis" and won't be returning to give it another shot. The fries were the typical thicker cut variety which were also unseasoned and bland. At least they were crisp, but after that burger they offered little consolation. My quest for a great burger continues..

text: I've been to McFadden's at the Ball Park a few times, the most recent being last night when my boyfriend and I went because we had a Groupon for it. The only rule on the Groupon was that we couldn't redeem it during any of the Eagles, Flyers or Phillies home games. That's fine, we figured, we'll just go when the Phils are on the road, have a few beers, eat some food and watch the game with other fans. Can't go too wrong there, right? WRONG. First, this place is absolutely DEAD on a night when there isn't a game going on at home. Seriously we were 2 of maybe 8 patrons in the whole entire restaurant. There were more staff just standing around drinking and talking loudly than actual customers. That brings me to my second point- The waitstaff/bartenders/employees all decided to congregate 10 feet away from our table and hung out there the entire time, laughing and joking around with one another. (This is fine, I'm all for a happy and friendly work environment, but don't do it while you're practically standing on top of customers!) A few of the guys were putting together a shop vac right there and had all the pieces strewn on the floor around us, so that I couldn't even get up to go to the bathroom. Then once they finished putting it together they tested it out right there, vacuuming up under our table without saying anything to us! It was so awkward, and honestly felt like we were intruding on their space. They made us feel like we were over staying our welcome at a restaurant that is trying to close for the night (even though it was only 7:30). It was really rude and we didn't get one apology or even an acknowledgment that we were sitting right there. The food was something that I remembered being pretty decent from the last time I came there, though it could have something to do with the fact that the last time I ate there I was completely trashed from the game and was so hungry that even Chase Utley's sweaty batting helmet would have tasted delicious. Yuck. This time however, completely sober, the food was nothing special. Just basically bad pub food. The cheesesteak nachos, which they claim to be famous for, would literally been the same as me opening my mouth and having the waitress empty an entire container of Wiz into my mouth and put a chip and a small peice of dry meat on top. YUM. Anyway, I'll wrap this up. I would have given it ZERO stars, but the fact that it's a pretty fun atmosphere when the game is going on warrants some recognition. But really, give me a tv screen, lots of beer and other Phillies fans and I'm a happy girl. Moral of the story- Go here if there's a game going on and you're too broke to buy a ticket, but you still want to experience the game atmosphere, BUT for the love of god and all that is holy, don't even think about going to McFadden's when any of the teams are on the road. You're better off at Chickies and Pete's or just staying at home and watching the game from your couch.
label: NEG

text: I've been going to this restaurant for 10 yrs. and I have to say, this is the absolute best sushi in the bay area. Family run with the father and son cutting up the fish, their's is the freshest, best tasting sushi I've ever had. 1 piece per order, Reasonably priced, but I'd pay double for the taste alone. If you come to the Tampa Bay area, you must make a trip to this north Pinellas gem.
label: POS

text: I don't get it guys. The pizza here was sub-par, even for the area. Frustratingly bland. I'm still getting used to South Jersey's strange definition of pizza. I have had obnoxiously thick crusts, over-cooked and under-cooked tasteless cheese, and full on marinara for sauce. Born and raised in North Jersey, I became very accustomed to what pizza is there and I'm not trying to be an elitist. Not every pizza place is Lombardi's or DeLorenzo's. And thats ok. But they could still be good! I called up after reading all of your glowing reviews, and asked for a tomato pie. There might have been some confusion, because I ordered a Tomato Pie, and wound up getting just a regular pizza. The cheese was way too salty and overcooked. The sauce tasted weird. The crust was a little sweet, which is good, but decent crust alone does not make a pizza. Grease rolled right off every slice. I have had better pizza in a bowling alley. I want to go back. The people here are nice, and from your reviews the portions are large. But I don't know if there is any value to large poritions that don't taste good.

text: I know, you probably think I'm a hater for giving this place 2-stars. The service was actually great, so I'd give it 2.5 stars. Hear me out and you'll find that this is not actually some crazy rant, or even a horrible review. I was just super disappointed, I heard such great things about this place. We came here for lunch and got a salmon plate with veggies and rice, and biscuits and gravy, my favorite. It was bustling- a cozy restaurant indeed, sunlight streaming in, the smell of butter and pancake syrup. The food was mediocre- maybe it was just a bad combo. The fish was dry, but a little bit of the store-bought Cajun Power really made a big difference. It's like putting spaghetti sauce in your pasta. The steamed veggies were old and wilted, and the rice was super plain. My biscuits were a little soggy and the texture was off...and the gravy was lukewarm ( BIG deal, really) and not very flavourful. Bad gravy really gets to me. Here's the deal breaker- they microwaved my muffin, biscuits and I'm pretty sure the gravy was microwaved too. Total dealbreaker, - 1 star, hence the 2.5. They have a toaster, it would have made my biscuit taste much better. If I wanted microwaved food I could do it myself at home. I could rant on and on ... but you get my drift. I'm sure the omelettes are good, and there aren't alot of places to go in this tiny town. Just ask for toast instead of the muffin.
label: NEG

text: I'm not usually a big chain restaurant kinda gal, but this Cosi is attached to my office building, and sometimes, when it's raining (like today), and I don't feel like wandering through Old City, I stop here. This is certainly not the best Cosi in the city -- but I maintain that it's not THAT bad either. I've gotten bagels (err, squagels) here pretty frequently -- and they're pretty tasty and cheap (esp. the Asiago cheese bagel...mmm). No complaints really, except for the bagel man always hits on me (/any chick with two legs and a butt), which makes me sorta uncomfortable. During lunch and dinner, things can get pretty hectic, and service is generally pretty poor. I came here once for dinner, and watched the waitress stumble and bumble her way through the cheese list (my friend wanted to change the cheese on her salad -- you would think she was asking the waitress to compute nuclear physics!) Apparently, they have a cheese called Gor-GON-zola. And ricutty. And brye. The food though actually isn't half bad though -- if you don't mind waiting for excessive periods of time. And the staff is sort of terrible, but in a humorous way. At least, that's how I try to look at it...

Both of them made noises that would have been vulgar had they not been devouring baked goods. Each cupcake was around $2 (under, but I couldn't tell because prices weren't listed). The owner chatted us up for a few minutes. It felt like we were just hanging out in her kitchen.

text: Charles Schwab Bank lives up to its promise to give higher interest on balances. That's the good news. Potential customers should also be aware of some things that the Bank does not advertise. The rebate of ATM fees is capped at $9.00 per month. More than that you have to pay yourself. (3) If you need services like a Cashier's Check you are limited to dealing with the Reno office via courier. (4) You will still have to deal with a local bank for a safe deposit box. (5) You can't use your Schwab Bank checks at merchants that only accept checks from a local bank. (6) The interest rate moves with the economy. When Charles Schwab Bank opened, the interest rate was 4.25%. Today (2008-06-19) the interest rate is only 1.99%.

text: When I have out of town guests who want a laid-back meal, at a good price, that's sure to please ... I have never gone wrong with Saleem's. I believe the standard fare is Lebanese cuisine, but I just call it delicious. The staff are always prompt and courteous and the food always arrives quickly and freshly prepared. Best of all, everyone always raves about how great the meal turned out. I've been there more than a dozen times over the years and have never been disappointed. For appetizers, I highly recommend the garlic pita chips. What could be bad about fried pita wedges drizzled with a sauce of garlic and butter? They can be had as a stand alone item, or part of an Appetizer Tray for 2 or 4. I highly recommend the sampler, because then you get to try the falafal and the hummus, which are also both quite good. Either way, it's a tummy pleaser. The flavor is always consistenly delicious. If those other items don't appeal to you, the roasted head of garlic is a simple and enjoyable appetizer as well. My favorite entree is the Safeena. It's a chicken breast that's been marinated, charbroiled, and then drizzled with that same garlic butter sauce. At dinner-time, definitely pair it up with the garlic-mashed potatoes for a hearty meal that won't leave you hungry. For lunch, you automatically get the rice ... which is fantastic as well. The house salad is always crisp and fresh, and the house dressing is tangy and light. I've never had anything here that wasn't good. My vegetarian partner enjoys the entrees here also, so it's a definite crowd pleaser. Go ... and then go again. You won't regret it!

text: So being the gluttons for punishment that we are, my wife and I came here last night for dessert. We had just finished a fantastic meal at Miga at it was just to easy to cross the street to indulge my wife's chocolate craving. We were pleasantly surprised when we walked in the door and the place was actually open. No malfunctioning C3PO to rush us out. We were seated immediately in a dining room that reminded me of a tacky version of the Cheesecake Factory. Vats of chocolate, trite aphorisms on the walls, abstract drawings of some bald dude with an earring, references to Willie Wonka. . .I read somewhere that these restaurants belong in Disneyland or Vegas and I have to agree. So we decide to order the banana split waffle. It was very expensive -- $14 for a dessert -- but sounded delicious. The pictures on the menu made it look amazing (it was the one dessert they chose to showcase on the Waffles and Crepes section). But it SUCKED: 1. The waffle was one of the worst I've ever tasted. It was as if they took a week-old cake donut (not the Krispy Kreme kind, but the really heavy kind that crumbles), and shoved it into a waffle maker. The waffle was so hard that I needed a knife to cut it. And it tasted like, well, a re-baked week-old bad cake donut. The waffle we had at the Days Inn was a gazillion times better. 2. The chocolate was way too sweet, as if put too much sugar. Now I'm not a chocolate connoisseur, but I do know a few things about chocolate and I did take chemistry in high school. I know that high quality chocolates typically have a higher cocoa content. And from chemistry, if you increase the content of one ingredient, then the percentage allocated to the other ingredients goes down. So if the sugar content is very high (too sweet), then the cocoa content, by definition, will be low. So my conclusion: Max Brenner uses low quality chocolate. Unbelievable for a restaurant that bills itself as "changing the world's chocolate culture." 3. The banana was way over-ripe. Over-ripe to the point where it left a pungent aftertaste in mouth. 4. There was not nearly enough vanilla ice cream for this dessert. Ok, so maybe we didn't the amount of vanilla ice cream with the waitress (the menu just says "vanilla ice cream", with no indication of the unit of measure). But for a $14 dessert, most people would assume you'd get at least a scoop. We got something closer to a dollop. So there it is. I can't believe anyone could screw up a waffle, ice cream, fudge, and bananas that badly. Now that I think about it, there wasn't even any fudge - it was chocolate sauce. At any rate, this dessert SUCKED. It would suck even if it cost $3 in the "day-old" section of a bakery.

We walked in the lobby at about 8pm and I noticed that the lobby was completely deserted and there was no one at the front desk. Waited a good 10 min. before someone made it from out the back office and checked us in. The guy checking us in was not very friendly, not very welcoming, and rushed through the check in process as if he had better things to be doing. As a seasoned traveler, i know that more often than not, hotels offer free upgrades if there is space and availability. I asked if there was any possibility of a room upgrade, and the guy gave me a look that would have been deserved if i had asked him to stick a pine cone up a certain orifice, and flat out said "NO". Did not check the computer or even offer to check, just directly said "No". When i politely brought this point to his attention, he gave me attitude and said that i was booked on a special rate. Whatever. I was hungry, tired, and wanted to get settled in, so i left it at that and checked in. We waited another 10 mi. in awkwardness till a porter cam for our bags. Our luggage was loaded onto a cart and we were unceremonously shown into a rickety elevator that smelled faintly of stale vomit and lemon pledge. Our porter took us all the way around the 3rd floor, before he remembered that our room was on the 2nd floor. Oookay... Get back in the elevator, and make our way to the 2nd floor. Instead of our room being in the actual Hotel building, we were taken out back and into another building that was once, in its past life, servant's quarters. I'm dead serious when i say, the hotel room i stayed in was a converted servant quarter. The porter left our bags in the front of the room, and left. We opened the room, and were dismayed to find a tiny room (about 12 x 15 sq ft) with a FULL sized bed, 2 pillows, an arimoire housing the TV. The closet was barely big enough for 2 people's luggage, and the bathroom was downright shabby with peeling wallpaper exposing mould underneath. So much for a Deluxe King room. Despite the 'deal' i got on the price, I still feel like i was misled or cheated. So here's the breakdown of the pros' & cons' +1 star- Location, Location, Location: it is right in the French Quarter, one block away from the madness of Bourbon and 5 brisk blocks from Jackson Square, and 2 blocks from Canal Street. If you plan on partying hard or want to be centrally located so you can drop your shopping bags off in between your French Quarter sprees, its location is ideal. There is a Chase bank (with the worlds loudest ATM) half a block away and most late night restaurants (not to mention the heaven sent Krystal Burger) are literally a stagger, skip, and stumble away. +1 star-- Central Courtyard. This is the only jewel in the St. Louis' crown. The open air courtyard was tented for the winter, but that did not detract from the lushness of the plants or the beauty of the fountain. There were private functions 3 of the 5 nights we stayed there, but during the day, many hotel patrons enjoyed their breakfasts and lunches in this charming and exotic setting. -1 star-- Service. Granted, I was not expecting Ritz Carlton like service, but overall, I was pretty disappointed about the staff, especially the front desk, who run this place. Its like they either forgot or just did not pay attention to Hospitality 101. The only nice employees we encountered were the dining room staff and the kind old man who does security at night. The only problem is, half the time, he's not at the security desk. -1 star- Housekeeping. Granted, i have slight OCD, but i really had issues with the housekeeping and overall maintainence of this place. Some examples are: on the first night, we called the front desk at about 7pm and asked for 2 extra pillows since there were only 2 on the bed. They said they would send them right up, but they never came. We had to ask again the next morning as we were leaving for breakfast. We came back 5 hrs. later, we found 2 pillows haphazardly flung on top of our still unmade bed. In addtion to the mouldy wallpaper in the bathroom, the showerhead was unscrewed and one of our towels had stains on it. yuck.

We didn't have any cash on us, and luckily, you can still use credit as long as you spend 6 bucks. We picked out the standard, glazed so we could fairly rate Plaza against the other shops we've been to. Making up the rest of the cost, we got a raspberry filled, cinnamon bun, carmel long john, a large coffee, and a chocolate milk. After talking with the owners a few minutes about their businesses on this strip of Morganford (day care, donut shop, and restaurant), we jumped back in the Scout, excited to try the donuts. Before we took off I opened my milk carton. I noticed that it smelled a bit funky, but I passed it off as maybe a weird carton/chocolate milk smell combo. I noticed that the sell by date was a day old so I took a small sip. It seemed ok. So, I took a big gulp, but felt chunks of curdled milk swirling around in my mouth. Needless to say, I spit it right out on the parking lot, where it was so curdled, it looked like someone threw up donut. The aftermath was simple. No more donuts from Plaza. I am sad about this point because I liked the donuts, all of them. Although they didn't make my top three donuts in town, they also weren't the worst donuts I've had in town. The glazed had a generous amount of glazed on it, which was great, but almost too much. The donuts themselves were all a lot heavier and more dense than other fried donuts I've had in the area. They all stuck onto each other in the bag. I never noticed this happening before from other shops. But, like I said, they had a nice flavor and weren't that bad. But, all I can think about is the blinky milk I had for breakfast. I am willing to completely overlook a past sell by date by a day, because this shouldn't mean the milk is bad. But I'm not willing to forgive poor refrigeration. Gross.

Over 15 types of grilled cheese (their specialty), like 10 types of cheese fries... they have some of my friend's favorites - lobster mac and cheese, sliders... and a grease truck sandwich that will either make you drool or vomit. They have ice cream, of course, as well as other dessert items... I like how every time I go, my ice cream choices get complimented. :) Maybe I really am the best orderer in the world. If so, I recommend the warm cookie pie with cookie dough ice cream and hot fudge. They also have specials for each day of the week - weiner wednesdays, sundae sundays... you get the idea. The only day that doesn't have a special is what I've taken to calling, 'F-you Fridays'. Saturdays has some free food if you wear pajamas, but there's fine print I can see on the sign because it's behind the soft serve. If I had one thing I would change about the Pop Shop, it would be this: Baffles The place needs baffles. It's a big open room, with high ceilings and nothing to absorb sound at all. I've got a couple of sweaters still tagged that will probably never see light of day until I take them to Thrifty Threads. TT will turn around and sell them for pennies on the dollar of their worth and somehow be able to make money. Some of the women's clothing donations (especially suits) go directly to the victims themselves (after thorough cleaning.) The great other thing about my donations to TT? I receive a receipt that is legit for me to write off the value of the goods from my federal income tax income liability. Last year those several donations of several hundred dollars worth of clothes kept me from owing to getting a slight refund. Helping those in need and helping my wallet at the same time. Now, if I can keep from buying clothes I don't wear... but if the volume of clothes for sale at thrifty is any indication, I'm not the only one with the same problem. text: Sorry animal lovers...not a place for you, unless you are completely unaware of animal cruelty problems in the world. I haven't been to a zoo in years so I thought I'd go with my girlfriend to the Santa Barbara zoo. We were told by a couple of people that it is really nice. Here's how our day went. Parking: Avoid parking in the zoo parking lot, it costs just as much as admission. Minute 1: Our admission ticket was given to us by a 9 year old girl. I assume she is the daughter of one of the employees but I feel like there are some unemployed people out there that could really use this position. She seemed nice of course, but seriously guys. *NOTE: she was 1 of 3 ZOO employees I saw the entire day, excluding vendors. Once inside the park prepare to be bombarded by pregnant women smoking cigarettes and children running everywhere unsupervised and out of control. *NOTE: there is a very fancy mound of TURF about 3 feet of high for the children to slide down on empty beer boxes. This seemed to be a HIT with the kids. Next to spitting on cages this was definitely the most popular activity. Once we weaved our way through the chaos, we did get a chance to see the lone zookeeper feeding some capibaras. Unfortunately, this was the ULTIMATE highlight of the day. She seemed smart, well trained and open to answering questions. About 4 feet from this exhibit, we were able to see just about every other exhibit, as there is NO ROOM BETWEEN ANY OF THE ANIMALS. Minute 10: We arrived at the Elephants...I was hoping to see a large area for the elephants to roam free. The only reason I was hoping this unfortunately is because I hadn't seen the rest of the exhibits. Both of the extremely depressed elephants were standing still and looked like giant versions of Eeyore except sadder and hotter. SEE Eeyore photo: http://images.pictureshunt.com/pics/e/eeyore_cartoon-4820.jpg Minute 15: We arrived at what may have once been the Lion Den, but is now a glass cage the size of a child's bedroom, right next to what may have once been some sort of make shift lagoon that could at least seem like something out of Africa, but only when there is water in it. Both of the lions were passed out and hiding from the kids knocking on the glass, trying to wake them from their dreams (which I'm sure are self induced states of unconsciousness so as to feel they are in actual nature where they belong.) Minute 20: The Giraffes!!!! Very pretty designs on these animals. And what's even better, they can see the highway from their own safar--i mean sand box (also equipped with fancy, empty water hole to make us feel like we are really watching giraffes move in loose herds on the open woodlands and grasslands of the African Savannah.) Minute 30: Can we bear seeing what the "snow leopard" is forced to sit in. Or even the Gorilla? No. So we left. Unfortunately not before seeing HUGE GREEN GRASSY AREAS FILLED WITH NOBODY. Perhaps on the 4th of July or Memorial day, these areas are filled with happy children and families picnicking. Not today. My question is this, why don't they extend some of the animal exhibits so they can walk more than 10 feet in each direction, and reduce some of the "natural parks" in the zoo. I would have asked a zookeeper but I guess they fired all of them.

text: If you have lots of money, special dietary needs, or need rare/high quality pre-packaged products, and don't care about the quality of store employees, then Whole Foods is just great. I don't fall into most of those categories. I'll shop at WF, these days, when they're the only option or when I'm looking for something that can't be found at any other local place, but I also expect it to put a dent in my wallet. Let's just do a run-down of my criticism: 1. Many products are expensive. Some because of their rarity, some because that's the standard price for that item in any store, others because they can charge way too much and still have someone pay. Example: Two normal-sized, in-season pears should NEVER cost $5+ (although, since Feders opened down the street, I've never had a reason to get produce from WF). There's just no excuse for most of their produce section's pricing, organic or not. 2. Employee quality is... inconsistent. I'll give them some credit--in the past year or so, it seems like most employees are decent (if not friendly) human beings. Additionally, the folks behind the bakery, meat, and fish counters have been excellent in all my interactions with them. The cashiers and other employees, though, tended to be a combination of the following: surly, rude, useless, helpful, knowledgeable, and/or friendly. That is, some would smile and proceed to tell you "Sorry, but I have no idea what X is," others might lead you to where you can find a particular item (although they wouldn't always be correct or find the actual item), and others would openly criticism or make fun of you for your purchases. Nothing makes me want to shop somewhere more than having a barely-employable ex-punk brat harass me for buying groceries at their store. 3. 365 Brand is... well, also inconsistent. Some items are about what you'd expect (although never better than what they're imitating), but some store brand items are just inedible. They don't give you any grief about returning items you hate, but it's still disappointing and wasteful. 4. What happened, bakery? Bread's easy (and fun) to bake for myself, but it's too hot to be worth it during the summer, so I started getting some WF fresh baked bread this past year. And it was good. Then, one day, tired and hungry after returning from a trip to New York, I grabbed a fresh loaf before going home for making a sandwich. And it wasn't fully baked. Chalking that up as a fluke, I tried their bakery bread again, a while later, and experienced the same problem. I've tried contacting management regarding the issue but never gotten a response and not found it pursue the issue, if the people running the store didn't care. 5. This is probably petty, but the whole naive "we're helping!" feel/message of the store is kind of annoying. It's really cool that they have battery and polypropylene (#5) recycling, but giving cashiers a fundraising quota for horribly misguided projects is bothersome and weirdly depressing. Edit: Since writing this review, they eliminated battery recycling, but they did further expand plastics recycling, so now you can take any recyclable plastic there. Which is pretty awesome. Employee quality also seems to have improved in the past year or so. I still can't comfortably give it a third star--there certainly are much better stores--but I have at least come to be okay with the occasional trip to this store.
label: NEG

text: I was lured here by the promise of sweet potato fries and iced coffee. What I didn't expect was the most amazing veggie burger I've ever had...but that's what I got! This veggie burger is full of black beans and has a wonderfully pleasant heat to it- it is not so spicy that it burns your mouth, but it lets you know there is pepper in there and really adds a little something-something to it. The sweet potato fries were served as big wedges and had just enough savory flavor. My iced coffee, the Irish Setter, a chocolatey concoction flavored with irish cream, didn't have the chemically saccharine taste of most iced drinks. I was pretty stoked to see they had carrot cake, but I was actually so full and satisfied with my meal I actually passed on dessert! Some other notes: Fido's parking scares me a little. There is but one way to get in and out of the parking lot, and it is only wide enough for one car to squeeze through at a time. But I'll man up and risk possible collision for the awesome food. The coffee shop/restaurant is tiny, but on the inside it feels pretty open and roomy somehow.
