text: To be honest, I almost gave it one star as it better fit the description of "Eek! Methinks not" than "Meh. I've experienced better" but I didn't feel right about giving Cuba Libre a single star, it probably deserves more like 1.5, so I rounded up. I also need to preface the following review by saying that I went for Restaurant Week brunch. Now I know that they are not primarily a brunch spot and I know the argument that Restaurant Week is not fitting for a review of an establishment but I personally disagree with both arguments. If you can't do brunch well, don't offer it and if you plan on half-assing Restaurant Week, don't participate - those are the restaurants decisions and so my review is based on the experience that Cuba Libre offered me. The specialty brunch menu appeared really wonderful online and so I was really excited to try this new take on Restaurant Week. My friend and I started with two cups of coffee. The coffee was watery and hugely disappointing. I see from past reviews this is a common problem here. For the starter we both ordered the Chicharrones de Pollo. The entire dish was extremely heavy and greasy and covered in some sort of thick "sauce". The chicken was not the most appetizing and I found it to be lower grade chicken than I tend to eat. Both of us took a few bites and then let the rest be taken away. Our entrees were different but both were disappointing. I ordered the Huevos en Cazuela which is described as a "casserole of eggs, olive oil smashed potatoes, chorizo sausage, Monterey Jack cheese and roasted tomato chipotle salsa". The dollop of roasted tomato chipotle salsa on the top was the only highlight and it wasn't much to write home about. The rest of the dish can better be described as overly cooked to the point of two glassy and hardened eggs (which I had to fold off they were so hard and disgusting), small spam like meat substances with one or two chorizo pieces thrown in and a burnt bottom and strange smell in a 2x4 inch casserole dish. My friend went with the Miami Frita (aka Cuban burger). She said the meat was OK but the rest of the dish was disappointing. We both ended the meal with the churro's. I found them to also be very greasy and heavy (and not in the way you would obviously expect but in a twice fried and left on the counter kind of way) and I didn't love the thin sour chocolate that accompanied the dish (but this could be personal preference). In the end, I came to a restaurant for extremely sub-par food and will never return again. Oh and I should probably mention that the service was pretty mediocre. Maybe they did deserve one star...

text: My husband and I recently stayed at Ashton's Bed and Breakfast in New Orleans for five nights to celebrate our anniversary. Our trip was more fun (and more delicious, thanks to Ashton's!) than we ever could have imagined. Ashton's is located in a beautiful neighborhood on Esplanade Avenue in between the French Quarter and City Park. It is a quiet location and very easy to access all of New Orleans' points of interest by cab or by the city bus (which stops right in front of the B&B). Ashton's itself is a beautiful and historic mansion with eight rooms. We stayed in the Creole Queen room and it was gorgeous and so comfortable. The rooms are cleaned thoroughly everyday and your bathroom is stocked with Aveeda skin care products as well as bath salts. It is hard to describe the breakfast in words because it is so delicious. Patrick and Karma (the lovely innkeepers - Patrick is also the chef) alternate a sweet and savory breakfast everyday with dishes like bananas foster waffles, crepes with eggs, crab and a fancy creole cheese sauce, french toast with sweet potatoes, honey butter and pecans. And don't worry - the sweet breakfast is served with a side of bacon or sausage, and the savory breakfasts are served with a first course of coffee cake, muffins, or one day I think we had something Patrick called a "croissant flower" mmmmmm. There is also coffee, tea, and juice at breakfast, plus there are snacks and coffee out all day. They do not skimp on anything! Patrick and Karma are so nice and hospitable. They will answer all of your questions, chat with you about the city, and can recommend delicious restaurants. Ashton's is also and excellent bargain - I couldn't believe we got all this for the price we paid. We can't wait to go back!!!

It's good because of two reasons - I don't spend all my time just eating Naan, plus the Naan that comes out is always fresh and delicious. *The soup! The soup is always available on their buffet line. I can't remember the name of it for the life of me. Their menu only lists one type of soup (Dal soup), but I could have sworn the soup on the buffet line starts with an S. Anyway, this soup will light your fire. It's high on the spicy side, but not enough to torch your tongue. The barrage of flavors in this soup bewilders me. I need to get this recipe! *Chicken Tikka Masala - For a generic Indian Buffet dish, it's done well. I'm sure the sauce is 99 percent full fat cream, but I could probably drink it daily. *Service - The service at this place is great. Unlike other buffets in STL, the employees actually seem to be happy you're there. Very personal folks. *Environment - The restaurant is spic and span. They do a great job keeping it sparkling. In conclusion, I highly recommend Saffron. It's a bummer it's so well hidden off Manchester. I hope it stays around for a while.

They make it with real fruit (it's frozen, but it's better than canned) and add a splash of milk (or cream?). It ends up being well balanced and not too sweet. The tapioca was a little on the soft side, but it wasn't falling apart and the coldness of the slushie firmed them up nicely. My friend and I also split their steamed buns - one mung bean and one custard. The mung bean was good but the custard looked kinda funny/had funny texture. I'm pretty sure it was just a result of being steamed but I'd skip it next time. Next time I come back, I'm getting the egg waffles for sure.

text: I kept driving by this place and seeing banners for special rates so i finally booked a massage. On the phone they were quite polite and were able to get me in right away at a great seasonal rate--it was $34 for an hour massage! I am giving this place a two star rating because, while the massage itself was decent and the masseuse addressed my problem areas, I thought the ambiance was lacking and they skimped on using decent products. When we first crossed the quaint tiki patio and got to the massage room, I noticed that the area was clean but that it smelled like bathroom cleaning products instead of a spa. My biggest let-down was that the masseuse used "Equate baby oil gel" instead of a massage oil or lotion. This left me feeling very greasy after my massage, and I worried about ruining my clothes--in fact, when I got home, I had to towel off excess baby oil. The CD that was playing kept skipping and eventually stopped so there was no music for the last third of my session. If you need a quick rub-down this wouldn't be too bad, but I have to admit that I've gotten better rubs at massage schools. My masseuse seemed a bit brusque and hurried, but I'll give her the benefit of the doubt and chalk it up to the fact that I was the last client of the day. Edit: I went back because I got an email for a freebie massage and although the massage was better (the masseuse was friendlier and actually used real massage lotion this time), the ambiance was the same and they were running the washing machine/dryer this time, which was right outside my room.

text: Let me start by saying, I used to LOVE Iron Hill. I started going back when the original was the only one, and it was a great place to have Mom and Dad take you when they came to visit you on campus. The food was varied and always excellent. While the menu was short, there was always an option or two that even a picky eater could find to love. So in writing this review maybe I'm being a little harsh because I feel a little like a spurned lover, I just don't feel like Iron Hill loves me as much as I used to love it. I've tried different things, but I just can't get that loving feeling back. So to the review. Over the past couple of years I have been going back more frequently, usually as a place to take people from out of town that I want to show some local flavor and avoid the chains. Over those past visits, I have felt that the atmosphere has changed the most. The food is still as good or better than it was, but the personality of the servers and staff is what has changed. When a woman I was with asked the server what sort of beer he would suggest his response was "How would I know what you like?" That was it, end of sentence, and he stood there just expecting her to pick something. Now that was awkward. The servers that I used to have were IHB brew fanatics, they loved the beers, they drank the beers, and they wanted everyone to love them too. So when he offered no help I knew we were in for trouble. I chalked that up, however, to just one bad server, and possibly just one bad night. Who knows, maybe he just found out he was getting audited. Another occasion a few weeks or months after, while there with another couple, I was just struck by the lack of personality in all of the people we dealt with. I'm not sure if I'm articulating it the right way, but I just really felt that the mood had changed and we were now at a TGI-Applebee-Tuesdays. While it doesn't mean that the service was bad but it just wasn't a place I would say had any local sort of flavor anymore. Considering it is a brew pub, I feel that I should admit that I don't drink. So, while the service issues are a problem, I have no idea about the beer situation. I still hear good things so I am thinking that aspect remains unchanged as well as the food. Regardless of everything else, I've never had a meal that wasn't very good and priced well, so I would say if you want to take a small step up from the chain restaurants on 202, it's worth the visit.
label: NEG

text: Finally, I've eaten somewhere so horrifically bad that it compelled me to sign up for a Yelp account so that I have an appropriate forum in which to trash it. The atmosphere and service, while nothing special, was fine. But I go to sushi places to eat sushi, which at Mikimoto went from difficult to impossible. We ordered four rolls: two of the smaller, more modestly priced rolls and two of the larger, $10+ rolls. All four arrived looking like crap, though I'd still have been ready to eagerly devour them if they tasted even vaguely like fresh fish or other such tastiness. The salmon was way past its prime, inedibly so, and all the rest of the fish was mushy, warm and otherwise disgusting. That was enough to make it the grossest sushi order I've ever had, but beyond that, the rolls were just falling apart and virtually impossible to eat. And one of the more expensive rolls was sliced into four huge pieces: two of them impractically big, and the other two cartoonishly big. We managed to get the impractically big pieces in our mouths, and I suppose I should be thankful that they left us with no desire to even contemplate how to approach the other two. After a sad taste of each roll, we'd had enough. We declined the waitress' offer of a box, and she walked off with the half-full plates, never asking if it was OK. It was sort of a relief-- I hate the thought of complaining at a restaurant, and have never done it. I accept the gamble of trying new restaurants. This was the first time we ever seriously contemplated sending something back, but I can't imagine that doing so would make the fish any fresher or the rolls any more structurally sound. I'm still grossed out and I'm never, ever going back.
label: NEG

He was definitely trying to be funny and had a good personality, but I thought cow manure was a weird thing to call food that you were serving a restaurant. I don't think the chef's would have liked that too much haha. All the spreads were delicious though, even the "cow manure". Since we were going to be partying later and I had already stocked up on large amounts of the pita that was served and replenished often with our appetizer, I figured I would just have something lighter for dinner. I went with one of the soups of the day. I'm not really sure what it was called, but it had a lemon broth base with pulled pieces of chicken throughout mixed in with a curdled milk substance. I was not a big fan. It had a strange bitter taste that I am not accustomed and they lemon mixed with the cream or milk was not to my liking. However, the other plates that my friends got were colorful and looked interesting, I just don't think authentic greek food is for me. Give me some spanakopita or a nice gyro and I'm set, but that's about as wild as I'll probably get.

text: I'm a huge fan of Tim's. They are all over the place in Canada and I believe it is possible to drive the entire length of Canada and always eat at a Tim Hortons. I have been to several in 5 Canadian Provinces, the Yukon, and even West Virginia. This Doughnuts and coffee chain also has a nice selection of sandwiches and soups. And if you eat in, you get china cups, plates, and bowls. Service is amazingly fast and the coffee is pretty darn good. Of course I also like the doughnuts. And they are not as annoyingly sweet as Krispie Kreme. You also get a great view into one aspect of Canadian culture. I still remember one time in Fort Saskatchewan at 5 AM at -40 C and there was a line-up out the door and a backup in the drive through. All that time, folks were in good humour as the line moved quickly. I have experienced similar queues and Canadian politeness and patience in other stores. I'm only going to write one Tim Horton's review on Yelp. I chose this one because it had the most interesting local "flavour" early one morning a few months ago when I was walking around a sometimes rough downtown Edmonton. Tourists, people going to work, and transients were all lined up patiently and later seated in the same area as we woke up and warmed up together.

If you have to eat at one of Emeril's restaurants since you are in New Orleans go for it, but if you want some really great food there is plenty to be had for a fairer price.

text: What a dump. I fly in and out of this armpit weekly, and it's a misery every time. The following applies to Terminal A, I haven't had the misfortune of being subjected to any of the others. So, Terminal A... It is dirty, a large quantity of the seating available has holes in it or is torn up, the restrooms are a disgrace, the employees are surly, and every food place I have been to in PHL is apparently staffed by zombies. I've been to many an airport and PHL is damn near the bottom of the heap. Even god-forsaken Newark is superior in almost every way, and that ain't saying much. Oh yeah - extra bonus: the worst delays I have ever encountered have ALL been at PHL. From what I understand, PHL gets the short end of the NE Corridor stick with regards to air traffic when it comes to weather delays, so it's got that going for it too. It all adds up to a perfect storm of air travel misery. I will give a second star, however, for the (usually) short lines through security. I leave PHL on Friday afternoons, and there is typically less than 20 people going through security. Every once in a while the lines are bad, but usually it's a pretty quick trip through.

text: Some investigative Yelping: I had an Arrogant Bastard, a Sam Adams Winter Lager, and a Manhattan. The bartenders consistently under-poured on the pints throughout the night for my friend and I. We are talking about 7/8ths inches lower than the rim on each glass. ( I know it was 7/8ths of an inch since my thumb is measured as such). I went home and it turns out on an American pint glass--16 ounces, which is what my beers were served in, 7/8th of an inch from the rim translates to 2 ounces of liquid. TWO OUNCES. That, friends, is 12.5% unpoured undrunk yet very paid-for beer. At four and five dollars a pint, that is more than a dollar's worth of precious ale that I did not get to touch my lips to. And the beer still had a decent head, so it wasn't like it sat around too long after it was poured. It wouldn't have been so bad if my complaint was corrected, or even just fixed on the second pint. Not so. So that was the Platonic form of Lame Itself. Then, since I am considerate and wanted to give the bar one more chance, I ordered a Manhattan. Now I know the International Bartender's Association official recipe for a Manhattan. It calls for it to be served straight up, and with a cherry. So does Mr. Boston's guide to Bartending. Well, I got a rocks glass full of ice and watery Manhattan less cherry and seemingly devoid of bitters. Rubbish. C'mon folks, The King of Cocktails wasn't even made right here. I also don't understand the infatuation with several huge televisions on all walls of bars. This place exemplifies that model, however. Do we really need to be surrounded with replays from high school football games from the night before? High schools from other states? Can we not talk to one another at bars? This may be a complaint with the notion of sports bars, but I wasn't expecting it from a professed Pub and Grille. Grille with an E ought denote classy, not Class 3A sports highlights. While their tap list is certainly much better than most, I don't know if it is worth it. Smoky atmosphere too, if that is a problem for you. Not so much for me, but I know this worries some folks. Their Spinach & Artichoke dip was good, but not great. The restrooms were very nice though, with complimentary mints.

text: "Jackson" re-opened a little over a year ago and has gone from OK to very good. Jackson has become one of our regular stops, we live nearby. Caveats: There is no Cajun anything here, despite menu names. Also, don't sit under exposed A/C ducts, they may drip condensation. the bar is well-stocked, but doesn't have Coors Light. O/W, building is neat & historical, exposed brick, creaky floors, etc. Looks like no parking, but EVERY TIME, a parking space magically appears for us. Everything is good but the braised beef ribs are wonderful. Good burgers & po-boys, too. The small bar is cozy and N/S, restrooms are clean, waitstaff is really nice, overstreet balcony great when weather permits, owners always there & friendly. We go about 3 or 4 times/month. We haven't had anything bad here in our many visits. 3/9/11 Update: Seems that Jackson suddenly got a lot more expensive. Be sure to check & confirm prices when you order. We got a really big bill for a really small meal; didn't challenge it, but, haven't been back, either. Rick

text: I've driven past Soprano's a thousand times and never went in - it doesn't look like much from the outside. My neighbor went and said it was great so I thought I'd give it a try. i needed good Italian cured meats for an antipasti feast I was preparing, so I decided to finally check out Soprano's. They had a nice selection of proscuitto, coppa, soppressata, etc. etc. which was exactly what I needed to complete my meal. While I was there I decided to grab a panini for lunch - and WOW was it amazing. I had the Italian tuna - which is real European tuna (in oil, not water) combined with capers and onions, served hot on their homemade bread with some delicious melted cheese. I'd definitely head back to try one of the many many paninis they offer. They also make trays of lasagna, other salads, and made to order canolis. (which I picked up the morning of my feast. they were delicious.) They also have an array of homemade breads from baguette to rolls to take away. I was there before the lunch rush, and since it was quiet, service was good. I'll make Soprano's my little Italy in the burbs and grab paninis when the mood strikes me.

I had a 16oz T-Bone that was tender and juicy. They have tons of seasoning and sauces next to the grill that you can add to your steak, chicken, or fish as you see fit. T-Bone came out just right because I did it myself and would have no one to blame but me. All the comforts of home with out any clean up! The salad bar comes with every dinner and includes baked potatoes, chili beans, warm bread, and salsa! Do yourself a favor and load up on their homemade croutons. They were really good! A couple people I was with had the Steak and Lobster option and their consensus was the same...everything perfect! The Palms is like an old school self serve yogurt shop of the new age! I highly recommend a meal at The Palms the next time you are in Carpinteria!

The bar was pretty sexy, rotating for a 360 view of the resort, the lobby, waterfalls, beautiful gardens...all this, and it's a bar, so hopefully some great scenery and a couple cocktails will cleanse any questionable food I was about to eat. The seating was first come first serve so I found myself a dirty table (which the cleaned promptly). I ordered the Crazy "Ari" Sushi Rolls...I was warned it was spicy, and you know at $16, I expected some flavor. It wasn't "bad", it just was in no way fulfilling. Way disappointing, but if you're desperate and no one else will give you a table, it is what it is...food. Overall, it wasn't a great value. The rolls were served in plastic take-out containers...For $16, I expected something better. _____________ Notes: It is a misdemeanor to bring a firearm to this restaurant, since they serve alcohol...The more you know...

text: The best way to sum up my second visit to the cupcake truck would be "confused". This time, I ordered the Bailey Stout and the chocolate peanut butter. I'm pretty certain she gave me a pumpkin cupcake instead of the Bailey Stout. If not, it was the most pumpkiny non-pumpkin cupcake I've ever tasted. I don't really like pumpkin, so I didn't enjoy it too much. The frosting on the pumpkin was supposed to be cream cheese frosting, but this didn't taste like cream cheese frosting... in fact, it had a certain beer-like taste to it. The entire thing left me wondering which cupcake I had actually been given. The peanut butter frosting on the second cupcake was absolutely excellent: rich and creamy and smooth, with the exact correct amount of peanut butter. However, the "chocolate" cupcake was actually some sort of half-chocolate hybrid with a vanilla cake bottom and center. This is particularly odd as there was also a vanilla peanut butter cupcake on the menu. I'm not exactly sure what was going on there. Anyway, the quality of the cake was better than last time (less straight-out-of-the-freezer, I think), but the quantity of frosting was not sufficient. It was more a dollop than a covering. The frosting on the pumpkin/beer cupcake didn't even cover half of the top. Not too my liking overall. It has to be two stars this time.

I have been there, i know what its like to have that last table come in at the last minute, but we arrived at 8:35 and the closed at 10. Service was just disrespectful, and I am going to have a difficult time bringing anyone back here again. It completely ruined the night for us and our friends, who drove an hour to eat there.

text: I uploaded photos, because you really just have to SEE just how bad this, or ANY tattoo can turn out when you don't thoroughly research your artists/shops. I went to Electric Ladyland because it had a great reputation, and I'd seen some killer tattoos come out of that place. I had the name of the artist that I wanted, recommended by a number of people. Sadly, I got screwed, and screwed GOOD when I was there (for my first tattoo, sadly). First off, after talking to the girl at the counter and discussing what I wanted (sun and moon off an album cover) and who I wanted to do it, I was told that if I would come back in an hour I could get it done that day. Great, right? When I returned, the person I assumed was the artist I'd requested came up and showed me the sketch of my tattoo. It looked enough like the original, just an outline without much detail. This was my first tattoo, so I foolishly thought that the detail wasn't necessary for the stencil and he'd just work off the original image. WRONG. You can see what I ended up with. It's since been covered up. With something bigger, fancier, and also THE SAME PRICE as the first one. Months later, I visited the Electric Ladyland website and discovered that the person that did this tattoo was NOT the artist I had picked (I knew only his name, not what he looked like). I've only given the place two stars because it was clean, the guy that did my tattoo did explain everything and was actually very nice (I believe his name may have been PJ, and he relocated after Katrina). My boyfriend at the time got a custom tattoo from the same place (different artist) and his turned out really well. The artist that covered up this tattoo for me was pretty surprised when he found out where it came from. This happened in 2005, so I wouldn't necessarily dissuade anyone from going there, as long as they KNOW who their chosen artist is and make sure that they GET that artist.
label: NEG

text: I honestly can't say much more about the Capital Grille that already hasn't been said. We went there last night to celebrate a friends birthday. They easily accommodated our party of 10 and kept things moving along fairly well. The food pretty much spoke for itself. Everyone at the table ordered filet's and all were cooked exactly as requested. I ordered mine oscar style and it came topped with enormous chunks of crab and a very tasty bernaise sauce. Delicious to the very last bite. Absolutely no complaints regarding our meals. However.... Service, in my opinion, was not really up to snuff. Here's the deal. I've been to many a restaurant. One thing that irks me is when I order a drink and ask for something simple yet specific please bring me what I ordered. The culprit? My request of a vodka tonic with Kettle One vodka and a LEMON. What did I get? A vodka tonic with Grey Goose and a lime. Yeah, I know. Kind of petty right? Yes. But when you are charging a premium for your drinks, bring me what I ordered. Just because the others in our party who ordered drinks made with vodka requested Grey Goose doesn't mean that everyone wants it. That's my first beef. (haha, unintended pun, I'm silly..) The second? Please, for the love of god, don't reach OVER me or anyone else to place plates, silverware, drinks, food, etc. I have no desire to smell your armpits while you're reaching over me to place a steak knife or to refill the water of the person sitting next to me. Again, I know, a petty thing. But it is just annoying when you are in mid conversation and you have an arm thrust in front of your face. I expect a higher level of service from a high end steakhouse. But, those little things did not ruin the night. Again, the food was excellent. Lobster crab cakes (more lobster/crab than filling), deliciously executed au gratin potato's and a perfectly cooked filet oscar style all in the company of great friends? Life really doesn't suck at those moments. Definitely worth another trip back.
label: POS

text: Legal Sea Foods... Once I heard they were coming to my area, I was excited to try them. My wife and I decided to go here for our anniversary a year ago, and when I made my reservation I asked for a section that was quieter if at all possible. After being assured that they would handle that, I gave my information. The interior in LSF is akin to a modern steakhouse: dark woods and chrome, with a lower lighting level (which I enjoy and appreciate). My positive expectations were dashed when they sat us next to a very loud party of 15. I looked longingly at a section farther in the back that seemed much quieter, but my wife wanted to just enjoy the meal. Even though the restaurant was not full, service was extremely slow. Delays were across the board, from the waitress even stopping by to introduce herself to the food service itself. In our case it wasn't such a big deal, as we were enjoying a night alone... Well, us and our new-found 15 loud friends next door :) What blew my mind though was the food. Frankly, I've had better at Red Lobster. I will always have etched in my mind the picture of my tuna steak... cooked to a dull grey. Who overcooks tuna like that?!? I didn't send it back, as I didn't want to make the darling wife wait another 25 minutes for my entree to come out. I'd personally avoid this place, unless you are looking for a (not so) quick seafood meal while shopping at the King of Prussia mall. Unlike other reviewers, I'm not a fan of their pizza. If I want St. Louis pizza, I'm going to Imo's, sorry. I'm also really picky about red sauces and meat sauces. text: Yes, it's a bit of a haul. Every time I head out west to Wiethop, I feel like I'm in the country. But even though it's certainly out of my way, it's a fabulous place to visit if you're up for some gardening. I've made the trip to Wiethop six or seven times since mid-April. That first trip, I was astounded by the size of the greenhouses, just filled to the brim with colorful flowering annuals, hanging baskets and overflowing prearranged pots. Wiethop also has another greenhouse devoted completely to perennials. After the cold, grey winter months, just stepping into the greenhouses' riot of color was restorative to my soul and inspiring. I helped my mother-in-law plant her flowers. I helped her sister. I moved on to Justin's offices. And then finally, FINALLY, we bought our house and had our own yard to plant. Unfortunately, buying a house meant I was also out of money, so I had to exercise extreme restraint on my last trip out to Wiethop. Luckily, their prices aren't exorbitant and if you're willing to forgo some blooms this year, you can buy starter perennials for far less than the grown up flowering ones. So I had to exercise restraint AND have patience. This home-owning stuff is really turning me into a grown up... If you're looking for trees and shrubs, you won't find them here, but for your annuals, perennials and vegetables, Wiethop is a great choice. You can always head next door to Sherwood Gardens for the shrubs and such afterward. Parking can be rough, especially on nice sunny afternoons, but Wiethop opens up early--take advantage of their hours if you don't feel like waiting for a spot and standing in line at check out!

text: On a whim I decided to revist the Painted Cottage cafe on 9/5 and treat myself to a lovely breakfast inside a restaurant whose charming french country atmosphere was perfect for me. Sadly, all I can recall about my dining experience is the price. For $11.45 I ordered mediocre french toast - is it correct to say it was uninspired, forgettable, and I've had better at local diners? I also ordered a side of sausage, and a cuppatea. Perhaps my waiter was having a bad day, but common sense would dictate that if you bring out a full sized porcelin teapot of hot water for my order, then you should give the customer more than ONE teabag. Yes? No, I had one bag, and it didn't last. Trust me, I tried. Also my waiter liked to disappear. Needed cream - he disappeared and came out a several mintues later. Needed my food - another employee on the staff delivered it to me, and had to go back for the syrup and premelted butter. Needed my check - he walked by, said he would be right back with it...and then disappeared. Why is it when another person on the wait staff walked by my table, they wouldn't look at me? In fact, they didn't look at anyone except straight ahead. Odd. Honestly, I'm not trying to be overly critical of this cafe, and in all fairness, I'll go back and try it one more time. However the crux of my review is the high price and the service, and for a breakfast meal costing close to $15 including the tip, color me not impressed.

text: I recently visited friends in Santa Barbara and ended up here to catch up as I've never been before. Char's review was right on I think - it is a confused little tapas place that charges WAY TOO MUCH for their plates. Not only are the portions small (yes, I realize it is a tapas restaurant), but the food isn't even that great! Keep in mind that I've paid the same/more for similar tapas plates in LA restaurants and at least those were good and worth paying for! We ended up ordering the ahi tuna tartar, spicy chipotle prawns and the avocado hummus between 4 people (2 weren't hungry), with 2 drinks per person, and we ended up with almost a $200+ tab. I managed to lick the tapas plate clean, not because it was good, but because I was still hungry and didn't want the drop of sauce that probably cost about 50 cents to go to waste. The sauce on the shrimp was also the only semi-flavorful thing in our food order. Everything else tasted bland and I could have eaten grass and not know the difference. Coming from someone who has had a fair share of luxurious food items, this is not the place to splurge on food. It's just not worth it. I'd give it one star, but added another for their drinks. Yes, those were pretty good. The cucumber martini was strong, and their mojitos and sangrias were pretty tasty, too, but I don't know if I'd come back for them.

text: Now this place is a random neighborhood joint away from Rt 1 in northeast Philly. You would never expect it. It's a peruvian restaurant tucked away a couple of blocks away from Rt 1. I went with some coworkers and the portions were very generous. You can tell when you are the only non-Hispanic person in the room and the waitresses can only speak Spanish that this is the real deal. When you order the ceviche the portion is HUMUNGOUS. I loved the tostones. I'm not a big plantain banana fan, but these were to die for. Lightly salted and crispy, they are yummy. Next time I want to try their tostones filled with chicken or meat. If you love seafood, their seafood platters are plentiful. My brother had the paella valenciana and it was filled with lots of chicken and seafood. For $18 it was huge and we brought it back home. The guy next to us had some HUGE platter of calamari and shrimp and I forgot what it was called but that's what I want next time. Sounds like jaleo or something like that. It is slightly out of the way but you know what...it's worth the trip. Tax is included with each entree and it even has a full serviced bar. I think el balconcito II may be closer off interstate 95, so maybe I'll try that next time. Again, pretty damn good for philadelphia and a neighborhood gem. You can easily find parking on the street.

The German potato salad was very sweet, and the green beans were excellent. All of this goes well with their beer selection, particularly their choices of Sly Fox beers. text: As of this past weekend, I've now made two visits to Farmicia (and feel experienced enough to yelp about it). One thing that must be said up front...their menu has something for everyone, plenty of variety. Overall, I've found both experiences to be quite enjoyable, and equally satiating. A couple of months ago I went for a late lunch and ate the Jumbo Lump Crab Cake on a Brioche Roll. The flavoring was on, and it was a nice sized serving. Before the meal, a manager (perhaps) came by to offer some gourmet bread. Delicious. Service was good, real quick to refill your drinks, without being in your face. This past weekend I went for Brunch, which was a totally different experience. Both visits (on a weekend) I was seated right away, which was nice. Brunch seemed a bit off, quieter, service was a bit slower, asked for some bacon on a grilled cheese (didn't get it), stuff like that. But nothing worth complaining about, because the food makes up for it. No bread offered this time, but I did eat a scrambled egg quesadilla that was oozing with taste. I loved it, spices galore and some cooked up meat. I felt full for most of the day without feeling sick. Try it! Best part about Farmicia is the freshness! Everything tastes like it was grown out back and cooked on the spot. Prices aren't on their website, but I spent around 40 dollars for two both times (w/ one alcoholic beverage per visit. Half price happy hours at times). Overall, 4 out of 5. Great ambience, great food.

text: This restaurant is relatively new to the Alberta Avenue area. It is located on 118ave, at 95th street. Since the first time I ate here, the ambiance has greatly improved (they moved into a space that had been previously occupied by Renato's Italian restaurant, and were renovating the space). The decor is now warm and inviting. They have open seating for larger parties, as well as small tables for smaller groups. Most enjoyably, they have two little sitting nooks that provide privacy and a view of the streetscape. The food is very tasty and well presented. Make sure you're prepared to eat with your hands however, since they don't provide cutlery. You eat your meal by scooping morsels up with injera flat bread, which they refill as required. They have a menu from which you can choose individual items, as well as combination plates. The combination plates feed 2, 4, and I think 6 people. When the food arrives, you'll think you'll have no problem plowing through the meal. Think again! There will be leftovers! Truthfully, you could probably fill three people on the 2-person combo plate! If I remember correctly, a 2-person vegetarian combination plate will set you back about $21. The meat plate for two might run you about $23-25. The menu includes meat dishes (lamb, goat, beef) as well as MANY vegetarian dishes. I have had both and found all of them very flavourful. There are some dishes that are more spicy than others, so if spice is an issue, talk to the server. They will be able to help you chose what is appropriate for your palate. The service is FANTASTIC. The cook has come out every time I have eaten there (5 times since August). She's even given us a little dessert, on the house. The serving staff is friendly, helpful and observant (injera will replaced before you realize you need it). Apparently they hold a coffee ceremony on Saturdays and Sundays around 5pm. I haven't been but I think I will check it out in the near future. I have taken many friends to the restaurant and everyone loves it! I highly recommend trying out this new restaurant. You may want to call to make reservations on Friday and Saturday nights since in it's short existence, it has become a very popular eatery for local residents.

( don't have to pretend to know all sushi, but to enjoy and be able to appreciate the subtle texture and taste in different grade tuna fattiness: OO_TORO, CHU_TORO, Toro, or eel: UNAGI, and ANAGO etc, would be enlightening pleasure with the master chef) I know even before Iron chef Morimoto open his restaurant he came to check his sushi or you would notice many sushi chef from Philly at the counter. Last time I was at table, because the owner chef was not there....and sushi was disappointing. I do not live in Philly any more, but I know Sagami for past 20 years. I have to admit general quality became inconsistent. It is bit sad to see the restaurant is not the best of the best anymore, owner wife ( you can tell her looks and act by Japanese Martha Stewart like) use to care every single detail of the restaurant, always had fresh beautiful bouquet of flower, authentic Japanese kitchen food, best freshest sushi in Philly, and impeccable service. I even used to take a train from Philly to cross Delaware river and walk though Camden to get there when I did not had a car. 12-2008 Also, each fish has its own season, like vegetable. Some of my friends refuse to eat in summer. Like oyster or tomato. Fall to winter, many of sushi fish taste the best and affordable. In the end, usually fish arrives Sagami from NY market on Thursday. For master chef 5stars. Kitchen food 4 stars +, sushi depends on which chef 3~4 stars.

The entrees come with lettuce and pico de gallo, refried beans and some with rice too. The quesadillas are good as an appetizer but not as an entree because they do not come with all of these side dishes. The free chips are fresh and delicious with two salsas that I like to pour all over my meal. Service is good.

text: It's really confusing to me that there are two New Waves Cafes in Philadelphia. It's pretty funny since one is a restaurant in Queen Village and the other, a Polish dive in Port Richmond. I visited recently with a group of friends for lunch. I love that we are painfully out of place. Most people are middle aged and speaking Polish. And even though we're not the normal clientele, the waitress/bartender was very nice. It's almost like mom is serving you, assuming mom is very Polish. They have several polish beers on tap and in the bottle. I had a pint of Okocim at $3, and it tasted about as good. My first visit here a year ago, I had soup, and it was delicious. But since I had borsch for dinner the previous night, I decided to order potato pancakes instead. These were good and crsipy, but nothing spectacular. There are much better options on the menu. We ordered several different kinds of perogies. Everyone ordered fried, and they came out with perfect consistency. The cheese and potato were good, but a bit bland. I enjoyed the mushroom ones more, and really loved the suspiciously labeled "meat" perogies. With a little sour cream on top, all of the perigies were a great choice. We also had an order of kielbasa. Topped with (presumably) homemade mustard, this was fantastic. I'm fairly certain I could eat anything off the menu here and be happy. Bottom Line: I love eating here. You're thrown off by the brightly painted, beach themed sign out front. It's usually pretty empty, and soccer with Polish commentary is liking playing in the background. You can eat for under $10. And all of the food is made in house or locally. And delicious. It's kind of a trip to step right into the heart of Polish Port Richmond, and it's a lot of fun.

text: Just visited this while some friends were in town for the Fourth of July. I was perfectly content to just poke around the lobby and gift shop, but the out-of-towners insisted on seeing the tour. $12 later, I was seated in the small high-tech theater. The speaker/actress did her voiceover work very well, and the presentation was mildly captivating (the presentation format was rather impressive and engaging to me as an audience member). After the brief history of America's creation and the constitution, I followed my friends up to the second floor, where there's a more-or-less self guided tour of various facts and histories revolving around the constitution. Much of it was decent material. My only real complaint is that while watching a humorous video of Ben Stein explaining the various interpretations that could be made of articles and amendments and other facts about the constitution, the video was cut off (in the middle of a segment), and replaced with a PowerPoint presentation entitled "Political Cartoons 101". The only people sitting in the area watching the video were my three friends and I, and soon an employee walked into the area and asked us if we liked cartoons, and proceeded to delve into a 15 minute long presentation on the History of Political Cartoons in America. First off, we were enjoying the Ben Stein video, which was why we were sititng there in the first place, and I was annoyed that she assumed we would rather learn about political cartoons. Secondly, her presentation was dreadfully boring. The four of us just made awkward eye contact with each other debating whether we could leave without insulting her and just mumbled whenever she tried to engage us. Though we were all in our mid-twenties, she posed us questions appropriate to very young gradeschoolers ("Now, what do we all think the shark symbolizes? Anyone? That's right, it's supposed to be something we're afraid of!"), and while I would be fine with this if it were a presentation I chose to go to, she chose to come present this to us (against our will!), and could have at least tailored the presentation to the audience. The final room of the constitution experience was actually very cool. It was just a meeting hall styled room with bronze statues (I'm led to believe they are all accurate life-size casts) of signers of the constitution. They have a guest-signature book out, and it is a very nice photo opportunity kind of room. I regret that my experience here was largely tainted by a sub-par (albeit dedicated) employee, but overall the museum was just 'decent'. If you're a history buff, or just need to say you've been there, I suppose the $12 is worth one trip. I don't think I'll ever go a second time, and I won't likely recommend it to my less-than-110%-patriotic friends. Still, the building is very nice, and that's something too, I suppose.

text: I don't frequent the Manayunk area too often anymore, and when I did it was more to catch a band at Grape and do a little drinking than for eating. Last night I returned to Le Bus for only the second time and I couldn't be happier with the place. It was pretty dead on a Tuesday, so our service was more prompt than I recalled previously. I had a fresh pot of decaf all to myself, which was nice and delicious. My friend and I both ordered the turkey burger, but instead of my usual toppings extravaganza, I decided to just take it as it comes. I have to say, I was more than impressed! The turkey burger itself is ground turkey mixed with celery, spanish onions, shallots, garlic, scallions and peppers. It makes for an extremely tasty burger, even without cheese. (And I love cheese!) And all the extras inside probably are what kept the burger from tasting dried out as so many turkey burgers have the tendency to do. My only regret is that I wasn't more hungry so I could have finished my entire burger and side of sweet potato fries. Some people may think the portions are a bit on the small side, but I actually appreciated the small side of sweet potato fries. It's more in line with what a REAL serving size should be anyway. Overall our experience last night was excellent and I'm glad we happened to be back in the Manayunk area last night so I could have an excuse to enjoy a delicous meal.

text: Lets go with 2.5 stars...meh...maybe 3. La Parilla is one of those restaurants where there's going to be one dish that sticks out, and the others will be left in the dust. Out of the three times I have taken out, I have had four dishes, one of those turned out to be, not as authentic, yet exceptional. Chile Rellenos- For some reason, I wasn't impressed with this dish. It seemed to heavy, and the peppers didn't seem to blend in with the rest of the food. Burrito- Not impressed with this. The tortilla and the meat was dry; no flavor. Tamales- VERY DISAPPOINTED. I've traveled all over the country and have been fortunate enough to belong to a culture(s) to have exceptional cuisine. The best food is the one that takes all day to make! Tamales are one of those dishes. Though tamales are different in all parts of many Hispanic cultures, GOOD tamales are supposed to be soft, not dry, and with a kick. You should also know what kind of meat you're eating, too. With these tamales, the maza (coating) and the...meat (beef? pork?) was dry. Rarely have I seen the mole sauce cover the tamales, and that in itself was spicy but not flavorful. These tamales didn't taste as if they were made with the time and effort other tamales are. I would go as far to say that I would take a frozen tamale from a local Schnucks over this mess. EDIT: So, I realized two things about these tamales. When I got them, they were kinda warm and stiff. When REALLY heated them (after I wrote this review). It was better. The meat was still dry and sub-par, but the maza (too much, really) was soft and edible. It also makes me wonder if I got it at the resturant, would it still taste the same? I got this as take out, and there is no way I should have to reheat take out--and yes, I live 5 minutes from this place so its not as if it is cooled considerably. That's silly. It also doesn't help that their food comes in aluminum containers so you can't just willi-nillie heat it up ASAP. Arroz con pollo- When I think of arroz con pollo, I think of a whole peice of chicken on top of a bed of rice. This rice typically has your standard vegetables, corn, beans, etc. AT LP, they cut tiny pieces of chicken up and serve it with cheesy rice, sour cream, lettuce, tomato, broccoli and cauliflower. At first bite, I wasn't fond of it but it grew on me and I love it. No, its not your typical arroz con pollo but its still worth trying, as it has a very fresh and clean taste. My only problem is that with this dish, the chicken needs to cook along with the rice, but in this dish, the chicken and the rice were cooked differently-- at least it tasted like it. Other than that, the place seemed nice. My other complaint is that the lady said that the tamales were 1.99 but when I got there she said that it was 2.29. She said she was sorry, but, if she gets the $ wrong, I think I deserve to get my food at the price I thought it was. I was so lucky I went in the restaurant with an extra couple of dollars because if I didn't, I wouldn't have had enough money to pay :( My meal has always come with their salsa and chips. They're your standard kind, I suppose, though, I prefer Tostidos with my awesome mango salsa. I don't hate this place, but my opinion of it goes down the more I go. I'll try somewhere else next time.

text: I am a big fan of the sonoran hot dog and this is the place to choose, if you wish to partake of one of the best. Since a sonoran dog is essentially street food, originally served from carts, I give this location an extra star for being a hodge-podge assemblage of carts, tents and random structures. It is also in South Tucson, which gives it extra authenticity. There is another location in Tucson proper, but it has been gentrified, sanitized and fully enclosed (the food is equally good, but tastes less so due to the de-tuned experience). The menu has two staples: sonoran dogs and caramelos, which are basically quesadillas with a choice of meat. While the caramelos are quite good, it is the sonoran dog that delights. It is a hot dog wrapped in bacon and griddled. This is nestled in a steamed bolillo (soft pointed, bun with more structure than a normal hot dog bun) on a bed of beans and topped with chopped tomato, onion, mayo, mustard, and jalapeño sauce. The condiment bar offers several enhancements: pickled onions, cucumber slices, grilled peppers, grilled green onions, and a few salsas. The sonoran dog, as is, is a great balance of flavors and textures. It is perhaps the finest use of the humble hot dog. Both Guero Canelos are counter service. You place your order from the small menu and then wait for them to call out your number first in Spanish and then, if you fail to appear, in English. Everyone is friendly enough and they are very quick with the orders. Check it out next time you are heading south of Tucson. It is an authentic, local experience.

Food runners brought our food, and asked if we wanted sour cream for our baked potato. We instantly put the cash on the receipt tray and sat and waited for our change...and waited, and waited, and waited. I had to get up and walk to the bar where him and the manager were hanging out and ask for him to take our bill and get change...and the manager just looked away! So did we feel bad leaving a penny tip? No. I am actually a phenomenal tipper, but its called a tip because you have to earn it. Give me great service, I will be happy and leave you 25% no problem. text: It's amazing how different the experiences at two different locations of the same chain of restaurant can be. While I've always been a big fan of the downtown Old Spaghetti Factory, I cannot say the same about the WEM location. I've rarely heard anything positive about the WEM location, so when a friend decided to have her birthday dinner here, I was hesitant. But, it would be bad form not to show up on my friend's birthday just because of her choice of venue, so I went along hoping that the rumours were wrong. Unfortunately, all of the negative things I had heard in the past turned out to be true. While my own meal was fine, many people in our party had a less than pleasant experience. One person found a huge hair in their pasta, another was served spumoni that had a piece of lettuce in it (not a big deal, but still poorly prepared/served) and another person found their steak was over-cooked (though she decided not to complain about it). On top of that, my girlfriend's wine seemed like it had been heated up (the half-litre carafe was actually warm to the touch). When she requested a new carafe that was at room temperature, she was served what appeared to be the same wine, shaken with ice in a cocktail shaker and then poured back into the carafe (this is just a guess, based on the amount of bubbles in the wine when it was returned to the table). There also appeared to be a bit of a film when she poured her first glass. We couldn't tell if this was just from the bubbles or if it was soap film from the glass not being rinsed off after being washed. Our waitress wasn't as attentive as I'd have liked, but it was her first shift, so I'm willing to forgive her errors and won't suggest that her performance was representative of the rest of the staff. However, I did notice some odd behaviour by other staff members, the most disturbing of which was the fact that the busboy was carrying the towel used for wiping tables around his neck. I'm sorry, but I don't want your neck grease and hair gel all over my table. Use a clean rag that hasn't been rubbing against your sweaty neck all night, please! After the experience I had at the WEM location of the Old Spaghetti Factory, you can bet that I won't be back. There is a much better, independently-owned Italian restaurant mere steps away and, if I really feel the urge to go to the Old Spaghetti Factory, I'll stick to the downtown location.

text: Fiesta is the time of year that most of the locals I know leave town, (myself especially)! It's loud, it's crowded with tourists, drunks, frat-boys, scantily to obscenely clad young girls and gang-bangers from Oxnard. The bars all charge a high cover fee in order to maximize their Fiesta time income. Even worse than this, the city brings in police forces from all over the state to stand around and eye you under the glare of the bright Third Reich lighting that is also hauled in and installed for the whole occasion. LOUD mariachi bands everywhere and you can't escape the noise and the confetti from all those eggs. It's awful! --- it's messy, it's touristy and it SUCKS. --- Avoid at all costs!!! IF you are a local, then you know that there are a couple of redeeming qualities about Fiesta. For one, those tamales at Our Lady Of Guadalupe church rule. The El Mercado market that they set up in De La Guerra Plaza can be really fun when local bands like Spencer The Gardener are playing. Some of the food is pretty decent too. The Fiesta horse parade is cool. Family fun minus all the drunks that are home nursing thier hangovers from the night before. I especially like the firemen float. Most of all, though, I can totally recommend the Fiesta Bike Run. It takes place on the last day of the whole mess, (usually a Sunday). Bring your bike, some sunscreen, water and a fun attitude. It's total bike chaos, meeting at the dolphin fountain at Stearns Wharf and then proceeding up State st., fully and completely taking over the streets like Critical Mass. SO MUCH FUN! If you've ever been in something like this, you know how much fun it is. Horns honking, people hootin' and hollerin'. It's a total blast. Fun for the whole family and some good excersize too. Although they complain and threaten to every year, I hope they never succeed in shutting down the cruiser run.

text: I'm visiting from out of town this weekend and told my brother I wanted to get a decent cheesesteak while I was here. We ended up at Giordano's for lunch. We arrived around 1:45 totally missing the lunch crowd and had the place to ourselves. There was a bartender and a waitress restocking the bar and our orders were taken immediately. We each ordered a cheese steak and in addition I ordered a slice of pizza. The cheesesteak was awesome. It was about a foot long, cut in half, and full of meat, fried onions and cheese. Some french fries filled the rest of the plate. While not the best cheese steak I've ever had it was definitely a very good one and hit the spot. I'll be happy to have one of these again on my next trip up. The pizza was mediocre. At first glance it the presentation was nice however the best thing about it was the crust. It was definitely fresh. The sauce was bland and all but non-existent. Same of the pepperoni and cheese. It was cheap low grade stuff. Kind of surprising to me since the cheese steak was so top notch and this place promotes itself as a pizzeria. The bartender and waitress were both exceptional. We had great service and good conversation with them and another patron that sat near us. Over all a great time and I'm looking forward to my next visit already.

text: Oh my god! Tears of joy were streaming down my face with every bite. Bern's came highly recommended from my boss and quite possibly changed my life. I'm not sure how yet, but I woke up this morning feeling different (and I am not talking about the hang over). Where do I start? The decor in this place reminds me of the haunted mansion at Disneyland, but it is in every way top notch. Dear Reader, I travel all over the world on an expense account and get to try some amazing restaurants, but this by far was the most special dining experience to date. Big words, i know- but, I promise I am not blowing smoke. If I were to sum it up, this is a restaurant for connoisseurs. Two colleagues and I ordered the 27oz NY Strip and they carved it table side. With the steak came soup, salad, and side dishes - take that all of you a la carte steakhouses. Brad the Sommelier helped us road map our entire experience and we gave him the creative freedom to help us with the near impossible task of picking one bottle of wine for dinner in a wine list the size of a phone book. It couldn't have been more perfect; a 2000 Pauillac. Brad helped us get a great wine for a reasonable price. After dinner we got a tour of the kitchen and the wine cellar and then escorted up to the dessert room. We were already a little toasty by the time we got up there and upon seeing the dessert wine list we knew we had to kick it into gear. I was feeling a little spendy so i opted to spring for a 1949 bottle of port - it tasted so good that I almost cried. The restaurant was very accommodating and allowed us to be the last to leave. We must have left sometime after 1am. I would make a special trip to Tampa from SF just to eat at Bern's. Truly something special.

I've only been here one time but had a very enjoyable experience and will absolutely go back when I'm in town. As an FYI, this was on a Sunday around lunchtime.

text: Gluttony. Pretty much the only word that comes to mind after hitting this place with my friends. I felt like I committed a sinful act to my own body. On a rainy cool afternoon, my friend had recommended a lunch spot he would always like to go but forgot to tell me each time I come down to Nola until now. I should smack him for this. It's as it says, it's a place with house made pate, sausages, and other delicious meat based cuts and creation you can order by the pound. However, the great thing is there is a selection of sides, sandwiches, and plates you could order and each right there. Many of which are based on the most delicious animal in the world, the Cochon (pig). I had chosen the extremely sinful fatty pork belly sandwich with cucumber and mint with an equally guilty pancetta mac n cheese. Both of which are as good as they sound, but I know for sure my arteries must have hate me plenty for gorging on such as fat packed meal. The sandwich was very rich and fatty and topping that with a salty cheesy side was over-the-top indulging. I'd order and eat either of them again, just not together. On the way out I purchased some Rillette to bring home, which turned out to be a great choice to spread on some nice crusty baguettes. Great place to hit for lunch. It's clean, modern, and solid food with what seemed to be a decent selection of wines and beer at a glance. They also have charcuterie and cheese plates if you want something light. I will be back. =)

text: As I write this, I am completely stuffed to capacity from my meal at Bern's. When walking into the place, I was reminded of the Crazy Horse from the outside visade. The interior decor inside is unlike any steakhouse I've been to before, with a sort of renaissance mansion/burlesque/haunted house feel. The menu is pretty detailed with a variety of cuts of steaks and recommendations for preparation. The steaks are accompanied by an an assortment of sides including onion rings, baked potato, fresh veggies, french onion soup, and salad. An upgrade to the caesar salad is recommended. They make the dressing tableside, starting with grinding down the anchovies. Bern's prides themselves on their organic ingredients and even have their own farm 8 miles north of Tampa. Their wine list is the most expansive that I've ever seen at over 100,000 bottles. They will even give you a tour of the kitchen and wine cellar after your meal. If you're up for dessert, you can go to the "Dessert Room" upstairs and enjoy their house-roasted coffee and your choice of more than a dozen indulgent desserts.

text: My wife and I went there as we normally walk around the park and thought we'd frequent one of the latest businesses to open in our neighborhood. I'll leave aside the question about the decision to be half cafe/half eclectic store and focus on the restaurant experience. Layout: It has a quaint, comfortable feel both inside and out - nice big seats inside to relax in the A/C on a hot day, and the usual outdoor tables with umbrellas to enjoy the breezes, fresh air, and view of the park across the street. Food: The menu seems to be a mix of whatever is in the display case and some made to order items from a menu board which is inconveniently placed off to one side and not immediately obvious to those who first walk in. We had the quiches (delicious) and the pasta salad, which was frankly a bit of a let down (watery/vinegery, not terribly flavorful). The coffee was good, but not great - the new machine they have across the way at Park Avenue Coffee makes a MUCH better espresso/latte/etc if that's what you're after). Service: This is where it really fell down for us. It seemed as if on some level they were trying really hard (good table service, for example, when bringing out your order), and then dropped the ball on other areas - for example, i heard four separate identical conversations (one with us, three with other tables) while we were there, which consisted of the server saying to the patron - "If you want silverware or napkins, they are inside next to the coffee station." My first thought is, "well, if you're bringing us food, wouldn't it make sense to bring us the utensils, too? otherwise, what's the point as we have to go back inside anyways, and now it's after the food has arrived..." The other thing was a strange vibe that we picked up that just seemed out of place for the laid back nature of our neighborhood. It's hard to describe, but it just didn't seem as friendly or welcoming as all the other shops we normally frequent here. Overall: I know they're still fairly new, and maybe there's still the teething pains and stress of getting into their stride.... we do intend to go back a few more times to see how things improve through the summer/fall.

text: My husband and I were staying at the Don Cesar and wanted a really high-quality seafood dinner off the Don's property. I used my handy Yelp mobile app to find Snappers, and we were not disappointed! We started with the Gulf-to-Bay oysters, which had a heaping layer of spinach, breadcrumbs and tomato sauce on top. While I thought the topping overwhelmed the surprisingly tiny oyster meat, I had never had oysters before so I had no basis for comparison to know if we got screwed on the size of the oysters or not. Regardless, they were delicious and prepared to perfection. Our meals came with a house salad and Snappers' signature hummus and pita chips. The salad was a very generous portion, and the pita chips were warm and crispy. I thought the hummus was interesting, as it was chunkier than normal and had a spicy kick to it, which I assumed was cumin. It was a bit too much cumin for my taste, but my husband loved it. Hubby got the Stuffed Gulf Grouper which came served with Snappers' signature potato puff pastry, fresh steamed vegetables and some sort of shredded radish salad. I was blown away by the portion of the meal, as places at this price point usually have high-quality food but completely skimp on the portions. I had a bite of everything on his plate (including a crabcake he ordered a la carte) and have never tasted a plate so full of fresh, hot, flavorful food. I ordered the chef's special that evening, which was a Tandoori-roasted Escolar. I had never eaten escolar before and it was tender, yet chewy and robust - not as delicate as, say, halibut. It was roasted beautifully and laid in a light champagne sauce that was both creamy and flavorful without being heavy or overly salty. I also had grilled asparagus and garlic whipped potatoes on my plate, both of which were delectable and complemented the escolar perfectly. Not only was the food incredible and the value for the price quite reasonable, but our server was an absolute delight! She was knowledgeable, friendly without being invasive, and I was very impressed when, as I was taking photos of my food, she asked if it was for Facebook or another restaurant review app. I can always appreciate a social media-savvy individual! :) Finally, I wanted to make a quick note on the atmosphere: the restaurant strikes a great balance of casually elegant and modern. It doesn't feel too pretentious and, though it doesn't boast significant square footage, you can still feel intimate without feeling cramped in amongst other diners.

text: For the price, this hotel falls very short. There are nice things about it, but the service lacks. They didn't start out very well when I flew into the Nashville airport at 8:30 pm, visited their shuttle desk, paid $40 for a round trip shuttle, was told the shuttle would be there in 10 minutes, and an hour later, I finally had to call the hotel asking where they were. Their answer? One of the two "shuttles" had mechanical problems and they didn't know someone was waiting at the airport and they would be there in 7 minutes. 15 minutes later, a full-sized tour bus came to pick me up. They are definitely doing their part to contribute to global warming. By the way, I found out a taxi ride from the airport is $25. I wish I would have known that. When I finally got to the hotel, I waited another 20 minutes to check in. This might be normal during the late afternoon. But, it was now nearly 11pm and I was the first in line the whole time. There were about 5 or 6 people running around behind the front desk, but I have no clue what they were doing. What I DO know is that they weren't checking me in. Just a warning to anyone who has difficulty walking. There is a good chance you will have to walk a really, really long way to find your room (that's if you ever actually find it). I'm sure they make a pretty penny on the motorized wheel chairs they rent for $45 a day. I'm fortunate and able to walk, so I headed off with my map, dragging my luggage and got quite a workout, but eventually found my room. I suggest bringing a compass and a canteen for the trek to your room. I saw no sign of bell service. My room was clean and efficient. When I say efficient, I mean small. If you are looking for a spacious room, forget this hotel. The bed was OK. I'm not big on pillowtop mattresses, but I know they are the current trend. I tried to change the temperature in the room several times, following the very explicit directions. It never worked. If you aren't into 71.7 degrees, you may be in trouble. The bathroom was OK. Basic soap, shampoo, conditioner. No shower cap, no other amenities. The hair dryer didn't work, so I had to call for a new one. The food I ate in the restaurants was OK. The only really good food was served at a convention dinner I attended. The service in the restaurants was OK. Probably the best service I got all week was the room service. It was speedy and effiicient. If you want your room made up anytime before 5pm, this hotel will probably not be for you. Housekeeping has two speeds: slow and stop. Probably, the most pleasant surprise was the fitness center. There are plenty of up-to-date machines from treadmills and eliptical machines to weight machines and free weights. The fitness center overlooks the pool and is clean and well-lit. The daily mandatory resort fee includes use of the fitness center and pools. The pools looked very nice, too. Internet access was good and fast. The convention center was nice. Nothing stood out bad or good. The atriums, waterfalls and plants are all nice if you are into fake and sterile "nature". I guess it would be worth a stroll through the place if you were staying in another hotel. I was here on business, so it was OK because I was usually in meetings. I would never spend my own money on this place.

text: one word....YUMMY! So my husband and I were heading to Clearwater for a play that a friend was in. We headed over and got there at about 5:20. It was kind of dead, but within 15-20 minutes it was getting packed! It's not a huge place, but it is a nice place. The building seems to be well kept and has a nice italian feel. You can sit indoors or out. Neither my husband or I were that hungry due to a late lunch, but knew we had to eat something so that we weren't starving in the middle of the play - no one wants a loud growling tummy during those inevitable silent moments in a play! We decided to share a "personal" pizza. I love that a 12" pizza is considered "personal." We ordered the Margherita pizza - tomato sauce, mozzarella, oregano, and basil. Nothing too fancy, we like our pizza simple :P Now I will tell you that this place is not a normal Pizza Hut Pizza like place. It is much more like authentic Italian pizza...though I've yet to find pizza that's exactly like the pizza I had while in Italy. Oh well. They have lots of food besides pizza. They have cold or cold paninis, ravioli, pasta, appetizers, soups, salads, etc. There are a lot of options. Okay, to the pizza arrived...in what seemed like no time at all. We both started to eat...and next thing we knew, the whole thing was gone. Seriously, I wasn't that hungry...but I couldn't stop eating the pizza because it was so tasty! Then it happened....they are smart people...they gave us small samples of four of their gelato flavors! How they know me so well, I'm not sure. I LOVE Gelato. It makes me think of my short trip to Italy where I think we had gelato every day we were there because it was SO yummy! We ended up getting a small vanilla with dark chocolate chunks gelato (which has a long Italian name that I couldn't pronounce). The small was $3.50 and was probably about the size of a Cold Stone Creamery Like It size...actually probably in between that size and the Love it size. It was a nice amount. It was delicious and creamy. It was amazing...and now I want more...ugh. My husband also ordered a cannoli and he was in love! Over all we had a great experience. We are already raving about it to friends. We overheard the owner while we were there saying that he would love to open up in Tampa, but right now it's just not possible. I really wish that would change, because it would be nice to not have to drive so far to get such delicious food. I also think they would do really well in Tampa!

text: I'll happily update this review should things change, but right now I'm pretty pissed at City Fitness. I should have been wary in Dec 07, when first walking in to sign up for an account, there was a customer yelling about his account at the front desk. I should have walked right away! So the deal at the time was $99 to sign up and $59.99 a month thereafter. I am an avid reader of contracts, and I pointed out the many loopholes to them before signing it. I was assured it was a very casual contract, they were a neighborhood business, and they weren't going to screw anyone over. What a convincing little song and dance. Well, I believe in giving people (especially neighbors, and so called "neighborhood businesses") the benefit of the doubt, so I signed up because they were conveniently located and had yoga classes. And for 6 months, I happily went to my yoga classes and paid my bills. ...Until one day I come in and find out it's going to cost an additional $10 a month (in the middle of my contract!!) to continue to attend those yoga classes. Pretty shady, right? Whatev. Since they bailed on their own contract, all I want is a refund of the initiation fee, and a refund of the last 39 days I'd prepaid upon signing up back in December. They've decided to ignore that request. The excuses they've given me on the phone are piss-poor, and one member of their staff even got verbally abusive on the phone. I highly recommend you check out the neighborhood message board, northernliberties.org, before considering a membership here. I'm not the only one to complain (just the first one on Yelp, for some reason). Here's one recent thread in particular: http://pub50.bravenet.com/forum/4226496069/show/637106 If City Fitness does the right thing and refunds my money (and reconsiders cheating its members in this manner) I would update my rating to 3 stars. There are a lot of excellent things about this gym, and there are a lot of things that leave a foul taste in your mouth. Here's the short list: The good: - Many of the yoga teachers, including Lisa, Kelly and Mark, are fabulous and I miss them. - The TVs & vents atop each aerobic machine are nice - The overall gym vibe is nice, full of neighbors, not meatheady The bad: - The gym has some cleanliness issues. Yes it is new so it looks new, but get close up to a yoga mat: they don't get scrubbed down and you can smell an interesting, unique sweat bouquet on each one. Dust bunnies float about like tumbleweed, too. The bathrooms are often out of toilet paper and I used a shower once and told myself never again, ew. A professional cleaning company really needs to be hired here. - When machines break, they should be fixed promptly. Some of the treadmills were very shaky. Some of the TVs and air vents don't work. - The nickel-and-diming across the board is very annoying. How about providing towels for the prices we are paying? Or the full shampoo/soap/conditioner range in the showers? And the website still says a juice bar is "coming soon." I was told it was "coming soon" in December and it's still not been worked on. Oh, and the tanning bed costs extra? They should clearly state what is covered in a membership before people sign up. Because all things (that you don't know up front) considered, it's not that great a deal. Sigh. Now to find another yoga place.

text: I've been to Elle on a couple of occasions and have always left with an "eh" feeling about it. I've never been able to say that one thing stood out as actually being really good. Their wines are decent, their pastas are ok, the ahi tuna was pretty bad, the service has been sub-par... Last night, however, Elle stood out... In the worst way... I went with a group of friends for a "girls night out". We were doing dinner and a show. We showed up to the restaurant and were seated around 6:15. We thought we'd have plenty of time to get through dinner and be at our show at the TCC by 8. We were approached by a backserver who looked perpetually stoned and he brought us waters as he gawked at us like he'd never seen a pretty girl before. Our server showed up about 7 minutes later to take our drink order. We ordered 2 bottles of wine with our appetizer, but didn't expect to have to wait for our wine until our app was ready, and she only brought us 1 bottle and acted surprised when we told her we had ordered a white wine as well. The white wine took another 10 minutes to get to us. The appetizer was ok. The dinner itself wasn't bad. 4 of us had different pasta dishes that we enjoyed and 1 had the short rib that smelled more tasteful than it actually was. Around 7:15 we began to get nervous about the time and our backserver cleared our dishes and we asked him to have our server bring us the check... About 5 minutes later, he came back with dessert menus instead... We decided we'd order a dessert and tell the waitress to bring our check before the dessert came out so we could leave at our convenience. We didn't get the check until our dessert was gone. We gave her our payments and said to split it evenly five ways (we are all servers ourselves, so we know that's not a hard thing to do). 5 minutes later the server comes back showing us the long division she did on the back of the check so we'd know what we were all paying... Awesome, but we're in a hurry and had already figured that out... It's not like you're going to show us our totals and we are going to change our minds about the payment... One girl put cash in (which we asked for change for since we were splitting evenly and the girl's long division accounted for that) but the girl did it wrong and applied our friend's entire $40 to the bill and then split the remainder 4 ways, so now we all owe our friend money. One girl didn't even get her credit card receipts, so the 2 girls who weren't going to the show said they'd figure it out for us since we had been trying to pay our bill for 40 minutes and now our show was starting in 5. We got to a show we spent $50 to see and had to wait outside and watch the first 15 minutes on a little tv. We called our friend at intermission to see how the rest of the night went for her and she informed us that the waitress was rude to her and blamed the missing card receipt on us... At this point I was so enraged that I thought I'd call and inform a manager about our evening. I actually was able to speak to the owner who seemed a little less than upset about how we were treated and said that if we'd like to come back, he'd buy us dessert... I'm not in the business of asking for free things, but when my friends and I have been put out and our waitress has treated us like we don't matter and made us late for a show and nearly ruined our evening, it's going to take a lot more than a free dessert to make me want to go back and spend more money at this restaurant... To top our evening off, we saw the entire staff of Elle at a bar after our show and got some lovely glares and looks from our server and her friends. Thanks for that... Long story short, this restaurant doesn't seem to care about their patrons... If you want a real nice dinner with quality service and food, I'd suggest going to Feast or a Fox restaurant like North or Wildflower.... I guess it's true what they say, give somebody good service and they'll tell close friends, give somebody bad service and they'll tell the world...

text: Sherman Properties rented me my first place in East Falls in 2001.
