However, at some point a long time prior to me renting my place, someone had ordered their gas and electric service under a different apartment and street number completely - one which belonged to the house next door. Having no clue about this, I ordered my electric and gas to my street and apartment number, and was concerned when I received bills that said I owed either nothing, or at the most, twenty dollars. Then one Friday morning, my heat got turned off (and yes, it was wintertime). After numerous phone calls, the gas and electric companies set me straight and told me that Sherman Properties registered my particular apartment as a different house number, and though it was no fault of my own, someone from Sherman had to come and unlock a box in order for the companies to be able to turn on the heat and electric for my apartment. Essentially, I was paying for a vacant home's heat and electric for months, and a vacant home was getting my electric and heat bills and not paying for them. I called Sherman to discuss this and Sherman said they don't come out on Fridays or weekends and would have to take care of it Monday. I begged and begged. It was so cold in my place that I was sleeping in a jacket and two sweaters and my roommate couldn't even bear it - she took off and went somewhere else for a bit. I didn't have that "luxury" as my job needed me to come in. Sherman wouldn't budge. I made an appointment for Monday morning. I called out of work. Sherman did not come to unlock the box. The oil and electric companies both came - on time! - and would not give me another appointment until I had direct word from Sherman that they'd actually show up to unlock the box for them. It took another three days for Sherman to unlock the box. I emerged from the incident very sick from days of no heat in winter. When I wrote Sherman a letter to complain, they sent me back a form letter indicating that they are excited that East Falls has many new restaurants and shops opening up in the spring and attached as a coupon for the Mexican restaurant opening next door. My apartment was decent; it was bi-level with the lower level being garden-style (basement) and the second level meeting up with the street. The rooms were small, but the price was good and it was a nice enough place for two young people to live. However, the care Sherman put into it - or us, their tenants - was nonexistent, and we chose not to lease again. Sherman took two months to send back our security deposits, and were very rude to me when I would call and ask for its whereabouts. I gather that Sherman had bigger, better plans in mind - and perhaps those were a success - but stepping on the littler people on the way is not a great way to do business. Had they been better to their tenants, perhaps we would have stuck around and frequented those new restaurants and shops... all of which have since closed down - except one... because they can't even rent out their apartments these days.

text: I suppose the facility served its purpose in the sense that yes, it's a budget hotel. The room was fine - we only needed a place to sleep a few hours before heading back out on the town... Jazz Fest rates were in the 160.00/night range - pretty steep, all things considered. However, they are getting one star because of this: Sunday morning, we realized that four of our Jazz Fest tickets were gone. After tearing the room apart, to no avail, we went downstairs to the front desk to report the loss to the Asst. General Manager, Eric. At first, he was helpful enough, and came up to the room with the little black box that plugs into the key module on the door. A cursory analysis of the findings indicated that on Saturday afternoon, our room was in fact keyed into twice by a hotel employee's keycard - despite having a Do Not Disturb placard on the door. Our room was left un-touched by housekeeping, as we wished. Later that afternoon, I returned to the hotel to see if Eric had made any progress with the inquiry to the keycard holder, and he said that well, it appears that woman didn't actually have that keycard. He wouldn't look me in the eye as he reported this. Eventually, realizing this was leading nowhere, I got the name of his boss, and we were to take it up with her on Monday morning. She was somewhat concerned, it seemed, with our report, but still dismissive of our claim - the report was now that our room was only keyed into once on Saturday, not twice, but conveniently, the batteries were dead in the little black box. Fortunately, we were able to purchase more Jazz Fest tickets from the Sheraton, but we were still out over 200.00 for the stolen ones. After brunch and touring around some, we came back and found out she had 'closed' the case - assuming we had found our tickets. Ummm, no - we had checked out hours before. We re-opened the case, and now the story was that yes, our room was keyed into, but the handle wasn't turned. That makes a whole lot of sense... or not... The housekeeping log noted the DND sign. We chose the Holiday Inn Express because it was a chain, and they are usually pretty good about security and the likes. We were disappointed by the ever-changing story from hotel management, a complete lack of interest in digging too deep into the issue, and absolutely no semblance of responsibility for the actions of the staff... If you stay here, leave nothing of value behind in the room, as there are no safes available. The hotel management kept saying that the cleaning lady was new to the job and country, didn't speak English, and they couldn't readily communicate with her, and because of that, she didn't even know what Jazz Fest was!!! Also, she was at work on Sunday, so the tickets would have "no value" to her. Right - tickets have no value, except of course their same-as-cash nature.. Take your business elsewhere - support the local merchants and stick with a B&B or private Inn...

I asked for a seat at one of the 5 empty tables for 4 that were in the open area of the main room and was told that these were all reserved--however, these tables remained empty for our entire meal. I can only suppose that the restaurant was holding these tables open for possible walk ins, which did not appear. The maitre-d's attitude towards my table request I found to be very condescending as he assured me that the table tucked into the corner next to the kitchen door was one of the most requested tables in the restaurant. He staunchly refused to offer any of the larger tables. On the plus side, this restaurant has a very pleasing "french" ambiance and several of the servers were native French. There was also a large party of French speakers at one of the back tables. So if you want to feel a little like you are in France, its worth checkiing out. The service at A La Maison reminded me of the service I experienced in most French cafes, which is to say not very attentive, and somewhat brusque. A La Maison is a BYOB. I noted that our waitress did not offer to open the wine. After I asked, she opened it, then set it on the table rather than pouring it into the glasses. text: This is what I have been waiting for. A place where a man can get a man's sandwich. And a place where the sandwiches are affordable. And a place where the sandwiches are delicious. I was dying to try Fozzie's ever since they opened, and upon viewing the menu, I know I will become a regular within no time. My first visit I opted to go with The Big Bend Mafia. A delectable mix of spicy italian beef and salsiccia suasage covered with peppers, onions and cheese and smashed between two hoagie buns. We got our meal to go, and by the time I got home the juices from my sandwich were seeping through the paper my sandwich was wrapped in - a true sign of a great sandwich. The Mafia was bursting with spices and flavor - and the meat had some kick to it. My wife had the falafel sandwich, which was pretty good but didn't compare to mine. The falafel came on a bun in 3 round "pucks" along with a bunch of other more healthy toppings than my Big Bend Mafia. It still tasted good. We both had the home-made chips which were surprisingly crunchy and delicious, cut very thin and cooked to a good crisp. Most home made chips are too thick and soggy and covered in grease, these had a good crunch - quite the opposite. She also ordered the Carmel milkshake - another big hit. Sweet and creamy delight! I liked this place so much I brought my brother back the next day and he had rave reviews for it as well (he had the classic italian sandwich). I would recommend ordering ahead by calling - we did have to wait awhile for our food when we just walked in to order. But, everything is made fresh, which partially explains the wait. It was worth it. I can't wait to go back and try some of the extensive menu Fozzie's has to offer.

text: I was really disappointed by Tabu. This place has soooo much potential, but it's being wasted at the moment. Maybe they think they don't need a sign because it's right next door to the 12th Street gym. The downstairs space is enormous with a bar and plenty of table seating. Even though the place was nearly empty, the service wasn't very good. But the server might have been new and that is why she forgot orders and took a long time in serving drinks. The menu looked good, but I think the presentation left something to be desired. The food was in generous portions, but didn't look appetizing. When I went upstairs to use the restroom and see the lounge, I gasped. It is this large, long empty space. The space is breathtaking with window views of 12th street. I ended up staying upstairs for a long time and was the only person there. I thought that Tabu has a treasure of a space and fantasized about what I'd do if I owned Tabu. The upstairs could be a fabulous dance spot. Or a performance space. The decor in the lounge was shabby with visible plaster on the floor. The furniture was modern, but looked cheap. With the economy, I understood that the owners were probably losing money and couldn't decorate. But they had scant decoration using dollar store paper lamp shades. Tabu is a diamond in the rough... I fear that the place will go under if it doesn't attract a clientele. Right now it's used as a spillover place for more popular gayborhood spots. They are trying to bringing people in with Quizzo and karaoke. We'll see how it goes. I want Tabu to get out of it's gawky teenage phase and blossom. Go Tabu, go!

text: Whenever anyone asks me what I like better, Pat's or Geno's, I always answer, "Philip's of course." I love this place. There are a number of great reasons this is the best steak spot in town. But let's just talk about the steak. Some places like to chop the meat like crazy when it's on the grill, giving it an almost ground meat consistency. Most pizza places do this, and so does Jim's and Dallesandro's. Geno's and Pat's, and Tony Luke, and Steve's Princess Steaks, all leave the steak unchopped, which is better. But Philip lands right in the middle, he chops it a couple times. And there is plenty of meat, without it being ridiculous. The meat is fresh cut every morning. Philip himself told me that he does it most of the time. And due to the fact that it's kinda out of the way, there's never a long line and they make your steak to order. It's not sitting on a pile or in a warmer like the busy places at cheese steak corner. And Philip's will accommodate any special order. My friend likes his steak with sauce, and he likes it cooked with the sauce on the grill, and he likes a lightly sauteed hoagie onion, not the chopped onions, and they'll do that for him, no problem. try asking somebody at Pat's or geno's or jim's to do that. you'll get stabbed, or at least glared at and told to move to the back of the line. Anyway, this place is the best. So if you're in your car trying to park at pat's and geno's, just keep driving and go up to broad street, make a left, and then make a right at passyunk. it's about 5 min's down the road. the extra time you spend in your car will be handed back to you in spades when you can just walk right up to the counter and get your delicious steak right away. All without freezing your ass in line, and trying not to get in a fight with one of the hundreds of drunk douchebags around you. No excuses, Philip's is open all night, too.

text: Shangri La! Much like its semi-mythical namesake, the restaurant is shrouded in lore. A full-on, vegetarian cafe/restaurant in the heart of meat-mad St. Louis? It sounds like a mirage, an explorer's story that's more wishful thinking or fatigue-inspired false recollection. But venturing down to nearly the terminus of the criminally underrated Cherokee Street strip, you soon find out that the cafe is very, very real. It's not a perfect place. I've had better veggie fare, although this is the type of joint that wins massive points for knowing their audience. It's mostly uncompromising towards non-vegetarians but not militant (notice the only meat on offer, salmon, which pops up in three dishes), and always friendly, plus the menu's massive range (excellently mimicking what a proper diner ought to offer with great stuff like a veggie meatloaf platter) goes a long way towards balancing out the sometimes average quality. More than anything else, Shangri La is a refuge for the meat weary. Its '60s thrift store decor and space-age plastic tableware, bright colors, and enthusiastic, tattooed/pierced alterna-hippie staff wrap you in a comforting, accepting embrace. It's also a prime location to dig in to healthy, vegetarian fare or to snag hearty comfort food that both soothes the soul and satisfies that occasional animal flesh craving, but won't quite give you a coronary in the process. Of special note is Shangri La's vegetarian brunch, which knocks the one over at Mokabe's into a cocked hat. You won't wait for a table, you won't be overwhelmed by the din, and while the spread wasn't as ginormous, upon walking away I felt more satisfied. As a word of warning, the buffet selection varies and can be somewhat meager: on my last visit, there were hash browns, a tofu scramble (of sorts), blueberry pancakes (that were delicious but basically and weirdly cold), a green salad, some type of veggie sausage patty, and the meal's crown jewel, insanely tasty brioche french toast. Wash it all down with multiple cups of dark, freshly roasted coffee and you've got enough fuel to power you all over south city till dinner time rolls around. I can't stress enough the quality of the coffee, by the way. It's easily one of the top 5 cups of joe in the STL, and possibly the best that isn't made one cup at a time. In fact, a bottomless mug and one of the handful of sidewalk tables is a reason alone to frequent the place. That said, actually doing so is one of the strikes against Shangri La. Their small-scale, DIY ethic unfortunately means they're only open Thursday through Sunday, and that they don't open till 11am, 9am on weekends. But while the schedule is odd enough to prevent it from becoming a daily haunt, Shangri La's variety, dedication, and radiant, living room vibe are more than enough to make it a destination when its doors *are* open.

text: I've been reading about how New Orleans was voted the number one spot in the nation for flea markets; so how come Yelp is lacking on reviewing them? This is why a NOLA Elite is needed... Of all the stores and spots she recommended, this was my favorite and definitely the best. It was a little difficult to find because their address online says the city's name is Jefferson and my GPS only recognizes Jefferson as a parish. Now I know it's in New Orleans city, and not all the far away at all. It's located literally right by the river, separated by a grassy bank and the levee. The building is HUGE. It's like a warehouse divided into little rooms, all of which are decorated with amazing antiques and thrifty finds for a fairly reasonable price (about 125 for a desk-sized table, 150 for a wardrobe or dresser). It's not the cheapest spot, but the quality of the merchandise makes up for it. They get most of their merchandise from estate sales, apparently, and the eclectic collection certainly reflects that. Several of the rooms are themed: jewelry, records, children's furniture and toys (there was an amazing vintage rocking chair that I would buy just to anticipate having children... except I'm not), books, etc. Outside in a small gated area, they sell specialty Mexican pottery, most of which is large and would be appropriate for a yard, and wrought iron benches and trellises. I purchased a vintage bracelet for $5, and I can't wait to go back and actually purchase furniture, once I'm moved in! Just don't beat me to it; there's a table and a bedframe that I've already got my eye on...

text: I have been wanting to go to this place for a while. I live about 10 minutes from here but didn't even realize it until we drove there last night. I saw it on Yelp and thought it sounded interesting, then drove by it once and knew I had to try this out. My girlfriend and I were craving BBQ and were going for a late dinner and they served until midnight. We also wanted to watch the Cards game after the rain delay which started at 9:35 so it was all going to work perfect. I wasn't sure if they had TVs but when we got there, they had 2 flat screens in the corners of the bar area which were both easy to see from anywhere in the bar an most of the restaurant area. The place isn't that big but there is plenty of seating, it was very slow when we got there so we could sit wherever we wanted so it was great. The band had finished up right before we got there but we were actually happy. We sat there and had dinner and drinks watching the game and listening to the music on the jukebox. The place is pretty cool on the inside. There is all kinds of stuff on the walls but not cheesy like an Applebees. Our waitress Kendra was awesome. Super sweet girl and did a great job filling drinks and making sure everything was good. I don't know what it'd be like if really busy but was good this night. Now to the food: I had the half rack of spare ribs, with cream corn souffle, and mac and cheese. My girlfriend had the 1/4 BBQ chicken with the BBQ spaghetti. Everything was very good. The corn souffle was basically cornbread but had a lot of corn in it and was very good. The mac and cheese had spiral noodles and was super cheesy w/ a nice baked crunch on top. The BBQ spaghetti was interesting but very good. Another Yelper said it was basically spaghetti with BBQ sauce on it, which it was but with some meat in it and was good. My ribs were meaty with a nice little char on the outside like they were finished off on the grill. I also had a couple beers along with a specialty cocktail. We really enjoyed the ambiance, food, service, drinks. It was great for dinner and would be a fun place to hang out and watch a band. We will definitely be back to try more items off the large menu and will bring visitors here as well.

Bluefin is notorious for it's shabby exterior, chic interior, so the strip mall didn't scare me. What did scare me were the prices. Maybe I'm just used to crummier sushi, and I understand this is all *the freshest* fish available prepared perfectly. I would've liked to see my budget go a little further, and my companion and I left hungry. What we did have, Miso Soup, Sushi Dinner and Rainbow Roll, were excellent. The soup starter was fresh and not overwhelming or too salty. The fish, literally, melted in my mouth with a dab of wasabi and a splash of soy. The pickled ginger was used sparingly. Ending the meal with some fresh-cut pineapple and tempurad banana (that is served so piping hot, we might have to join that Starbucks tea lawsuit for burnt tongue! So worth it though...) was a nice treat. For $50, the meal lasted all of 30 minutes...guess we should've ordered more and expanded our budgets, so now we know. We will be trying Bluefin again once we've saved some money in our Sushi jars at home.

text: If you are serious about your coffee, this is the place to go in Santa Barbara. There is a nice selection of teas as well, which come served in a small tea pot. I recommend the Cakewalk if you like ginger. The Magic Bowl (Chamomile, steamed soy, honey) and the Chocolate Chai are fun treats for those with a sweet tooth. I buy my beans for home from here as well, they use and sell Verve coffee http://vervecoffeeroasters.myshopify.com/ My favorite roast is the Manheling Sumatra. The last thing I'll say is that this is a coffee shop to invest in if you are a local. Make yourself a regular, talk to the staff about the coffee, especially Todd and Julia the owners, and you will be rewarded. No, seriously, they gave me and my friend who have been regulars there since opening a free FP mug, which is not only very nice, but a perfectly proportioned and weighted mug for morning coffee sipping at home. Pros: high quality coffee, tea, and espresso drinks knowledgeable staff patio seating Verve beans downtown location non-cliche coffee shop music Cons: no outlets (for laptops, ect.)

text: This restaurant is located inside the Inn at Chester Springs. First off it's a restaurant within a hotel/motel, which already puts it at a serious disadvantage. It's tough for these types of restaurants to really stand out and distinguish themselves. They have to pretty much be doing everything right. The place is fairly cozy - read small. In fact the bar of the same namesake right next door is actually twice as large as the restaurant. The place is done up to be slightly upscale in terms of decorations and table settings. As for the food, we were there on a Friday night and it turns out they have a buffet on Fridays. It smelled good and the price was right so we opted for it. For starters they had mixed greens salad which was fresh and delicious, a mozzarella salad, breads and chilled shrimp. The chilled shrimp where the medium-small size and they had a really off/chlorine taste to them. Fortunately I only took a few of the shrimp. For entrees they had a cook to order station with choice of pasta, toppings and sauces. They also had a chicken dish, tilapia in a butter cream sauce and prime rib. The sides were mashed potatoes, squash and a few other typical sides. The pasta was so-so. The chicken was the same. The big stars of the night were the tilapia, the prime rib and the mashed potatoes as all were delicious. My wife even commented that the tilapia and the mashed potatoes were amazing. The desserts were in a word, horrible. It was painfully obvious from just looking at them that they were the mass manufactured type (you know, the kind that taste like Little Debbie) and not at all fresh. We sampled a few between my wife and I but were disappointed by it all. The service was half decent and friendly, though not exceptional. Our server was MIA at various times which for how small the dining area is and how empty it was when we were there is a bit ridiculous. Another strike was that the first wine glass I was given had obvious lip marks on it. YUCK! This is a fairly benign place that I think wishes it was more than it is but just doesn't have the tools to quite get there. I would really be curious as to what items from their regular menu taste like but I doubt we'll bother going back just to see.

text: So, positives and negatives: Positives: Decor is nice, very well appointed and nicely done It is quiet as you get into the inner sanctum of the restaurant It is upscale but not stuffy The Margaritas were good, especially as I am not a Margarita fan. It had no texture, was awefully briney, and had no flavor, versus some mild flavor. and it was slimy. Like thick korean Seaweed used in soup, but the seaweed has flavor and some texture. I remember Cactus as being subtle, but this was just bad. The Filet Mignon was not a Filet, it was a poor cut of tenderloin masquerading as a Filet Mignon. It lacked the flavor or tenderness of a Filet Mignon. The low star count is due to the quality of food versus price of food ratio being off. The entree was just that unappealing, and we go out to restaurants for the food, not the atmosphere. I would go for a drink and appetizers after work with some friends. I would not see myself going there for a main course sit down type dinner again. The interior is nice, well done, and a pleasant place I could sit, drink, and have some side dishes. If it was a Tapas type place with no main course/entrees, I would give it 3 stars. text: This is our second visit to Philly from DC in the last month. It's closer than NY and has some fantastic dinning options and a good nightlife. Last time we stayed at the Hyatt at the Bellevue, which was okay, so this time we decided to stay at the Westin. Between the two, the Westin is the clear winner. Our check-in process was a bit rocky. Marcel, the front desk person who checked us in, was very nice; however, there was a long queue of guests waiting to check-in and just her working the front desk. The have a sign for gold and platinum members (I'm platinum) next to one of the front desk stations, but no one was working it. Since the check-in process is so important, you're probably wondering why I gave the Westin 5 stars. The reason is that the staff is outstanding. They really turned the experience around for me. From the bell hop who brought water to the room to Marcel calling the desk morning to make sure the stay was going well, everyone was great. Westin Hotels have a "service express" button on the phone, which is centralized operator rather than multiple buttons (front desk, housekeeping, valet, etc.) This is actually a really good feature because you're dealing with the same people each time you call and don't have to think about which department would be most appropriate. The risk to a Westin is that the service express person is your only point of contact, so he or she really must be great. I've been to hotels where the service express person isn't friendly or doesn't care, and this ruins the hotel experience. This was NOT the case here. The lady working Saturday and the gentlemen working Sunday were both incredibly friendly, knowledgeable, and seemed to really care about making sure our stay was wonderful. Our room, 1412, was quite nice. It's 400sq ft with a lounging chair, desk with built in plugs (great for charging all the electronics), and a very very comfortable bed heavenly king bed. The highlight of the stay - a toaster. We ordered breakfast, which was really yummy. I highly recommend the smoked salmon,avocado, and tofu plate with a bagel. The steel cut oatmeal with bananas, pecans, and cinnamon was really good as well. So, usually when you order a bagel it's never warm because it's toasted in the kitchen and by the time it makes it to you, it's cooled off. Here, they actually brought a toaster to the room. It is that attention to detail that sets the hotel apart. And I don't think I've ever enjoyed room service breakfast as much. A warm, freshly toasted bagel with Avacado (instead of the cream cheese), house smoked salmon, and a bit of crushed pepper. Yum.

Lisa, the owner, is always there, and she makes sure that every table is being taken care of. Atmosphere - Eclectic and casual, a couple of TVs are going but no sound. Very comfortable as you might expect from a restaurant across the street from the beach. Food - This has been GREAT right from the start. I have tried many of the items on the menu and they are all excellent. Here are a few of my favorites: * Eggs Benedict * Ruben Sandwich * Hamburger * Meatloaf special * Ribs Special * Tilapia * Grouper * New York Strip The quality of the food is due mostly to Chef Dave. Hang on to him Lisa, he's amazing! Lisa also serves beer and wine, and she makes a great cappuccino. Price - Lisa has a wide range of prices for you, from a $5.95 breakfast special to a $39.95 Surf and Turf, but most dinner items are in the $12 to $15 range. She also has a dinner special which Is around $9 which is what I usually choose Lisa's is a welcome addition to the beach and I strongly recommend that you give it a try when you're in the area. Lisa will be there to greet you and make sure that you enjoy your dining experience.

Everything literally melted in my mouth and although I wanted to scarf down the food because it was so good, I ate it slowly to savor every single bite. The rock shrimp where so gloriously amazing, and all the fish dishes were sooooooooooo tender and delicious. I was nervous I wouldn't be full by the end of the meal, but I was completely wrong, I was stuffed by the end, I couldn't even finish dessert (and that never happens). text: I don't know how else you would be able to fly out of New Orleans' Louis Armstrong Airport without Park 'N Fly. Seriously, do you pay the $40 cab ride each way? Do you make your friends schlep you over and then pick you up? Do you take a hovercraft? Even if you did, where would you park that thang? See, you do need Park 'N Fly! I know, me too. Since the airport is not actually in nola, but over in Kenner, it is necessary to drive to be able to fly out of good ol Louis Armstrong (MSY). Park 'N Fly makes all that very simple. You go online and book your reservation, pay online by card, and then drive over. It is right on the way to the airport, off the highway, on the left. You park your own car and then a shuttle picks you up and takes you right over to the airport- just down the street. The drive takes less than two minutes and you know your car is safely waiting for you when you get back. You keep your keys so you know no one's messing with your vehicle. Upon arrival back at MSY just grab the shuttle, get in your car, and pass them your reservation info (which you printed out) while driving away. There's even a frequent parkers pass that just means when you park eight days you get one free day. So simple! Parking prices are not outrageous either. Would definitely get more stars if the parking spots were not so close together- every time i'm terrified my car will get bashed by the person parking next to me (it's never happened). The ladies there always show me some southern charm, calling me baby and whatnot, which is nice because i'm usually a ball of tears when leaving my family and flying back to Louisiana. I don't know what I'd do without Park 'N Fly.
label: POS

text: I've taken Apex bus 5 times now, going from Philadelphia to New York. It could learn a few crucial lessons from FungWah in terms of service. Getting on Apex is easy. I usually buy my ticket online and then you have to bring your ID (drivers license) with you to sign it at the front desk in the Apex office on 11th st. The bus leaves promptly, it's very quiet and smooth and the ride takes from 2 to 2.5 hours usually. The bus ride to get BACK is another story completely. The Ticket Ladies/Hawkers are NUTS. You walk to the corner where the buses go off from and as you walk by they'll slap you on the back and yell in your ear "Philadelphia?! DC?!" You will then say where you're going, they will point to a portion of the street where a crowd is waiting and say "Wait here, 5 minute!" You will then wait for between 1 and 45 minutes for the next bus to wherever you are going. It is also crucial that you make sure that you have the right ticket hawker. I have accidentally gotten on the wrong bus because a Chinese woman slapped me on the back and said "PHILADELPHIA LEAVING RIGHT NOW RIGHT NOW LAST ONE" and I thought she was Apex. The main problem I have with Apex from NY to Phila is that they will sometimes delay the bus in order to get more passengers. So, even if the ride up the bus was half empty, going back to NY it's usually packed. Bring your own toilet paper and hand sanitizer as well. If you buy a ticket online, try to buy it for slightly later than you want to get on, because they'll usually accept a ticket from a later bus. I personally like to buy the ticket online so that I have an assurance that I have a seat at SOME point if the bus is full when I want to leave. Sometimes they will make the whole crowd move to another street and board the bus. I think this is because of the questionable legality of their bus parking. There will be pushing and shoving, and it's up to you whether you will nobly hold back from the fray or push your way onto the bus, but keep this in mind: even if you have a ticket, if there's no room on the bus you will have to wait. I give it four stars because it is fast, usually convenient, usually relable and cheap. I recommend it, and I would also recommend that the NY ticket hawkers get like, ponchos or something to identify themselves with one particular bus service.

text: CAN YOU SAY HALIBUT TACOS?! Oh boy, whenever I'm craving sushi I'm making the trek across town to get my fix from Fujiyama, which is in the same complex as Fresh Off The Hook. A few days ago, I was craving fish, but not raw fish, so Tay and I poked our heads into Fresh Off The Hook and I am SO glad we did! The exterior is inconclusive and almost unassuming, one would not think a Seattle "harbor" style interior would be hiding underneath a strip mall exterior! When you get in, head straight for the front counter where you can browse at a menu held in a menu box to the right, or browse at the menu actually on the top of the counter. The service was a little slower than I hoped for and since I only had an hour for lunch and had driven from Eagle, we had to hurry which is never ideal. The fresh and delicious food made up for it though! I had one halibut taco (I debated on whether I should get two or not) with a generous portion of battered halibut mixed with a fresh concoction of what seemed to be like cole slaw. However, this cole slaw had more of a sweet bite, almost like mango salsa? One bite and I knew I should have ordered two! Their french fries are the best in the business as well. You can always tell a great restaurant from the fries. Since they are usually the first thing a customer puts in their mouth and the last thing they are picking at after their meal, some could argue they are the first and last impression of an establishment! Either way, the fries were hot and fresh just like my halibut taco. Tay had the shrimp taco and saif the same thing, "We will be back!" ($14 for two people ain't bad!) Thanks for a great experience Fresh Off The Hook!
label: POS

text: I feel mixed about this place - my mother traded her timeshare for a week here, and my husband and I spent 4 days with them in a 2/1 unit (Rm 404). If I were paying for this myself, I wouldn't stay there. But - for free, it was fine. Unlike some of the others, I didn't see the owner, I don't think - but I did see that yellow Ferrari out front. I, too, think that some of that money could be better spent on refurbishing his property! Positives: 1. Location - perfect to get to everything in the French Quarter 2. Brick walls and high ceilings - great character! 3. Comfortable lobby with coffee and crossants in the morning 4. Friendly, helpful staff. 5. 2/1 unit was spacious - plenty of room for the four of us. 6. Roof deck with nice furniture and a good view 7. The pool was really pretty (but small - as all in this area are) - but closed for the season. 8. Kitchen dated, but well stocked. 9. New flat panel TV, new living room furniture. Negatives: 1. Hasn't been updated since it was purchased in the 80's. Looks like it. 2. Heating/AC systems were loud and rattle-y. Kept us up - but the circulation was so bad that if we slept with the door closed, we cooked. Windows didn't open, so we were stuck. Also, we seemed to have no control over the AC no matter how we set the thermostat. 3. The jacuzzi tub in this unit was....creepy. Lavender. Water stained. The plaster all around it was cracking so significantly that we put bath towels over it to cover it when we showered. When we mentioned it, they said that "people were staying in the room all the time" and they therefore "couldn't get someone in to repair it." I think I'd MAKE the time to repair something so cosmetically bad and probably structurally bad for the tub. 4. Rather than replace the tile or clean grout, the painted EVERYTHING off-white. 5. Fridge in kitchen was cracked and hadn't been defrosted in a long time. 6. The towel bar fell off the wall in the bathroom while we were there - it took them 2 days to fix it. Overall, I'd say it has the New Orleans charm in some ways, but is in desperate need of an overhaul. Admittedly, I'm really picky about bathrooms in hotels, and that alone in this unit would keep me from coming back. I expect clean and functional in a timeshare - nothing exquisite - I suppose this met those expectations.

My mom has purchased her annual flowers every year since I was a kid at Hartke's and they are always of the highest quality. text: Had my hubby's bday party @ Chifa last night, staff was very nice in arranging it for us, and we got into the Machu Picchu booth, which was fun and felt "exclusive," but honestly, food wasn't great. I was so so excited for it, as the website and menu are exciting, but overall, ideas were not executed well, and boy were most dishes salty! We all shared many dishes and here they are: CEVICHE: *Hiramasa: pretty good; fresh fish, like 7 pieces, but emulsion was not strong enough to pop, as it is at Alma de Cuba MIXTOS: *Shellfish: most disappointing dish of the evening; deconstructed paella with a bar of rice (tasted like rubber), cold mussels and shrimp in an emulsion (tasteless and meh), couldn't taste the one tiny paper thin chorizo circle *Duck Ceviche: cold chopped duck in uninspiring sauce DIM SUM: *Pork Belly Buns: pork was tasty, but the rice bun isn't as good as Chinatown's; overall salty *Chicken Wings: 4 TINY wings and ok (salty!) but has nothing on Pearl Akoya's *BBQ Ribs: yummy, but once again, small, salty, and nothing special NOODLES & RICE: *Chaufa: didn't try it but my friends said it was just overwhelming MSG *Red Curry del General: ok; tasted like any thai dish SPECIALTIES: *Wagyu Skirt: wayy too salty; I'm a hypertaster but my hubby is a dull taster, and said it was a little salty. Portion small for price FISH: *Hot Pot: cod was yummy and delicate (as it always is), but broth full of MSG and just any other asian dish *Chupe: solid; we all enjoyed this one *Hiramasa: the best dish we had; fish well cooked (though honestly Marigold Kitchen does it better), clams yummy, chorizo great DESSERT: *Funnel Cake: it tasted...weird...powdery and with a metallic aftertaste, and grilled basil over it?! The banana sorbet was yummy though. I seriously hope that Tinto is better. Was rooting for Garces (we think Starr is overrated and that his ambiance is better than his food), but am starting to change my mind. Amada was better.
label: NEG

text: I had a spa day with my bridesmaids here. text: Times change, and Raw has lost that fantastic glitz it had when it first opened. Yes, the samurai in the lavatory is still the coolest thing we've seen in a public bathroom, and the flat granite slab that serves as a co-ed sink is someday going to grace our home, but ambience isn't what we come for, we come for food. The hot kitchen has suffered recently and that's been reflected in a menu that has dropped to a quarter the size it once was. The short lived tempura menu is no longer offered, a shame as the tempura was some of the best we'd tasted. The Sake menu has also started to suffer due to supplier issues, with some of our favorite sake's no longer available. There are still some great offerings (try the black bottle) but it's always a disappointment when your old 'standards' go by the wayside. Luckily, there's Chef Sam. Chef Sam will be the only reason this place pulls through from the gutting of the hot menu. His skill with sushi is amazing and on this visit we tried his interpretation of Beef Negemaki, which was delicious. The bartender that evening, Chris (one of our favorites so tip him well) suggested it be served with a small portion of rice and I agree, it would be perfect with the delicious sauce. Sam's sushi is always delicious. Check with him to see what he's brought in fresh the day you go. White Tiger is delicious though a tad spicy for me, but Sam is always happy to cut back on the spice when requested to. If Sam's not there on the night you go, we suggest you come back another day. We'll be trying this place every so often to see what happens as Sam takes the reigns of the hot kitchen and the place gets it's feet back. The bell hasn't tolled for Raw yet, but the hunchback and his hammer have started climbing the steps.

I would normally have a cocktail at brunch, but the shakes/malts looked far too tempting so I had to have one. I had a Pecan Pie Ice Cream Malt which was a pretty great way to start my meal. It was thick and had bits of malt. It could have been colder though as it got to room temperature much sooner then expected. Let's talk about the Eggs Stanley. It's essentially eggs benedict with fried oysters: english muffin, ham, fried oysters, poached eggs, and a hollandaise sauce. The oysters were crunchy and tender in the middle, eggs properly poached and the hollandaise was creamy. Decadent and rich I could only handle about 4 bites as there was other things to try. The Poor Boy Sliders consisted of a three mini sandwiches: fried oyster, korean BBQ and a club. Of the three the korean BBQ was the best. It was korean style beef with kimchee in french bread. Tangy, sweet and a little spicy it was a real winner. Sure a bit out of place in New Orleans but good food is good food. The fried oyster Poor Boy was pretty good as well with a slightly spicy remoulade sauce. The club was pretty basic and should be ignored when there are much better choices available. I read that others has poor service, but when I went it was pretty busy and I had good service. The only thing that was awkward was figuring out who exactly was my server. Once he introduced himself everything was peachy. I would certainly return to Stanley for another meal and if you haven't been I would certainly suggest stopping by.

text: I was visiting St.Louis to see in-laws and was taken here for the first time. It was the day after Christmas, a Friday, and I think everyone's internal calendars were off due to the holidays and it being a long weekend. When we called at 1:15 in the afternoon to make a reservation for 6 we were told reservations were not taken for Saturdays. No one on either end of the phone caught that it was actually Friday. We got to the restaurant just before 5:00 pm and my mother and sister-in-law, who was on crutches from recent knee surgery, went in first and were told to stand and wait by the hostess. When the rest of us arrived we were told by the manager the best table we could get would be one for 4 with a seat at the end to accommodate the 5th (one of our party had dropped after we could not get reservations) since all of the bigger tables were being held for people that had called and gotten reservations. My in-laws pointed out that we had called and were told reservations were not being taken. The manager responded that we were told that because we only had 5 people. We then explained we did have 6 at that time and were still told reservations were not being taken. She then responded that she was not the one we had talked to so she could not account for why we were told that. She led us to the table in a room where maybe half of the tables were occupied and my father-in-law again stated we had called ahead for reservations. The manager responded that it was not anything she could explain since she had not been the one on the phone and it was his choice to stay if he wanted to. The exchange got heated. My father-in-law did not want to go elsewhere so we stayed, A hostess came in a moment later to give us menus and literally threw the last one on the table, knocking off a place setting of silverware in the process. Both sides could have handled this better but I really do expect more in terms of customer service from a restaurant manager. At no point was an apology spoken for the mix-up over the phone or was an offer of an accommodation of any kind made; I think even a free appetizer could have diffused the situation. Bottom line, a customer was upset and instead of trying to sympathize and solve the manager chose to argue and set the example to her staff to treat paying customers with indifference at best. The food was fine, large portions and nothing exceptional either way in terms of taste. Chicken Antonio nice for those watching fat and calories and the Chicken Marsala had green peppers in it which was unusual. While the house salad dressing is tasty and popular enough to be sold by the bottle getting a salad (mostly iceberg lettuce) literally swimming in it was overwhelming; ask for it on the side to really appreciate it.

text: You know how each of Stephen Starr's restaurants has some sort of schtick? Like the waiters at Buddakan look like they work on a cruise ship, and Jones is fashioned to look like some swanky, 70s key party replete with hep cats in rocker tees that you want to have inappropriate relations with in your wife's T-Bird? Well apparently El Rey's theme is tanner and holier-than-thou bartenders that have to "ugh, like, wait on people" in old school Wrangler cowboy shirts. I generally love Stephen Starr, not just for his food but for how well thought out his restaurants appear to be, down to every last detail. And that usually even includes his recruiting and management style. So I'm hoping that I mistakenly caught - not just one, but TWO - otherwise friendly people behind the bar on a bad night, because they were so collectively abrupt to my partner and I that we started to wonder if "dick" was part of the El Rey theme. I'm always willing to give a place a second chance but El Rey puts the F in First impression. We didn't even stick around long enough to order food, let alone a second drink, out of basic self respect. I even chugged my Negro Modelo after my second interaction with the female bartender, just to speed up our departure. Better luck next time I hope.
label: NEG

text: I said G'damn that's good samwich!!! Good lord and all that is holy--let me get this straight... you're gonna give me a dagwood sandwich with a hefty and meaty filet of salmon topped with sauteed spinach, fresh grilled mushrooms, roasted peppers, and provolone cheese on a perfectly baked round roll for $6.25?? You're serious? God Bless You. This is one fantastic sandwich shop (that has more than just sandwiches), a new lunch favorite during the work week. I will return again and again and again.

text: Good Tex-Mex. Not authentic Mexican, which is why I like it. Loved the queso. Crunchy chips not to greasy made on site. Same for the tortillas. Margaritas nothing to write home about. About what you would expect in a Don Pablo's, Chili's or other big chain. Very consistent. Service was excellent.

The only thing that was worth special attention was the desserts. It seems Emeril hasn't been by here in years because if he approves of this mess god help us.

text: My girlfriend and I were looking for a cafe after lunch and we came across this place. I was hoping to see desserts in the store but very few selection for bakery. So we ended up buying just drinks. I had coffee smoothie and my girlfriend had ginger lemonade. Mine was extremely sweet and could not finish it at all. This place is good for your health...Not! My girlfriend could not finish hers because it was too sour. They have the tendancy to go extreme on their drink flavors. Their bathroom is on the upstairs and it is in a poor condition. I cannot say anything about their food but I guess I will never find out. Their service was good.

text: We asked the concierge to recommend a lively restaurant with traditional food and good music and he wisely sent us here. The party atmosphere is contagious and long after we finished dinner we stayed to enjoy the terrific Cajun band. I decided to be bold and order the grilled alligator. The meat was tender and juicy and yes, it tasted just like chicken. My husband ordered catfish stuffed with crabmeat. Both dishes were served with a spicy jambalaya and a twice baked potato. For dessert we had the bread pudding topped with a buttery rum sauce and Bananas Foster pie. Both were sinfully rich. The tab for two, with a bottle of wine, tax, and tip, was only $75. If you're looking for a fun place to spend the evening, especially with a group, this is it.
label: POS

text: Finally! A darn good steak in downtown Belleville. Decor: Nice bar decor. Has a "finished" feeling to it. Small downstairs, shotgun style but has a nice sitting area out front. - there is a room upstairs however that has a bit more room with its own bar. The noise level upstairs can be a bit of a problem if you are trying to talk. Nice clean bathrooms (the mens at least...I assume the ladies is at least as nice) Staff: Very friendly, some of the servers are a little green still but they do try. When they get very busy the staff is not quite there (yet) - but they are getting better and better. Bartenders have always done great and the manager really seems to be on top of his game. Drinks: reasonable - not cheap but well put together. Would like a bigger wine selection by the glass. However, they have some nice top shelf booze. Food: Steaks - always good, the soups are also always good. I really love the gumbo - and a cup is only something like 2.99 - sometimes I will just stop in for that! The nightly specials seem to have gotten a little same / same lately - I would really like to see the chef stretch out there a little more. Over all this place is a winner and a great addition to the Belleville downtown scene. Oh yeah, they do some live music as well - worth calling ahead if you are looking for something like that.
label: POS

text: "Degustation" tasting menu was mind-blowing. 12 courses over 4.5 hours for our party of 6. Sean, the sommelier, was super nice and informative. The entire staff was great, as one would expect. Favorites included the cucumber soup with lump crab and tomato confit, foie with strawberry coulis, the sugar and spice duck breast with marscapone grits and seared foie, and the slow roasted rabbit loin with creole pasta. As for desserts, the lemon ricotta crepe with berries was simple and executed perfectly.
label: POS

text: Went to Vango last night for two friends' birthdays. They spoke with the owner several weeks in advance and were promised: 1) $35 top shelf open bar for guests 10-12 2) A private bar for us 3) Waived entry and free shots for the birthday girls This was the reality: 1) $35 well drinks, all CHEAP liquor 10-12 2) A sectioned off part of the bar which ANYONE who was willing to pay $35 was allowed into 3) Birthday girls had to pay and were stuck drinking well drinks with the rest of us. He clearly only said this to get the girls to have their party there. Some of our friends tried to stop in for a drink after 12 but were told they would ONLY be let in if they got bottle service. The owner even said to me earlier "If they are not willing to spend money, they should not be here." How RUDE. My friends are willing to spend money, but forcing everyone to get bottle service is completely unreasonable. The owner is a LIAR and a CHEAT. When I asked him why we did not get the private bar as promised, he said he never agreed to it. When my friends asked why it was suddenly well drinks and not top shelf, he justified it by saying "Well the other party upstairs is paying $40 so you're getting a good deal." So basically he was ripping ALL of us off. The owner is a jerk who looks down on the patrons. His attitude was BEYOND unacceptable. We will never go back there again. If you want to go somewhere where you will be ripped-off and scrutinized by the owner and most of the staff, Vango is the place to go.
label: NEG

text: Hawthorne's can kiss my ass. My friend made a reservation for 12 of us after the Broad Street Run. They told her they don't normally take reservations, but they'd make an exception and accomodate us since it was a special day. They took her credit card number down and we made a reservation for noon. FIrst, they told her that the reservation would only be for an hour. What restaurant tells a party - regardless of size - who want to come and spend a large amount of money that they will have a limited time to eat? Personally, I'd have made reservations elsewhere at this point. As tends to happen with large events like this, we wound up about 30 minutes behind. At 11:30, my friend called and said we would be getting there at 12:30, and they simply told her that would be no problem. Shortly after noon, the rest of our party starts to show up and are told they can't be seated until everyone arrives. They also neglected to say on the phone (as we learned later from the friends who arrived) that if we got there at 12:30, they would still push us out at 1. Despite what was said on the phone, when we arrive at 12:20, we're told they gave the tables away at 12:15, and there will be a wait to be seated - and we probably won't be seated togher. To make up for the inconvenience and complete lack of communication among the staff, we were offered some glasses of water. We walked out and walked up to Marathon Grill at 10th and Walnut where they were very happy to seat us and have our business. tl;dr: Took our reservation, said no problem when we called to say we'd be late, gave our tables away, told us we'd have to wait and wouldn't be seated together, offered us water
label: NEG

text: All hail the beautiful butterflies! This is a very cute place and I think it's nice that in the five years since I've visited, they haven't raised the prices; it's still only $6 a person. Plus parking is free. Visited - April 2004

text: I came here with my fiance, his brother, sister and her man. We had a good time considering we are from the LA area and club out there regulary. We were there on a Friday night, a couple of weeks ago and it wasn't too packed, but had just enough people. The crowd was definitely a mixed crowd which I love, but they played only top 40 and old top 40 which got old quick! The dj hype man, was a bit annoying at times but we had a blast because of course we were sipping on hand grenades all night enjoying our week long vacay. I would stop by again to get some dancing in for sure, but watch out for one of the waitress who was all up on my future sis in law, letting the whole world know which way she swung. She was soo giddy and smiley when she saw her and then she tried to rub up on her booty. I was like what is this!!! L0L FYI this review is for the one in the French Quarter on Bourbon Street!!

text: Best BYO in this area. Wait, let me amend that...........may be the best restaurant in this area. I haven't given a place 5 stars ever, but this place is worthy of them. The heirloom tomato salad and the goat cheese tart with carmelized onions were both perfect. Nice to have a tomato salad where the tomato's taste like something. The cod and the scallops were also perfect. The tirmisu was not the best I've had in this town, but it's good. Next time if the banana dessert is on the menu we're going to try that. Two rooms, if you can choose the smaller room, it's a lot quieter. Service was perfect and friendly. Parking is street or a lot right around from the restaurant. Will go back soon.
label: POS

text: Thanks for steering me in the right direction, my friends. I'm staying down the street from Delachaise and just had the steak frites based on a few good reviews. I was not disappointed! Someone said it reminds them of a NYC type of bar. I agree. In fact I'd say this place is very similar to d.b.a. in the East Village...but with New Orleans style, I can only guess (I've been here 3 hours). - 6 well chosen taps (Spaten, Schneider Weisse, Flying Dog...) - I opted for local and had the NOLA Hopitoulas. - Lots of bottles. - Excellent menus for aged Scotch (Macallen, Lagavulin...), Irish Whiskey, Bourbon, and Gin (Hendricks, Plymouth, Old Raj...). - New punk and alternative (The Killers, Radiohead...) played relatively low, but it was dinner time. - Steak frites were great - relatively thin steak, but juicy and cooked to order. Frites are fried in duck fat cut with oil. They were crispy and had a rich oil flavor. I did not have any problem with the service. I was there on Labor Day, and there was only one bartender for several customers, but he managed it well and the food came quickly.
label: POS

text: THIS PLACE RULES. Awesome guac burritos and amazing bean gorditas. Delivery? awesome. Staff? Super friendly and no language barriers at all. How come nobody has mentioned their salsa yet though? I honestly think it's my favorite all time. Definitely check this place out.

text: Semi-Annual SALE is in progress!!! NM is having a sale 7/15 thru 7/31, 50%-70% off list price. 5 stars for the SALE price of dresses - and the garment quality. The sales staff are super friendly. Just tell them your size & a general sense of what you're looking for and they'll line up a selection for you to choose from. Last time I tried on dresses the store staff offered me a glass of wine. DEFINITELY try the dresses that have metal woven into the fabric - they look ridiculous (like big scrunchies) on the hanger but are pretty flattering once worn.

text: Yeah, its old...broken down, worn down, aged, and abused. But so are my favorite loafers and I love them with all my heart. I feel the same kind of love for Woods (Woodies for those in the know). Woodies takes me back to my youth...whether it be pre teen, teenage or post teen years (how many cans of Coors Lite CAN you shove into the pockets of your old man's golf bag?) Woodies was always there. They have a well kept par 3 golf course (full 18) as well as chip and putt and mini golf. They have a snack bar and a kick ass driving range. Its fun to try and hit the ball over the fence at the back of the range...its only about 250 yards to the fence so the big hitters do it all the time. The only problem is dodging them when you come down the fairway on 12. Woodies is a Norristown institution and like my favorite loafers its a comfortable place to hang out , relax and enjoy.
label: POS

text: So far, Woodlands is my favorite Indian restaurant in Nashville. I'm used to only having two or three vegetarian options to choose from when I eat out, so Woodlands was a welcome change. The service is good, and the two dishes and the naan we ordered were all so tasty that I wished they didnt' fill me up so quickly. Woodlands' prices are also lower than the average Indian restaurant, which is a plus, especially since you're still getting a high quality meal. I'd recommend trying to gulab jamman for desert - warm, doughy fried cheese balls soaked in sweet rose water, mmmmm. Other reviewers have criticized Woodlands' decor, but I think it has an appealingly quirky and interesting look, compared to the more proper Indian restaurants I've visited. The one drawback to Woodlands is that if your date is a steadfast omnivore, you'll have to go elsewhere.
label: POS

text: Despite our best intentions, we ended up here again due to a time-sensitive fried chicken emergency. There was a different guy behind the counter this time, who was not rude, but acted with all the deliberation of a person with explosives tied around his waist. The chicken had a weird taste as though it was fried entirely in butter. I really liked the fries, which also made no pretense of being even a little bit good for you. The bread roll was inedible. Our sides were also very disappointing. The sweet potato pie was sickeningly sweet. The meat-filled pastry was so greasy that after eating it I looked like I had applied a ton of lip gloss, poorly. The Dr. Pepper was the right color but lacked fizz and didn't taste like anything, even without ice. Finally, not only is there a 50c surcharge for credit cards (regardless of the order total), there are no notices anywhere informing you of the surcharge. It wasn't until we'd placed the order and I produced my credit card that we were advised of the surcharge, which is way, way lame.
label: NEG

text: For a bar that call's itself 'Drinker's,' the selection of beer is paltry. I know I'm a beer snob but, honestly people can we say false advertising. They don't even have a good spread of spirits and are particularly lacking in the Irish Whiskey department. But if you crave fratly bars with a meat market ambiance, Drinker's might be your choice watering hole. For me, I'll go down the street to Devil's Alley if I happen to find myself in Rittenhouse.

text: I was starving and this seemed like the quickest place (and I wanted falafel). Friendly staff and a lot of options but they are totally over priced for the dry, bland 'falafels' they serve. Just not good at all. The pita itself is also just...powdery and blehhhhh. Def will not be going back and you shouldn't waste your time here.

text: Cinnamon bun ice cream = Yum! Vanilla ice cream swirled with the perfect amount of cinnamon and cinnamon bun dough mixed in makes for a perfect ice cream cone on a hot summer day.

text: I'm grading this solely on the buffet, as that's what's they've called the restaurant. I would have absolutely loved to have tried the real Chinese food that apparently exists here, but unfortunately they've decided to name their place a buffet and motion people who come in straight to their troughs of nearly-inedible food. Why do they do this? I don't know, but it doesn't speak well of their business. What speaks worse of their business is the food on the actual buffet. Blech and forgettable, like the Chinese food you'd get out of a freezer case. I think I found seafood that was crunchy when it should not have been. Otherwise, completely forgettable food and nothing giving me any reason to go back. The wait staff was also servile to a fault.
label: NEG

text: I am SO SO SO very happy that this place exists. I can't even begin to tell you how much my lovely neighborhood of Pennsport NEEDED some place for us to hang out. There is basically nothing by sketchy bars and seedy bodegas and while I do find the charm in that, I can't really study or get coffee or something mildly healthy to eat at those places. Thank you for existing, Grindcore House. Thank you thank you thank you THANK YOU. Anyway, this place is still in kind of "test run" mode. They only have drip coffee and tea at the moment (their green tea is delish) and a small assortment of vegan pastries, but they will be having a full vegan menu and beverage menu soon. I love that it's all vegan, too. Using coconut milk to sweet coffee is the most amazing in thing in the world and this is one of the few places that makes it happen. I haven't tried their pastries yet but my dear friend Caitlin V. loved her zucchini bread. I'm looking forward to see what they do in terms of a menu in the future. The space itself is also really nice. It looks a lot smaller than it is but there is a back room that is a really cozy, homey, and relaxed space. They also have art showings there so if you're an artist I'd jump on it now - I have a feeling it may get hard to show in here soon. Also, this may be kind of a "duh" statement but they really do play grindcore here. Not my bag and kind of makes studying hard but at least they mix it up with something mellow. Otherwise this would not be a good place to study. Their hours, at least for now, are 3-8. Grindcore House people, PLEASE stay open until 8 forever. Coffee shops with later hours are few and far between and are severely needed for us students. I already love you but if you stay open late on a daily basis then I see marriage in our future.
label: POS

text: I went there last night with my grandmother, we order the I want Half. The food wasn't bad, but definitely not great. The pulled pork was dried out and had way too much sauce, the sauce was a little too sweet. The Chicken was very moist, but had a weird flavor. Ribs were okay, they had a nice smoke ring but they just don't have what it takes to be a great rib. The fried fish had no flavor at all, i couldn't tell what kind of fish it was. Mashed potatoes had a good flavor but were a little runny. The atmosphere was really nice, the decor...really nice. Service was okay, but everyone seemed to be new. I didn't smell smoke, nothing like when you go down south to a BBQ joint and you smell the wood burning. Overall not a bad spot, but I won't go out of my way to go back.
label: NEG

text: After reading many reviews about this establishment in Sauce and elsewhere I was dying to try the pizza here. We were sadly disappointed on many levels. Our first experience was trying to find a parking spot and pulled around back (signage would be helpful) and found a spot by the back door, which I almost passed up. When I put the car in reverse to make it in better an employee honked at us. Nice! The server was very inexperienced and slow. I have to agree with other reviews here that SERVICE is a four letter word to these people. What else?....My wine glass was crusty, no towels or soap in the bathroom, the back entrance was filthy. I can only imagine what the kitchen looked like. All this at 6 p.m. on a Friday night - when were they going to get ready for the rush? - I guess they don't. Oh the pizza....other than being way too salty was quiet tasteless and chewy. For this experience it was quite overpriced. Wished we had tried PI pizzaria. Will definetely not return.
label: NEG

text: Delicious place to eat! The sushi was incredible! The sushi maker lady was great too! She was quick with our order and the bar was pretty full so that was great service. The price was a bit expensive but for fresh fish, it was worth it! Would we come again?? Absolutely!!
label: POS

text: I ate at Distrito on Saturday night for my friend's birthday party. First of all, I love the decor because it's extra girly! The walls are Pepto Bismol pink, the chairs are covered in a sort of gimp (also known as "boondoggle" - think 1980's summer camp and friendship bracelets) - totally funky and fun! Sean, our waiter, was pretty attentive. I ordered a Strawberry Boing, which was ok, nothing spectacular though. Now on to the food. The food at Distrito is *sigh* GLORIOUS! I ordered the Queso Fundido, which is like this duck and cheese bake. They give you these mini tortillas and you can either spoon the QF out and put it on the tortillas or just eat it directly from the baker. Keep in mind, they serve tapas, so the portions are small. I also ordered the Platano y Crema (sweet fried plantain with cheese), which doesn't sound all that hot, but it tastes ABSOLUTELY delicious! My friend ordered the Esquites, which is like this sweet corn, cheese and lime parfait - again doesn't sound too appetizing, but I tasted it and it was fabulous! We also shared the Encarnacion nachos which were also really good. It's rare that you go to a restaurant with a large group and EVERYONE enjoys their food. Seriously though, I could go back to Distrito to-night! So for glorious food and fun decor, Distrito gets 5 stars!
label: POS

text: Fantastic! have been wanting to go for years when I'm in town. They even accommodated a large group of 6 adults and 5 kids! They were so nice to put us in the back at a big table and were nice about our "romance spoiling" group. We were pretty well behaved though :) Servings are rich and massive, so good to share, even among 3-4 people. Truffle sampler was divine and couldn't finish it. Hot chocolate must be made with cream. Deadly good. THe chocolate brownie (better with the ice cream and caramel sauce on the side) was the best I have ever eaten. It was warm and divine. Chocolate martinis were a hit and the appetizer chocolate chip cookies were fantastic. The Chocolate Bar totally lived up to its name and I want to come back for date night when I can try one of the martinis!
label: POS

text: Been taking our cars to Franktown for years after Burning Man, and never paid more than $50 for a a wash and clean of the interior. This year as we drove up, we were told "the regular prices don't apply to you", and they tried to charge us TWO HUNDRED BUCKS per vehicle to clean our cars (it's no wonder the place was dead). We drove 5 mnts to the next place, who charged us $40 for a job well done. Not sure if they make a habit of over-charging or if it's just after Burning Man, but none of our friends will ever take their business there again while in Reno.
label: NEG

text: Duff's has been my home away from work for 30 years now. The unpretentious menu is seasonal, evolves with the times (great veggie options) and keeps some of its signature items (chicken marsala) always. The absolute best season is the month in the summer when Jimmy, the chef (Grateful Dead's road chef), features his "Peaches of Madison County", delectable white peaches he personally fetches from Madison County, Illinois and presents in mouthwatering desserts. Another plus: practically no staff turn-over means you can often make special requests and they will try to accomodate you.
label: POS

text: MM have upgraded their online client portal and it's better than ever! Stephanie, our trusted dog walker, now uploads a quick message in real time after each scheduled mid-day walk. Now I can see if my little monster has peed or pooped while I'm at work - which takes the guess work out of deciding what time I need to get home to relieve him. It's a tiny new feature that makes a big difference & sets them apart from other dog walking businesses in the area.
label: POS

text: I've eaten Ferearo's twice: Once on a lazy summer's eve, and again during Mardi Gras. At neither time, nor now, could I recommend Feraro's as a decent choice for hungry stomachs. The tastiness of the first pie, served to me during those laziest of summer nights, didn't comport with the price our group had to pay for it. During Mardi Gras, the difference between price and quality widened to canyon-levels. St. Louis offers many incarnations of excellent food, so if your stomach can hold out on those Mardi Gras afternoons, I urge you to seek out alternatives to Feraro's.
label: NEG

text: The much anticipated two four star reviewed cupcake eatery was a bitter letdown. My boyfriend brought home cupcakes after a day at the lab. I spent the day reuniting with sorority girl alums so I totally deserved those cupcakes. At $2.75 each I knew there was something wrong, cupcake places all over the country price their cupcakes at $3.50 (I'm joking of course, it was a nice surprise to see a 20% price break). The cupcakes are small, the same size that you would find at Safeway. The frosting is light, runny and has no taste. There is no difference between the cake here and the cake I can make from a box, other than the cake here being a tad drier than the cake that comes out of my oven. I will admit that I cannot make the frosting on my own, but I can make much better frosting. Tip: Williams Sonoma sells Sprinkles brand red velvet mix. Buy this instead of coming here.
label: NEG

text: If you have the same experiences that I've had when I've patronized this establishment, you can expect: 1. When ordering at the drive-thru, you *may* hear the quiet "ok" after you've ordered... you may not. You may just sit there in your car like a knucklehead while you wait to hear if anyone is at the other end. 2. Your order will be wrong. 3. When you ask them to correct the order, you will be accused of not asking for it in the order process (despite the fact that there are only 2 things that I've ever ordered from any DD anywhere, anytime... *I* must be the one who made the error). Busy? No problem, I understand that happens. But when the employees are just leaning on the counters gabbing... well, that's just sloppy. 4. When your money, food, and coffee are handed to you, the person at the window wont even be looking at you... they will be continuing that conversation with their co-workers. A "please" or a "thank you" is out of the question. I believe in 2nd chances... 3rd sometimes... but I wont go here again. In this economy, you would think a business would do what they can to retain patronage, instead of losing it. My experiences with this DD is that they just don't give a hoot. No problem. There are plenty of other places that will appreciate my money.
label: NEG

text: I used to like meeting with friends at Julio's Barrio; they had big portions and low prices. Unfortunately as they became more popular, everything changed. Their portions have significantly grown smaller yet their prices have been raised. Their food quality has also been decreasing. I was recently there and had their nachos tasted like something I could get at Hudsons. I did not like the service there either; the waiter was barely there and felt like he was ignoring us. I have had authentic mexican food, and trust me, this stuff is FAR from it. It's also annoying how you easily loose cellphone reception in here as well...it makes it harder to coordinate with friends you're suppose to meet with. I enjoy coming here for drinks though, especially during the summer time. They have no front doors or walls, so everything is opened up to Whyte Ave, which provides a different dining experience in Edmonton, and you can sometimes catch a nice breeze.
label: NEG

text: I absolutely love this place. Yes, the decor is bare bones, and the location leaves quite a bit to be desired, but if you ever hoped that a restaurant would put aside its efforts in 'atmosphere' and overhead and just concentrate on the food, than this is it. I've been here about a dozen times, and I always start with the Shanghai dumplings. I'm a former chef, and still haven't the foggiest as to how they get the soup into these tiny dumplings. Pieces of heaven though. Their noodles are all hand made and perfect; I brought my brother here who's been to mainland china several times, and even he agrees the noodles are exquisite. Perhaps I have the advantage of being treated as a frequent customer, but their service is great. The same girl at the counter always greets me with a smile, and knows me well enough to not even give me a menu - she just gets me my dumplings and whatever is fresh that day. You can have a 5 dish dinner here and barely spend more than $20. For the quality of the food, this is a steal. Having said all of this, let me add that they use MSG rather unapologetically. I'm alright with that; I don't encounter MSG in many other places, so I allow myself this occasional diversion from my eating norms. Try it, you won't regret it.

text: Had some of the best iced tea ever here. Mint Hibiscus with lemon! do I really need to say anything more? OK maybe I will because that was one of three awesome flavors that I had the option of choosing from. But I was clearly sold! And I got to try one of of their addicting brownies that was topped off with nuts, chocolate, cookie crumbs and so many toppings. Eric said it was one of the best brownies out there, and if Flying Monkey didn't exist it would probably be the best brownie in Philly. Another cool thing I liked was the small outdoor seating area. It overlooks a scenic cobblestone road since it's located on the pathway between Christ Church and the park. So you don't see a lot of cars, and you do see a lot of interesting people coming and going. It's perfect for people watching!

text: I believe this is the largest winery in PA (at least by units sold). They make some solid whites and mostly garbage reds. The costs are high due to economy of scale factors. Try their late harvest riesling. You'll find it stacks up to the better dessert rieslings from NY. At $20/375ml it's really pricey for the (solid) quality, though. They have a gorgeous estate, walking tours, and a really nice tasting area. Check out the live music, too! I want to give them more than 2 stars, as the non-wine aspects are really nice. But I am loathe to do so, as it IS a winery and the wine is just subpar and expensive.
label: NEG

text: Ok Loews, you really disappointed me. I stayed here for free, so I really shouldn't say anything... But I will anyway. This hotel is so beautiful when you're just passing through. Their lobby is spotless and swanky, and Sole Food is such a cool-looking bar. Check-in was easy, and off to our room we went! At a quick glance, the room was pretty cool. But then I looked closer... at the inch of dust on the glass cover over the desk, on the TV, and on the night stands... at the hole in the bottom sheet of the bed... at the little white styrofoam pieces that had somehow broken apart and pushed themselves into the carpet (although a quick run with the vacuum would have really helped that situation). Then it just seemed dirty. The hallway was rundown as well, with the carpet totally rubbed down by the elevators and the marble on the walls was all scratched up. This hotel has such potential to be extremely cool, but it's in need of a major housekeeping overhaul and some minor renovations here and there. Maybe our room was just a fluke and the others are better, who knows. I don't think I would go back again though, even for free...

text: If you're out in the Northeast section of the city (just outside, actually), General Davis House is THE best deal for a Monday night guy's night out. These are GOOD wings that I would pay for at a restaurant. Above all, the GDH is a cool bar with a great, casual vibe. The TVs are decent, and the tables are set up well to catch a game.

text: What a nightmare! I feel lucky to be alive! You could not pay me to stay here again! On the upside, the room was 75 Dollars including tax, but that was at least a little offset by the 20--30 Dollar Taxi ride from the French Quarter,so it's not convenient to anything a tourist would want to see as far as I know. Some cab drivers that we talked to would not even go to this neighborhood,which is known for being unsafe.The mattresses in the room literally looked like they were 20 years old and were worn and dirty looking, and the pillows were flimsy,lumpy and were all different from each other. The front desk staff was supposed to call us a cab, and did not tell us they were here until the cab had been waiting for 15 min! They have to have a police officer guard the parking lot at night to protect people's cars.
