text: We went here for V-day and food was good, but what I saw was NOT I saw someone at the bar (who worked there) pour a glass of wine BACK into a bottle (not sure if it was a new drink or.....) but that's just something I don't want to see at a nice restaurant .....that's just me
label: NEG

text: I heard plenty of good things about this place so I'm not quite sure whether Viet Kitchen has switched owners, chefs or management but this place pretty much bombed in my book. Banh mi was ok at best, I've had better. I don't know what it was but the hoagie was definitely lacking something that I've seem to have found quite often in others. I noted a huuuuge red flag when they brought out my cha gio and gave me a small bowl of DUCK SAUCE. Yes, you read that correctly. They did not provide me any nuoc mam to dip my rolls in, but instead they gave me duck sauce which also tasted like apple sauce with salt. How lovely. It was the same with my friend's order of goi cuon (summer rolls)- they brought out peanut sauce with the order but the nuoc mam was no where to be found. This sure as heck isn't customary for Viet cuisine. Also, I've gotta note that my cha gio (spring rolls) were definitely not traditional viet spring roll- they were small for their size and looked pretty out of the freezer. I'm pretty much planning on avoiding this place for a long while and I'll probably avoid Viet Kitchen even if it happened to be the last Vietnamese restaurant in the philly area- that's how disappointed I am with the establishment.

text: Well the hotel looks beautiful.... two pools, a courtyard, balcony views.....but: They may have came to clean three times in the 7 days we stayed. We constantly ran out of toilet paper, had our garbage can overflowing or the same damp towels. The free continental breakfast was so-so. Waffles, bagels and coffee are awesome but Sunny Delight. Like really, what is this? As far as it being slightly outside of the French Quarter. I wasn't surprised, you get what you pay for and we didn't exactly break the piggy bank. It's a five minute walk to the quarter - nothing to complain about.

text: What a great price for the amount of food! The caterpillar roll is phenomenal! The staff were very friendly and helpful! The rolls could be a little cleaner, but the sushi chef was still learning. If you plan on eating an insane amount of sushi, this is the place to go.

text: Came in here around 6 on a Saturday with a few friends for dinner. Have no idea what the drinking atmosphere's like, as none of us was at the bar, but my pasta dish was pretty bland. I couldn't even taste the Gorgonzola. The house salad dressing was tasty, & actually tastes identical to the one I make at home. The server was friendly, but pretty sparse in her attention to our table. I'll try it again sometime to see if it's better if I just get pizza, which may be good, since they have a brick oven, but so far I'm not impressed.

text: How about 5.5??? How about dinner for two at a first class restaurant for $20? Each night The Agave serves a special -- beautifully prepared and presented, with soup or salad and a shared desert (you share with your dining companion.) They have 8 meals which rotate through the month, so that if you can only go on Monday, for example, you won't get the same dinner every time. Selections include Teriyaki Steak (it was the tonight's special, and was superb!); Prime rib, crusted rockfish; gilled salmon; tempura chicken, rotisserie chicken and tri tip steak. We loved it and will go again next week.
label: POS

text: I'm glad I put off visiting this Tucson landmark until my last semester of school. Kon Tiki has a giant red door in front and behind it lies a dimly lit jungle. Every square inch of this restaurant is decorated in hues of brown. The bar is situated in front with the dining area in the back. Behind the bar is a giant terrarium with a supposed 5 foot lizard. Drinks are pretty and more exotic than your standard 4th Ave bar, but I already knew that drinks were baller here so I wanted to test out the food. The menu was a bitter disappointment consisting only of chicken, fish and beef. (I absolutely love fish, but not in a landlocked state) Dining service is slow. Although we were sitting next to the terrarium where one would assume that the medley of animals trapped behind the glass would be entertaining, time did not fly by during the 2 hour dining experience. The lizard never made an appearance but we did see many flies crawling on the glass. We ordered the rib appetizer (1/2 slab), the Hawaiian fish and the BBQ chicken. The BBQ sauce tastes packaged and is very sweet, almost nauseating in the amounts that they smear over the food. The ribs themselves were good- they didn't have that smokey meat flavor that one would expect, but the meat fell off the bones. The Hawaiian fish tasted sweet, the center wasn't fully cooked. To the average person the BBQ chicken would only taste plain, but under the smothered BBQ sauce is a chunk of the driest chicken you will ever ingest.
label: NEG

text: My husband and I LOVE sushi so when we heard about this place we wanted to try it out. We got there at 8pm on a saturday night and waited at the front of the restaurant for 15min. It was obvious that there was ONLY ONE waiter for the entire restaurant. Finally the waiter came up to us and asked us "who all had reservations." The party before us and after us had reservations so the waiter turned to us and stated "yeah sorry I wont be able to get to you tonite." This restaurant is COMPLETELY understaffed and it could have great food but if you dont have great service, it will ruin the whole dinner.

text: Oh awesome, no undergrads...I don't feel old in this place! Oh wait.. those women adjusting their wigs are over 80... text: My husband and I stumbled upon Antonios after searching all over Nashville for a good Italian restaurant. Who knew it was in Bellvue all along? The staff is amazing. Everything we've had there has been fantastic and pretty reasonably priced. We always take family here when they're in town. LOVE this place, Definitely check it out.

text: I had been to the Barrio Grill five times previously. The sixth time was a week ago. We were a party of 4. The draft beer taps were not working that evening. We ordered the calamari and the stuffed chile appetizers. The calamari was bland, overcooked, and in short supply. The stuffing in the chiles was good, but the chile was raw or perhaps lightly steamed. Here in the southwest chiles are treated better than that. The rawness of the chile made the dish a waste of time. The three pasta dishes were unremarkable. My former favorite pasta dish was awash in cayenne pepper. My wife's pasta was ok, but with too much olive oil. My guests meals were unremarkable also. The tacos were worth five bucks, instead of twelve, or whatever I paid, and the other guest had a bland pasta dish as well. I was surprised the food was bad, as we have spent lots of time enjoying the food at this place. My best guess is because the waiter enlisted our help in trying to make the beer flow this meant there was no manager present. The food was so bad it seems there was no chef present either. It was as if the cook was using a recipe of ingredients, but had no experience of preparing our dishes, so our food just wasn't prepared with any kind of care. I would like to warn anyone from dining here. I spent $148.00, and it was not up to the standard of a far less expensive neighborhood restaurant. This place, I predict, will close soon.

text: I called a couple months ago to ask about a possible wedding location at this rose garden. text: I've been going to Protzel's for many years now and it is one of my all time favorite places. Staffed by warm and genuinely nice people. Selling the best home made corned beef you'll ever eat. Terrific sides including various kinds of kraut, slaw, salads, and even deviled eggs. Also wonderful varieties of smoked fish. Take out or eat there.I've decided that I want my last meal to consist of a Protzel Nova lox and cream cheese sandwich on a Pratzel's (a different place - a bakery) onion bagel, a Protzel corned beef sandwich with sauerkraut on Pratzel's tzitzel bread, and marble halvah for dessert.What a way to die!

text: This place lacked anything that would qualify it as a "restaurant." Namely service and good food. The steak in my chimi had no flavor and the peppers hijacked any chance the other ingredients had of shining through. They do have beer specials, and I assume that is so you can wash down the bad memory of a lack luster dinner. The salsa bar was a nice touch but the sauce I had, labeled "XHot" had no flavor or heat. So what is there to look forward to about Pancho's? Nothing, don't even bother.

text: Used to love this place...then I found gnat bugs in my pasta. It was dark in thre and I thought it was pepper...got home to discover the bugs in my leftovers. Never again. If you have had issues with the Ardmore Fellini's, please try Newtown Square or Guiseppe's in Edgemont. Same menu, better waitstaff, amazing food and no bugs in the pasta. :)

text: I was really excited to eat some good seafood on my trip to New-Orleans, so I looked up a bunch of places on Yelp and in my guidebook. Felix's restaurant came up, and I thought I'd give it a try considering it was a block from my hotel and I didn't feel like waiting in line to get into Acme Oyster House. I went pretty late on a Saturday evening (around 9:30 or 10?), and the place was pretty much empty, which did not bode very well. Our waiter was friendly and helped us promptly, but I was not too impressed by the food. First, we ordered half a dozen oysters on the half shell: I expected them to shuck them for us, but I saw them pull out a plate of shucked oysters out of a fridge... bad. I wouldn't say the oysters were terrible, but they weren't great either: a little too fat and not as fresh as I like them (it might just be that I'm more used to cold water oysters). Then I had a half shrimp po-boy with a side of jambalaya: it was all reasonably good but really not that extraordinary. I left a little disappointed... I'm not sure I'd go again. 2-1/2 stars. (By the way... I tried the local brew, Abita, and to be frank, it kind of tastes like cat piss. Not impressed).

text: This is one of my favorite Italian restaurant on the north side of town. I eat here at least twice a week. The garlic rolls are to die for. I recommend this restaurant for romantic date night.

There were only 5 people in the restaraunt but it took forever to get a refill. Oh and the guy making sushi? Awful. He was on his cell phone the entire time i was waiting for him to make a california roll...but when i actually ended up getting it, i regretted waiting so long. This place is a total fail. Save your money and go somewhere else.

Great distance to the beach!

Their pizza is good, as are the wings (even if they are a bit greasy), but for me it's the spinach salad and the antipasti that are the real winners. I make no bones about the fact that I hate vegetables, but they make nice salads here.

text: 3 Monkeys, I'm glad you're here! I don't frequent you enough... My experiences here vary a bit! During meal times, I've found it's been easy enough to get a table and have had great service. The pizza is excellent. The most recent time, I split the chicken mushroom alfredo pizza with a friend and we each got a small side salad. The small side salad is really big for less than $4!!! We had more than enough pizza to eat and take home. The crust on the pizza is fab. The pizza we chose was really good, but I probably won't order it again. I think I'll like the other ones better. I do remember loving the BBQ Chicken pizza on a previous visit! Alternatively, I've been here on some late weekend nights for a drink and it's been a bit crowded. The parking is just on the street, so especially with Tin Can being right across the street - sometimes you've got to park a bit further back & deep in the neighborhood. Never anything unmanageable though! Dress code varies from casual (they have TV's with sports on) - to dressy casual/cute (the dark woods of the bar/tables/chairs give it a bit of class and ambience). But FYI- they have a good specialty drink (cocktail) list! I've tried the "Blue Monkey" and the "St. Louis Bellini" and loved them. I'm a sucker for a good cocktail menu.

text: I feel bad for being the first one to review Zaytoon's with a bad rating, but I think I am warranted in this rating. The night started out with my boyfriend and I waiting 15 minutes to be seated, with reservations, when it was not even busy on a Monday night. There were plenty of tables and the host said he'd go "survey" the area to determine where to place us. It was fine to me I was just enjoying the night in SB away from LA with my boyfriend. It takes another 20 minutes to just get water at the table we were placed. When I finally got water, my glass had a huge lipstick smudge on it and my boyfriend's was also dirty. We told the girl and it took her an additional 10 minutes to return with water. We wait for the pita bread and tables seated after us were given bread. I ask the girl what's in the dip because I am prone to allergies and she said she'd go check with the kitchen and never returned. I could never pin point my waitress down because we kept getting served by different people. They also delivered the wrong food to our table and the waiter insisted it was what we ordered... wrong. Who can mistake a filet kebab for chicken kebab. I mean, really. My food was cold when I got it and so was my boyfriend's. I could hardly get a refill for my coke. And all I really wanted to do was get out of there instead of enjoying a nice night with my boyfriend. I specifically asked this time that someone tell me what was in the beef shawarma which my boyfriend had. Yes, it was good, but they clearly had no clue what it was seasoned with and I think they might have made up what was really in it because.. I broke out in a serious allergic reaction so severe I had to go to the hospital a few days later. I know what I'm allergic to and the fact that they lied to me about what was really in the shawarma or neglected to tell me what was in the pita dip really irritated me. Needless to say, it was a terrible little get away for me and I really wished I could have added to the 5 stars. However, all you yelpers were right, the setting is very pretty and had the potential of being a great date night if it weren't for the poor service and negligence of the waiters.
label: NEG

text: This mall was heavily looted and burned during Katrina. It has never been the same since. Many of the merchants pulled out and the restaurants (Cannons and Semolina) are closed. There is still a limited food court. Id recommend you go somewhere else, but it is convenient to a lot of areas.
label: NEG

text: In a nutshell, Meagan is awesome. I've been using her for massage for several years and she has been a tremendous help for my constant aches and pains. My primary issue is lower back pain, but she manages to find and work out all of my kinks. In my experience, prior to Meagan, it was hard to find a therapist who was consistent in both ability and knowledge. As another review wrote, she is constantly educating herself on the latest techniques and methods and clearly has compassion for her clients and passion for her work. She has given me some great tips for home exercises (and knows when I haven't been doing them!). Aside from being a master massager, Meagan is a wonderful person, which makes the overall experience of utlizing her services that much more rewarding.

text: Not that this salon actually needs any more great reviews, but I've been so impressed that I finally made a Yelp account just to say what a great place it is. From the extremely friendly male receptionist, to the offer of coffee or water right after you come in, and the snacks and candy available while you wait (which I've never had to), this salon treats its customers unbelievably well! And that's all before you get to the good part. I've had Lana cut my hair twice. I liked it so much the first time when I really just got a trim, that I went for a little more boldness the second time and really had her take some length off. It looks awesome! I've always had to straighten my already straight hair just to get the awkward waves out, but somehow she cut and layered my hair in a way that I can just blow dry and go! I've gotten a ton of compliments on my hair, and I find going to the salon such a relaxing and enjoyable experience. The price is completely reasonable, I've had so many worse experiences for more money. You really can't beat this place!

text: So, I'm feeling juiced after buying a new suit, so I decide to wrap up my outstanding Kirkwood Hwy Indian joint lunches with the last one I haven't tried. I wish I had just skipped it and gone to the Maharaja down the road. I'm giving them 2 stars out of appreciation of their trying different dishes. I believe this is the former Cafe Chettinad, which specialized in South Indian. To be sure, you are given a choice of Naan or a dosa, and the dosa was the best part of the meal, except possibly the gulab jamun. The buffet offerings had some originality, including two goat dishes, Mongolian chicken, one other Chinese related dish, as well as a tofu tikka masala. Unfortunately, the execution was pretty poor. The chunks of meat were low quality, and the sauces tasted cheap. The Mongolian chicken in particular had a nasty red sauces that I'd expect only from the worst Chinese stir-fry place. The tikka masala sauce was not terrible, but the tofu chunks were too soft. I would have preferred a spongier texture, like a paneer dish would have. Alas. $7.95 may be cheaper than the places around it, but an extra $2 apparently makes a heck of a difference.
label: NEG

text: This is one of my favorite places in the city - although I don't make it over often. I like the atmosphere here better than the sister bar on Sansom... and it's usually easier to get a table. My favorite pairing thus far has been the TTE DE MOINE cheese and the MALBEC "SELECCIN," ALAMOS, '06. They also have a good Gorgonzola with Fig Jam Bruschetta (although I like Vintage's better) and a mixed marinated olive bowl that makes me sit still and swoon. Overall - a great little hangout. Makes for a great happy hour or late night hole - but I'm not sure I'd call it a great place for dinner. Still - if you're going - let me know so I can come with...
label: POS

text: It was ok. The service was very energetic and thoughtful but she had not tried hardly any of the food. I never understand restaurants, no matter how casual, not providing the wait staff samples of the menu items. She had nothing to recommend because she had not tried anything - plus who better to sell your menu than your wait staff? I had read about the fried chicken & how good it is. I ordered it. Unfortunately, they ran out and could not serve me fried chicken. So I ordered the catfish and it was tasty but not the best quality. The meat was paper thin (almost) and the crust tasted great! However, the protein was missing and it was not worth the cardiac-inducing calories. The "mashed" potatoes had a lot of something - mayo or some sort of fat. It's not for me but for someone who likes rich mashed potatoes. The green beans were excellent! As another review indicated they use bacon or some sort of smoked pork fat in these. I'm a critical green bean nut... so.... Great job! However, the collard greens (or as Michael Scott says "colored greens") were not fresh and tasted weird. Similar to other "meat and three's" I have tried. I don't know if it is because they are from frozen or what but they tasted like they had a slight chemical taste. I DO NOT think they had anything unnatural - again, not my taste. My wife had something unremarkable. Decent but not great. The banana pudding she had was not good and she had to send it back. They were nice about it and actually refunded us the pudding. The wait staff was very nice and excellent - very well intentioned. This meat and three was slightly above average.
label: NEG

text: I live in the neighborhood and brought a flat stroller tire here to be fixed. Two uses later, the tire was flat again. When I brought it back, they charged me the full price to have the tube replaced again ($5 for the tube, and $5 for their 4 minutes of labor). While technically they're right that the tire could have gotten another flat, it seemed to me more likely that there was a problem with the first fix, and it only would have cost them $5 to gain me as a loyal customer forever. I just hoped for better customer service from a neighborhood bike shop. We certainly won't be taking our bike there for any repairs in the future!
label: NEG

text: My husband already submitted a short review, but I thought I'd elaborate a bit. We dined here on a recent Sunday evening and were overall very disappointed. We started with 2 wine flights, but the server sped and mumbled his way through the descriptions so fast we couldn't understand a word. He also took the wine menu after we ordered, so we couldn't refer to them to see what we were drinking. But, the flights were reasonably priced and a good size pour, so that helped make up for the lack of flair with the service. We specified that we were going to share 2 appetizers, but they were served to each of us without any small plates for sharing the dishes. I asked him as he walked away for "2 small plates", he looked at me and then never returned. The braised pork ravioli dish was excellent (a bit small for sharing, but delish). We also had the Carmelized Onion and Goat Cheese Tart which was served with baby greens tossed in a light vinaigrette. It was tasty but a bit overdone, as if it had been left under a heat lamp too long. Everything was cleared away including the silverware, which wasn't replaced once our main dishes arrived. So frustrating! We had to grab new silverware from a nearby empty table. For our mains, I ordered the Seared Californa Bass, which wasn't very seared at all but still managed to be over cooked. So disappointed to have dry fish in a restaurant, especially at $25 a plate. But, the polenta cake and ratatouille were both good. When I mentioned to our server that the fish was overcooked he said "that's funny, it's usually UNDER cooked". My husband ordered the Grilled NY Steak with Bleu Cheese Scented Croquette and Grilled Rapini. Whew....if that is a bleu cheese SCENTED croquette, I'd hate to taste a "bleu cheese croquette". I LOVE bleu cheese, especially with beef. But this was just too much warm, melty, rich cheese. We found no evidence of any potato. The rapini was just inedible, very very bitter and chewy. It was almost as if they cooked the part you're supposed to trim off and throw away. The beef was rich and tasty and a tad over coooked, but after all of the fat was cut away it didn't leave a very big portion. So, overall I felt that they had the "B Team" working on Sunday night. Service is a big part of the dining experience, and when the food also doesn't measure up, it just makes for a very disappointing over all experience. If the food was A+, we probably could have overlooked an apathetic and bored service staff.

text: I'm completely confused...We went to Morimoto last night for my husband's 40th birthday dinner and we were all (the six of us) very disappointed in the quality/flavor of the food. text: If you're looking for a great pizza restaurant in Edmonton, look no further. Famoso has the best selection of wine and authentic Neapolitan pizza in the city. The environment inside the downtown location is nice and cozy, with tables or booths to accommodate you and your party of 4, or even if it's just for 2. The restaurant is small, medium to dim lighting, and they make use of every little space possible for tables. Do not let the small size fool you; the available patio essentially doubles the capacity and is great to sit in during the summer months. Not familiar with pizza and wine combinations? Famoso makes it easy by splitting the menu into 2 sections: 'red' and 'white' pizzas, with the color allocated to the wine type. 'Red' is also an indication that it is primarily meat-based, whereas 'white' refers to chicken-based toppings. Of course, you do not need to order any wine... The staff are very friendly and knowledgeable on menu items. Ordering involves a different procedure however. You are seat yourself at a table and take a menu from the table corner, and although a server comes to take your drink order, you have to take your main order to the ordering till. Although it's not really a hassle, it can be complicated if you have a large party and offer to take down everyone's order (Wait, am I doing the server's job?). Dishes are brought to your side of the table thankfully. Here comes the important part: recommendations! Their Italian Sodas are bubbly and full of flavor, even though it's really San Pellegrino. The Mediterranean Flatbread is an excellent appetizer. The Flatbread is warm and soft when you get it, and the house-made tzatziki and Tuscan hummus dipping sauce is made to a high quality. I found it easier to just take a knife and spread both on the flat bread instead of poking at the dip with the soft bread...it's just more efficient. The Siciliana pizza and Bella pizza were baked just right with fresh ingredients...this is definitely not your take out-style pizza. Still hungry for dessert? I recommend their Nutella Pizza pizza. That's right, Nutella and banana combined in a warm pita-like enclosure. In a rush? Waiting time for the above dishes was under 15 minutes! Speedy, especially if you're on the run. On Wednesdays, they have their Vino night, which is a free wine tasting event. Also, if you purchase a bottle of wine, you get a free order of bruscetta. Not a deal breaker but it's a good alternative if you go down with a group and share the cost of a bottle! I will definitely be coming back again!

On Friday I called at 3:30 to reserve my spot in the 5:30 class. I was told I called too early and to call back later. I called back at 4:14 and was told the class was full, oh well. Tonight I had planned on going to the 6:30 spin class. I called at 5:03 and was told the class was full up and that I could not attend. I asked them how it was possible that in 2 and 1/2 - 3 minutes 20+ people had called and reserved spots. The girl on the phone told me that there are three phones and three people answering them and that 6-7 people on each line had beaten me to it. Then she told me I could go to Zumba instead if I wanted. No thanks. That annoyance aside, spin class is usually great. Carl and Ellie are my favorite spin teachers, as they are both fun and challenging. Ellie is really the best thing that gym has going for it. If it weren't for her classes I might have just told the gym to take their spin classes and their 29.99 a month and shove it up their toned asses. Clearly I do it for the classes. That being said, I'm not an expert on the quality of the weight lifting machines. They seem pretty normal to me and are never very crowded. The treadmills, eliptical machines, and bikes are not many in number. If you are someone who prefers to run on the treadmill but can only get to the gym after a 9-5 job, this is very challenging. text: I like my Sprint phone. I really do, and I'm not picking on this specific location here, but on Sprint in general. I got my Sprint phone about a year ago and get very good reception at reasonable rate on the family plan with my girlfriend. I NEVER talk on my cell, but I do send out a ton of texts, so we opted to go with the unlimited texting plan. Easy as that, no real problems for the next six months. So, about four months ago the girlfriend and I decide to upgrade our phones. Hers is getting really old (she had it for two years before we got on our plan) and mine was just always a total piece of crap. She gets a Katana and I get a Rumor. She bought her Katana at Radio Shack, so they called Sprint and switched the service over for her, whereas I ordered my phone online and waited a few days for it. When I call to activate my phone I talk to the ONLY nice person who's ever been employed by Sprint and she tells me that we're racking up a lot of text message overages that are costing us a lot of money. I explain to her that we have unlimited texting, we've always had unlimited texting, and no one's ever changed that. She takes a look at the account, reverses the charges, and re-adds the unlimited plan. I figure everything's okay. The next month when our phone bill is autopayed we get overcharged by $80. This is shortly before xmas, and right around rent time, so we really can't afford the extra money and we call to see what's up. Now, I work in a call center and I'm extremely polite to fellow phone jockeys, but these people had me nearly to the point of screaming profanities. The first guy I talk to sounds like he's high on weed and cough syrup. He tells me that, yes he sees the problem, yes it's clearly their fault, but no, he can't do anything to help me. I ask him to transfer me to someone who can, so he puts me on hold for a little over five minutes. Finally a woman answers the phone who's that special kind of irritable that implies to me that she just quit smoking, is on the rag, and just found out her baby daddy is cheating with her cousin. She tells me she can apply the credit to next months bill, but there's no way she can credit it back to my card. She implies that to do so would require some sort of wacky technology that a humble multi-billion dollar company like Sprint wouldn't possibly have access to. I ask for a supervisor. Yay! Another ten minutes on hold! A supervisor picks up and tells me I have to talk to a different department. I wait on hold about five minutes for that department, and then they tell me I have to talk to customer service. I tell them that's who I was just talking to, but they don't care and transfer me anyway. At this point I just want to get off the phone before I hurt somebody, so I just agree to the credit and triple check that my phone does indeed have unlimited text messaging. I'm told it's all taken care of. Guess what happens when I get my next bill? Guess!!!! Yep, fifty dollars in text message overages. WTF? I call before the bill goes through this time and get it reversed, have them re-add the service for the third time, and take my bill the hell off of auto-pay so I can look at it before they take my money. Oh, and somehow they've charged me for six ringtones I've never downloaded over the course of the past year as well. If you're looking for a new cell phone carrier, look somewhere else!

text: I've been a regular staple on South street since I was one of those annoying noisy think I'm so cool high schoolers. None so more a staple till I opened a business a few blocks down from this South St. corner stone a few years ago. So walking pass his beautiful restaurant for so many years, I've really wanted to try it, but never really had the chance to. So with Father's Day approaching. My brother and I thought. " hmm where can we bring our dad [who's a chef in the Rittenhouse Sq. area ] for lunch? " BRIDGET FOY'S! Why not? The outdoor patio is almost always packed on beautiful sunny weekends! So off to Bridget Foy's we went!! HOW DISAPPOINTING! For Starters we had the Sante Fe Salad w/ grilled Chicken [which I stated in my order, but the waitress did not take our order correctly and had to come back twice to check we had ordered exactly]. The salad was AWESOME but a bit pricey at $9 for a very small serving. It came with tortilla strips, jack cheese, and a really yummy bbq ranch dressing. We also had the Hummus [ which was $6 ] with 3 VERY small scoops of pesto, kalamata olive, roasted pepper with garlic. The hummus was very dry, and tasted supremely bland. The pita points served were good, but could have been grilled for a little longer. Entrees I had the duck tacos. [$9] The duck was completely wasted. It came so sweet, and the Guacamole served on the side was bland. The meal was also accompanied by a spring mix that was also nothing to write home about. My dad at the Chipotle Pork Chimichonga[$9]. It wasn't bad had a nice jalapeno kick to it, but really greasy also served with a bland salsa, and the spring mix. My brother had the Crispy Chicken Sandwhich [$9]. Let's just say the chicken was soggy and the fries were dried and tasted as though they were re fried. Service was worst. Our waitress though very nice was clueless, the lady refilling the water would come by and fill one our of our 3 glasses. There was always an empty glass for some odd reason she would not fill. The girl that brought out our food was inconsistent. In the middle of eating my meal. I went to take a fry from my brother's plate, when she just swooped in and took my plate away without asking if I was done, which I was not. Our entree took FOREVER to come out. What was super odd, and I felt bad for this table was a table next to us. The 2 ladies sat down way before us. Ordered before us. But didn't get there entrees till we were paying our check. I guess if you want to try this place. On a nice afternoon, it's always a Nice place to grab a drink and sit out on the patio with appetizers, but if you want to sit down for a meal. Roll down the street to Jon's. This was not worth coming to.

text: I went in here the other day, partly because I wanted to kill some time in an air conditioned venue while waiting for someone in Olde City and partly because I have a whole stack of books that I want to get rid of, so I wanted to ask if they buy used books. However, the owner was deep in conversation with some guy when I went in, so I decided to browse while he was finishing his conversation. I had the same negative reaction to this place as I did to the Strand in NYC. Disorganized used book stores turn me off the worst way. The aisles are tight, stacks of books litter the floors in the aisles, so you can't get down them easily, and it's very, very difficult to find anything because it's so disorganized. That means you'll have to ask for help, and it's hard to do that when the owner is busy chatting away with his buddy, and there's no one else there to help out. Plus, this place was freaking hot. Especially the second floor, where the fiction and some other categories are. Anyway, it was hot and I wanted to get out of there, away from the clutter, heat, and moldy/dusty book smell, but I had to wait until I caught the owner's attention to ask him about selling him my books before I could make a break for the door. Finally, I managed to ask my question, and I was told that they only trade store credit for people's books. That was disappointing, but I guess they really are just a book trader in the literal sense. If this was a store that I ever thought I'd set foot in again, then store credit might be okay, but buying books that I need (and I need a lot for my grad program) from this store would be a nightmare. If they were more organized (and had air conditioning that worked!), I might consider it. But I think I'll take my business elsewhere. God, I miss the used book store from South Street that got closed down and replaced with a trendy men's clothing store! That place was the best : (
label: NEG

text: I'm only reviewing Figaro's, the little pizza by the slice place inside. The store itself is fine if you don't mind people with no time-space awareness and like excellent prices on a very wide variety of items. No frills, warehouse feel. For instance Feline Pine cat litter is about 1/2 the price of Petco. Meats/cheeses are the least expensive (as opposed to cheap) anywhere in the Reno-Sparks area. So, Figaro's, it's literally the worst pizza I've ever had. It deserves a negative rating to drive down other ratings. It's that bad. You know when you're a kid and you make pizza with ketchup, mozzarella cheese on a piece of bread or an English muffin in the toaster? It's far worse than that. Have you had the intense displeasure of Domino's pizza in the Brussels airport? The bread with ketchup on it that's even worse than the homebrew, sort of White-Trashy "pizza" I describe above? Worse than that. It was unfresh bread, flavorless despite having sausage on it, ketchup-y sauce and just disgraceful. If I hadn't been starving at the time, it would have gone out the window. I think even kids, you know the non food savvy little monsters that think McDonald's is delicious, would recognize their pizza as crap. Please do us all a favor and shut your doors. I'm not kidding. Tostino's, amongst the lamest of microwave pizzas, easily outshines this stuff. I think ketchup with cream cheese on pumperknickel as pizza wouldn't be this bad. It's been like six months since I had their pizza and I still revile the memory. I want the experience back.
label: NEG

text: the good: the mediterranean themed decor was inviting, festive, yet calming all at once. it provided just the right amount of lighting to give each table a private feel without being too dark. the lounge area was cozy yet chic. the bad: the food went from disappointing to inedible to just plain sad. course 1 consisted of stuffed fried calamari, grilled tiger prawns, artichoke, ricotta and lemon soup, and tuna crudo. the calamari tasted okay but it was an okay ball of dough with a tasty sauce. we couldn't taste, chew, or see any calamari. the grilled tiger prawns were also okay. grilled perfectly but had no flavor. the tuna crudo was basically chopped day old sushi. it desperately needed salt and lemon and eventually just felt gummy as we continued eating it. the soup however had a very nice balanced flavor. it incorporated all ingredients well. it wasn't a hit with everyone at the table but it was mostly due to their dislike of the individual ingredients. course 2 consisted of rack of wild boar and braised pork shoulder. the wild boar was unseasoned and overcooked. it tasted freezer burned and looked like it was sitting under a heating lamp for a few hours. the pork shoulder was cardboard dry with an overly sweet sauce that just assaulted your tastebuds. no one at the table was able to finish their dish. the side of gnocchi made a bad meal worse. the gorgonzola was just overpowering. course 3 consisted of creme brulee and nutella crepe. both were unmemorable. the worse: service started out fine. friendly smiling server. bread and water were re-filled rather quickly. but after the food was brought out and we noted to the server how there was a mistake, it all went downhill from there. he said he would not charge us for the mistake but we could keep the dish anyway. after that point, the server was m.i.a. the rest of the night. the wait time from appetizer to entree was about 5 minutes (approximately 8:00PM). the wait time from the entree to dessert menu was 20 minutes (approximately 9:00PM). the wait time from dessert menu to dessert was 30 minutes and were brought out by another server. the bill was also dropped off by another server. (even though we saw our server walking around) and long and behold, we were charged with the mistaken dish. after waiting about 20 minutes for the server to return, we gave up and decided to pay for a dish we neither ordered not ate because we were just plain tired and disappointed by then. as we got up to leave, we caught a glimpse of our server sitting on a table in the kitchen chatting with other servers. overall i may go back for drinks in the lounge area but dinner was really subpar for what it presents itself to be.

text: On the surface BICAS seems like a great group. Problem is that the people that work there, the inner circle if you will, take all the best donated bikes for themselves and put the junk they don't want out on the floor. I have seen this happen time and again. If you are donating bikes to BICAS realize that, if it is any good, you are basically giving a bike to one of a small group of people that work there or one of their friends. The only good thing is the availability of tools and work stands. If you need a piece to 1983 suntour downtube shifter they may have it. Still, I have found good bike parts out on the floor before and, when trying to buy them, been told that they were mistakenly put out on the floor and were not for sale to the general public. There is a "backroom" where they keep all their hoarded bits and pieces away from the commoners. Better to give your old bike directly to someone who needs it. That way the 1979 Trek touring bike you donate doesn't end up spirited into the garage of one of the shop rats never to be seen on the floor for the public.
label: NEG

text: Executive Chef Chris Broussard, I say keep your name off the business cards until you've fixed your kitchen. Eating at Creole Kitchen was a waste of time and money. The place is cute and the menu looks good, but tastes terrible. Let me start with the gumbo. You'd think a waterfront eatery would have fresh seafood in their gumbo... I didn't see anything other than okra and a single bay leaf and a spoon full of white rice garnish. Call it vegan okra stew, not gumbo. It was too thick and absolutely flavourless and serving it lukewarm didn't help much either. After one spoon I pushed it aside and ordered the Seafood Crepe... Gauging from the temperature of the three crepes filled with room temperature Campbell's seafood chowder, I would guess it was prepared an hour before I ordered it. I sent it back to get heated and it came back one degree warmer. Finally, for a place that boasts Sunday Brunch, they only have one kind of tea to serve, Ceylon. Sadly I had only two meals in New Orleans and this place was my last one. I headed to the airport straight after with a bad taste in my mouth.

text: The Gaylord Opryland Hotel is a world class resort hotel with an amazing history, unfortunately run by untrained, incompetent idiots. My girlfriend and I had both been guests there in the past, and in need of an escape from back-to-back to back family get-togethers, we stopped in Nashville for a quick holiday getaway. Let's start with the good: the hotel is beautiful, the shows (A Country Christmas and The Radio City Rockettes) were excellent, and the bell hop staff was top notch. However, that's where the praise ends. From beginning to end, our stay at Gaylord Opryland a nonstop shit show. It all started when we pulled onto the property at 2:00 in the afternoon on a Monday, only to sit in the car for 40 minutes waiting to get to the valet station. When I inquired (rather good naturedly) why it took so long to valet the car, the valet quite smugly laughed in my face and said, "this is a 3,000 room hotel - 40 minutes is a short wait around here." He was right, because over the course of my stay we waited in line an average of 55 minutes each time we attempted to valet the car. And since valet was the only handicapped parking option, and the self-park parking lots were a zoo from their ICE and SNOW exhibits, this colossal waste of time remained our only parking option. But the lines didn't stop at the valet station: 25 minutes of sitting at the bar at The Falls to get the attention of the attitude-encumbered bartender, who didn't know what a Hot Toddy was, didn't know bourbon was whiskey, and when another patron asked if the bar carried limoncello, made a face as if someone had broken wind and said, "I've never heard of THAT." And there was that time a maid, without waiting for a response to her brief knock, walked into our room at a MOST inopportune time. You'd think she would apologize, turn around and leave immediately, but instead she WALKED INTO THE BATHROOM over our shouts of disapproval to do lord-knows-what before finally leaving (sans apology). One evening we had the valet pull our car around but after 25 minutes of waiting we went back inside, so we weren't there when the valet arrived with the car. So he locked the doors, put the keys in his pocket, and promptly walked off. We stood in front of our locked car for over half an hour while the valet staff scrambled to find out keys. There was also the time we waited in line, outside in the cold, for 45 minutes to board a shuttle for the Rockettes that was supposed to start running at 6:30, but we didn't step foot onboard until 7:15 (for a 7:30 show). Or our final morning, when our wakeup call was a 'fire drill' demanding we evacuate the building, followed by a 30 minute 'all clear' alarm. But the icing on the cake was when we were ready to checkout. We called down to the valet for our car, only to be told, "We're not accepting phone requests for vehicles, you have to stand in line curbside with your luggage in hand before we'll get your car. CLICK." So we finished packing our bags, lugged them downstairs ourselves, and I joined the back of the valet counter line (which stretched halfway across the hotel lobby). Fifteen minutes later my girlfriend returned with a super friendly manager from the front desk, Brittney. We explained the wait times, the lost keys, and the morning's phone call, and she offered to find a valet manager for us. It took her ten minutes, but I was still only halfway through the line when she returned with the valet manager (Matt). I explained again the wait times, lost keys, etc. He looked annoyed, but under the eye of Brittney, took my valet ticket and offered to personally expedite our car. He disappeared, but 45 minutes later there was still no sign of him, or our car. So I tracked down a second valet manager, who chuckled at my inquiry and non-chalantly replied, "yeah, Matt was looking for a white Lincoln Navigator. I guess you're driving, like, a black car or something. He's pulling up now, he'll be there in 30 seconds." He must have missed the valet tag on the key chain which clearly identified our car as a black Charger (which looks nothing like a white Navigator). Five minutes later, my car finally arrived. Matt's response: no apology, no reason why he hadn't come to find my over the last hour to explain the delay, just an attempt to justify the situation by giving me the whole "looking for a white Lincoln" story. In the end, Brittany ended up reimbursing us for two nights and our valet charges. However, the problems at Gaylord Opryland Hotel run far deeper than one person's experience. Every other guest I spoke to in the lobby that morning felt the same way, and I heard stories from other guests that were far worse than mine. The general consensus among the staff I spoke with was that this was "just the way things are," and unavoidable for a hotel this large. If that's going to be the case, I would suggest that Gaylord Opryland itself should be avoided.
label: NEG

text: This is absolutely my favorite place to go see a movie. If you love movies, you will love the Tivoli. First of all, their movie offerings can only be compared to Plaza Frontenac's theater. They only show high-class, quality and generally independent flicks here. If you're looking for mainstream drivel, look elsewhere. And to add another positive to my list, they recently showed a completely independent movie that was made on Mizzou's campus for one evening. text: Since having my son, I have been exploring the inner workings of all things kiddo. This has been an ongoing challenge b/c I was never sure I'd have children, so I have generally avoided places that target family fun. I went last year and had a good time with my niece and nephew who are a bit older, and today, I experienced a different side of the museum. Tucked away in areas I had yet to check out were places that the little kids could really enjoy. A splash tub with lots of toys floating around and ponchos to cover their clothes was a nice added touch. Different textured floors to crawl and run on, a sand box area for the younger troops. It was great to watch Max see things for the first time! He really enjoyed all the things close to the floor at his eye level, from the flower potting area to the magnet wall. We also rode the carousel a couple of times. His first time he was mesmerized by the stars above and all the different colors and music that were going on around us. His face was beaming!! We went with three other friends, all with younger children and they just had so much fun going through the maze, digging in the sand and checking out the exhibits. I was really impressed this time. I could really take it all in and appreciate it better now that I am a mother. And, for me, the best part was the 50 years of Barbie history exhibit that they have going on now. I saw the Star Wars exhibit last year and was not impressed, but the Barbie's showroom kicked butt! There was a catwalk, dressing area, make up area, photographer's booth, tons of stuff for the kids, but the stuff for us moms, looking back on the years of Barbie and our own childhood brought back an insane amount of fun memories! It was really impressive all the Barbie information they shared and how beautiful the dolls on display were. They had two life size Barbies and lots of original Barbies in boxes showing how she has grown and changed through the years, the mansions she lived in, the car she drove and the man she married (and I believe divorced recently), Ken. It was a really cool exhibit! I was having as much fun as Max at that point. :) Thankfully he is loving pink right now, so all the bright colors made him happy too while I drug him around the showroom! I look forward to going back year after year as Max's interests change, b/c the museum will help him grow and learn. This is a great unique date option, a great place for families of ALL ages, an incredible value for money and is ranked one of the best children's museums in the country. It is worth checking out!

The dolmades taste like they come from a can, the spinach rice is overpowering, and the spanikopita and cheese pies are not fresh. The filo is chewy and tastes like it is made days ahead and nuked prior to serving. The Mediterranean mixed veggies were pure mush. So, all things considered, I don't understand why they are priced higher than most of the Greek restaurants in the area. The right side of the restaurant is completely odd and dated. First, you have to trek past the open station where they dump all of the food and dirty dishes in order to get to your table. They built a wooden room within a room that has lattice rafters up by the ceiling and it is ladened with dated would accents throughout. This "room within a room" wastes a ton of space in the restaurant and it is butt ugly. The light fixtures are big, obtrusive monsters from the '70's and I honestly think they haven't been cleaned since they were installed. Most of the bulbs are burnt out. Look up when you are eating and notice the splattered food and cobwebs in the pendant lights that hang over your table. Lovely. In addition, the grime is all over the wails, the artwork by the table and the condiments and table signs that sit on your table. It's a sticky, grimy, mess. The last time I was there, it took forever to get our food and while we were waiting, they stacked all of the chairs on the tables around us. How rude.
label: NEG

text: Here's an idea that it seems never dawns on a lot of people: do some research before you go to a place. I love the food at Tujague's, but I know what to expect--especially since it's on their website and the place is listed in most every guide book to New Orleans that I've ever seen. In case you haven't gathered yet--Tujague's is not your normal restaurant with a ton of options. And it's not the typical low-end, made from a box cheap creole that appeals to tourists, nor is it the fancy modern food you find at the nicer places in town. This place is one of the oldest restaurants in America and definitely the oldest in New Orleans, and the menu and service reflect that. They serve a fixed menu that typically consists of a shrimp appetizer, a soup, boiled brisket, your entree, and dessert. The entree options usually include a pasta choice and they always include a filet (which is pretty mediocre). Again, this is working class, 19th century food and that's part of the charm and appeal of the place. You pick the options you want and then they serve you your five courses. I suggest enjoying yourself and having a few drinks. The bar (separate from the restaurant) features a marble slab brought from Paris well over a hundred years ago.

text: I needed to take a lunch break while I was on my way to Morro Bay, so I took out my handy iPhone and went on Yelp. The reviews insisted the food was orgasmic, so I decided to come here. There was a gorgeous view from the pier. I ordered (outside) a clam chowder in a sourdough bowl for $9, a shrimp and scallop caesar salad for $13, as well as a fried calamari, scallops, shrimp, and oysters platter for $13. The man did not hand me a reciept. Just a number. You have to pay close attention because the guys taking your order expect you to wait on him like a dog next to the window. So, I just leaned my back to the wall and watched people take all the tables that were several yards away. As I read in The Glorious Oyster, Oysters are the most tender and delicate of all seafoods. The stay in bed all day and night. They never work or take exercise, are stupendous drinkers, and wait for their meals to come to them. Well, then I am an oyster. I DON'T LIKE BEING WAITED ON.This would be pretty frustrating for somebody who was eating alone because when he picks up his food, there may be no tables available. So he'd have to wait ten to twenty minutes just to get a table. Don't get me wrong. This wouldn't stop me from getting some kickass seaFOOD because the FOOD is what I came here for, right?. But whatever. I did find a table, but by the time I did, my salad had already cooled down. It tasted pretty good though. The clam chowder was hot, had plenty of clams, and wasn't too thin or too thick. The fried dish was fried to perfection! Not too greasy, so that's good. 3 stars for the service, 4 stars for the food, 5 stars for the ambiance. (3+4+5)/(2)= 4 STARS Now why did I just do that?

text: This is based on having been here once, whatever that means for you. A friend and I came here for a late lunch/early dinner and were sat in a booth. It was way too cramped. We ended up having to sit at opposite ends and skewing the table so we had enough room to breathe. The service was a little weird (leaving empty glasses even after refilling), but not a problem speed-wise. One issue I had was that the straws were already in the glasses when they were brought. I understand it is somewhat classier to avoid having paper on your black straws when drinks come to the table but the straw is there so that I don't have to drink where your hands may have been (i.e. the rim of the glass). The salad was fine, just to note. A good mixed green. I had the blackened grouper sandwich and had the side of fruit rather than fries. The fruit was served horribly. I was a little miffed at the one piece of pineapple, one piece of watermelon, and the small bunch of unfortunate grapes, but that wasn't the issue. The fruit was sitting on the hot sandwich plate. Maybe it's just me but I think a warm sandwich can withstand a room temperature plate better than cold fruit can withstand a hot plate. I ate my fruit immediately to avoid it cooking and it was still already warmed through. Hot fruit, not so refreshing. The sandwich was good. Not great but certainly not bad. I question their decision to serve it with shredded lettuce (which I declined) as that's got to be the least appetizing thing you can add to a sandwich. The fish had a good mild kick from the blackening spices. The remoulade was both tasty and appropriately portioned, which I appreciated. I'm willing to return and give it another shot, but the menu is a little odd. If I do, I will update the review accordingly.

text: Metropolitan Bakery is my favorite bakery in Philly. The bread is incredible, especially their multigrain. They culture their starters instead of using commercial yeast and it makes a very big difference in the taste. They make the only sourdough I have ever liked, this is due to the natural cultures, which most modern bakeries won't even bother with. text: We have always loved Great Basin over in Sparks and have visited for years, but I have to say, I love this new location much better. It's got a great vibe, busy and bustling and fun. The beer is, of course, fantastic, and the menu, which seems nicely expanded from the Sparks location, is just wonderful. I would love to give this place five stars, but I have been to this location several times and I have to say I agree with some of the complaints about customer service. It's not always on. So minus one single star for that. When the service is good, it's very very good, but when it's bad, well, it's meh. We always sit at the bar if we can, or in the bar area, because the bartenders are ALWAYS awesome and attentive; the same cannot be said of the waitresses. We don't ever get a table because it's a very busy place and generally, once one is seated, one tends to be forgotten. So that's why we sit in / near the bar. Who cares about a waitress forgetting you when the bar is right there? It's easy to just lean over and order another one. And you will want to order another one. That's why you're there, anyway, isn't it? To drink pint after pint of GBBCs life-changing beer. Since I'm years behind in reviewing GBBC let me just give you a quick rundown of the things I enjoy. First, the beer. Any of the beer. All of the beer. It's all great. Our most favorite of what is a truly awe inspiring selection has to be The Chili Beso, The Lemon Wheat, The Jackpot Porter, The Old Fitz Stout, the Wheeler Peak Wheat, the Ichthyosaur Pale Ale, the Wild Horse Ale and, oh, heck, whatever else they are pouring that day. But our two absolute most drop dead favorites are the Rosemary Rye Patch and the Harvest Ale. It was because of the Harvest Ale we were last at GB, as you can see from the photos I uploaded. We were there to help shell pinenuts for the Harvest Ale - for every glass you filled with shelled nuts, you got a free beer. Now, if you've ever shelled a pine nut, you know how difficult it is. But let me tell you, it was worth every bit of that hour's worth of work to get a free beer. And we have been back to taste the resultant batch, and ahhh! Heaven! It tickles me a lovely amber hue to know we "helped make" that great beer, even if it was only in a teeny tiny fashion. On to the food. Just try anything. It's all great. The stand out appetizer for us is the Jalapeno Won Tons. But be warned: they are amazingly addictive. I also have a weakness for their Willy Dillys; beer battered and fried dill pickle spears, they are outstanding with any of the beer. Other menu standouts: The Sausage Platter, the Shepherds Pie, the Fish & Chips, the Bruben, the Black & Blue Burger, the Garden Burger, The Shroom Burger, and the Pizza (any pizza). Try the pizza with macaroni & cheese and bacon. (See photos) Trust me on this one. I know it sounds crazy but you'll bite into it and you'll think you hear angels weeping, it's so good, but that will just be you and your companions, sobbing with sheer delight at your great fortune to be enjoying such soul-satisfying beer and food on a Friday night. Another thing I love about Great Basin: they've got terrific community spirit. (Thus, the pinenut shelling event!) They support all local Reno events and groups and give generously back to the community that loves them. Even though I have never been a Reno local, going into either Great Basin location always makes me feel like I am. I sit there with a beer in one hand, a pickle spear in the other, and sigh happily, thinking, "Man, it sure is great to be home."

text: I checked this place out for the first time today. The place was slammed so we had to wait a few minutes to snatch a seat, but that simply made my lust for Vietnamese grow fiercer. Once we were seated we were given our water, salad, and chop sticks rather quickly. For being so busy they did ensure that we had what we needed to get things started quickly. I had originally planned on getting a bowl of Pho and then something else on the side, but decided to try two new things. This is generally what I try to do when trying out new places. I decided on the Banh Mi Bo Kho stew and a noodle dish whose name, I believe, was Banh Cha Gio. It had sliced egg rolls and a type of crispy pork on top of a bowl which had salad and a layer of vermicelli. The crispy pork pieces were very good and the egg rolls were of good quality as well. The highlight of my meal without a doubt was the Banh Mi Bo Kho stew. The spicy broth was a perfect blend of hot and savory, while the ingredients were falling apart due to their tenderness. I just envisioned all of these ingredients simmering for hours making sweet sweet love to each other for my personal consumption pleasure. Chunks of carrots, large pieces of meat and sliced onion were the biggest players in the stew. It was so simple looking, but the flavors were very good and almost complicated. I could just poke at the meat with my giant spoon or chopsticks and it would fall into shreds. I've been to Kien Giang and I love their Pho, longside a Bahn Mi sandwich, but this stew was in a league of its own. I think that's the main reason I didn't go with the Pho this time. I don't want to have to compare other Pho to Kien Giang's Pho. It's close to my work so I have a feeling I'll be going back often. If you enjoy Vietnamese and are in the area, it's totally worth your hard-earned.

text: It's really sad to hear that the Val Rio Diner in Phoenixville will soon be closing it's doors forever. The famous cult classic, The Blob, with Steve McQueen was filmed there in the 1950's. When I drove by it last week, the parking lot was almost empty, the place looked forlorn and the sign "Walgreens Coming Soon" was placed prominently by the street. I'm a big fan of the classic diner, and while the Val Rio is gone, there are many that are thriving and important parts of towns and neighborhoods around suburban Philly. One such diner is Daddypops, located in downtown Hatboro. Daddypops is a 1940's diner that has been preserved perfectly by it's owners. Small, crowded, with a great staff that never makes you wait for menus and coffee, Daddypop's is my perfect way to start the day (I loved to be called "Hon" by strangers.) The food is really good and the helpings will force you to "Homer Simpson" your slacks. My wife thinks the pancakes are the best around, and she is a flapjack maven. Only quibble that keeps this from a five-star review is the fact that smoking is allowed in this small space. Great for puffers and it does keep the old ways alive and well; nothing like coffee and cigarettes, as Jim Jarmusch would attest to. But for most people nowadays, it's a turnoff. But please don't let that stop you from stopping by in the AM and getting a taste of Americana Maybe they can shoot The Blob remake their sometime soon.
label: POS

text: Italian bakery rocks my world! My husband was the one who discovered it, and now it is one of our favourite places to go satisfy our sweet teeth. Italians definitely know their pastry and creamy fillings:) They aso know how to make desserts look irresistible. I am unable to resist at least once a week! Some of my favourites are eclaires, "hockey puck" (soft pastry with crunchy chocolate topping, filled with cream) and amaretto balls. I don't mean so sound lame, but Italian bakery's amaretto balls are exactly like my mom used to make. They are sweet, nutty and melt in your mouth. My husband often goes for flaky cones filled with light whipped cream and dusted with confectioners sugar. Delicious! Italian bakery is definitely two steps beyond plain old Safeway and Save-On bakeries, and without a doubt a place to visit if you are looking for a taste of Europe.

text: Every time I walk into Sur La Table, I end up leaving with at least two things to go Sur Ma Table. text: This is a real hole in the wall deli, otherwise known as the "Dirty Mart." It's a tiny convenience store on Royal St. They've got your usual small items for sale on a few aisles, which almost every other convenience store also offers. However, they are open 24 hours and offer free delivery, which isn't offered by all their competition. When you order delivery by phone your location information is conveniently saved into their computer for future orders. The deli has a huge selection of items to choose from, more than most other delis in the quarter. I think I must have ordered about half the menu so far. The lasagna here isn't half bad, and I usually get the spinach and artichoke dip as one of my sides which makes for a nice poor man's chip dip. Servings for entrees are huge, so you can easily split a meal with another person. Their main claim to fame is the "All That Jazz" poboy. You'll get grilled ham, turkey, and shrimp served on french bread and dripping with "wow" sauce. Also comes with both swiss and american cheese. The bread here is more on the thick side rather than airy, which might be necessary to hold up against all those wet toppings. Personally, I think of it more as a hangover cure than the usual representation of a poboy, which is not to say that it isn't tasty. This huge greasy sandwich is large enough to satisfy the biggest of appetites. Costs about $10, which is not at all bad for the quarter.
label: POS

text: Not a lot you can add about this place that hasn't been said. The malts (I had a chocolate, banana, marshmallow malt) are simply phenomenal, it would be hard to overstate just how good they are. The candy selection is great, and if you're looking for Easter selections you should get down there now because they have the most amazing variety of homemade chocolate bunnies you've ever seen. Helpful hint. If you are there to get candy vs. staying to eat you should walk straight to the door and take a number at the ticket dispenser there. You don't need to stand in line. When there is a line out the door that procedure is not apparent and time after time people were waiting in that long line not realizing that they should have taken a number. The food on the other hand, is just OK in my opinion. I love the BLT, you've never seen so much crisp bacon stacked between two pieces of bread, and they use Miracle Whip on it! It's an architectural disaster, but oh so good. And the tamale is ok. But to be honest I'm not as ga-ga over a lot of the other items. None of it is bad, I just have a hard time giving 5 stars if I'm including food into the equation. The one mystery of the day was parking. There was a huge line of people out the door, none of whom lived locally (when you see the neighborhood you'll know why I can be so certain about that statement), yet there were open parking spaces all over the place when we arrived and when we left. How did all of those people get there? Is there some Crown Candy shuttle that I don't know about? Is there one of those Willy Wonka glass elevators hidden around the corner? Are they visitors from "elsewhere" taking on human form (there were a few whose human disguises weren't working so well)? I just don't get it.

text: It really IS ALL THAT. Yes, it's small & loud - so if you come on a weekend call in advance and STILL be prepared to wait. Chef RED did his thing tonight. As did Steve, our server. In fact, all the staff were "on point". The sweet lady who gave us the marvelous bread (infused olive oil with a blob of lemon ricotta in the center) and kept our water glasses full is a doll. The hostesses even helped to clear plates. Everyone pitched in and ran their asses off! A great team. We noticed and we love ya! One warning - this meal is a diet-breaker. Nothing we had was "light 'n healthy". They should have an MD onsite to perform emergency angioplasties. I had heard of Modo Mio for a long while - but when I tasted the Mozarella en Carroza at the "Taste of Philadelphia" event in July, I knew I had to come here. Our party of 4 had the 4 course menu and everyone LOVED everything they had. The house-made pappardelle with brussels sprouts, the bistecca, the skate wing - all of it. Chef RED even sent out a platter with 6 glorious desserts on it. Standouts were the flourless chocolate cake, tiramisu (theirs is light and wonderful), pumpkin bread pudding and home-made crusts, cookies, cremes and panna cottas of all sorts. A near orgasmic experience at Modo Mio tonight. Only one complaint, at 8:50 PM (We had a 6:45 reservation and were seated closer to 7 PM), they made us leave to seat the next table. Politely. Overtly. But I only had like 2 sips of that wonderful coffee I wanted to enjoy. Ah well - next time we will come on a weeknight. WOW!!!! Can't wait to come back. Can't wait to try Paesano. text: I used to go to this place all the time when I was in high school. Just got back into the area, and decided to show it off to some of my friends from afar as a great place to eat breakfast, remembering how good the Mile High was. I don't know if I just had poor taste in food back then or if the place has gone down in quality over the years, but I don't think I'll be coming back, although our waitress was *extremely* nice. Our tip reflected the quality of her service, not the quality of our food. The BLT I ordered was soggy, bacon clearly overcooked and not warm, with wilted lettuce and unripe tomato, along with a tiny bag of chips. My friends ordered the waffles and the Mile High, which were good but unremarkable; the Mile High I remember was mouth-watering just to look at; this one was soggy, the french toast an unpleasant pale shade and the bananas sliced in chunks, so that the whole thing kind of looked like magnified baby food. Extra charge for real maple syrup, also, which I guess is not a big deal.. but it's that kind of detail that makes a place memorable, and it would have been something special to make the rest of the mediocre food stand out. I imagine that most people would have put this first, also, but judging by the immense popularity of this place, I'm graciously going to assume that it was a freak thing? A crushed cricket on the bottom rim of my friend's plate. Yech. Do you know what it's like to eat a BLT sandwich after finding a crunchy insect has been in the kitchen? Let me give you a basic idea - try to imagine the opposite of awesome. I was really looking forward to returning to the West Ave grill; whenever I would walk past and see it bustling with happy business, it made me feel proud of the little Jenkintown business that could. So it was a pretty crappy surprise to find that most of the special had left this little place. Be good again, please??

text: Went here upon recommendation of some fabulous Philly Yelpers. My mom was in town this weekend for my birthday and wanted to take the boyfriend and I out to dinner. I chose Continental because I'd been seeing this place throughout my time here and Philly in always wanted to go, but knew it was too expensive for my poor self. So this was a great time to try it! The decor is really fun and interesting to look at; definitely a conversation piece. We were seated in a booth upstairs and ordered drinks first. I got the Champagne-O-Rama ("champagne & shot of raspberry vodka in a grenadine & sugar rimmed glass"), which was $9 -- one of the cheapest drinks on the menu. It came in a champagne glass, which made it a very small drink, in my opinion, for $9 (that was a little annoying). But it was definitely yummy and it gave me a really nice buzz, even with all of the food. It took us a while to figure out the menu and that everything was kind of share-style. Boyfriend thought that was kind of gimmicky, but I rather liked it. There were so many things on the menu that sounded good to try, so it made it easier that everyone could share. I got the BBQ chicken quesadillas w/ avocado sour cream and I was SO pleased with them. They were a little bit adventurous for me, as I'm very picky about food, but I'm glad I tried them. Mom got the chickpea crusted shrimp and those were fantastic as well (but you only get 4 in one order). Boyfriend got the Rad Na Thai Chicken, and was kind of disappointed -- it sounded like it was going to be something Chinese food-like, and ended up being a gigantic salad. We also got an order of the Schechuan shoestring fries with Chinese mustard sauce to share between the 3 of us. Those were really good, but I was surprised at how tiny and thin the fries were -- they almost weren't big enough to consider fries. Still tasty, though. The servers are all super friendly, and ours wished me a happy pre-birthday at the beginning of the meal when she checked my ID for my drink AND before we left, so that was nice. The bus boy was nice, too. We got there around 5 on a Friday, so we just beat the ensuing crowd. That may have a little bit to do with how fast our food came, but I was still really surprised at that -- I was really hungry when we got there and the food came before I even had time to think about it. So that was another huge plus. The only reason this place lost a star is because, as I said, boyfriend didn't seem to like it so much. But I was really happy with the experience and would definitely go back again if I had some extra cash. :)

text: This is really as good as it gets when it comes to working out. Millennium Place has everything you could ask for. They have an indoor skating rink & indoor soccer fields, a gymnasium, a large workout area with tons of fitness equipment, an indoor swimming pool, a track, food court, and outdoor soccer fields. The wellness center and track are open from 5:30am - 11pm and swimming and skating are open 9am-9pm, which allows for any busy person to get a workout. I honestly cannot think of anything to complain about and at about $30 for monthly membership or approximately $7 for any given day it is much cheaper than most other fitness centers that offer a fraction of the facilities. I usually go with a couple of my friends and we do everything from playing basket ball to soccer to lifting weights and we never have to wait for machines or benches to open up. I have never found myself waiting around for something to free up. We occasionally go for a swim and they have lanes set up as well as a general pool. If you need motivation to start working out I suggest you take a tour of this place and you will be convinced.

text: I decided to visit the Philadelphia portion of Yelp just to give kudos to Blarney South. We came for a pre-season Eagles game and bummed around Philadelphia a bit. I found a gift certificate for Blarney South on Restaurant.com that was a really good deal. 50% off your order for $3. We came on a Thursday night and hesitated a bit in the doorway because the bar is actually situated near the front and we brought our 8 and 12 year olds along with us. They brought us right in and took us to the back, which was set up more like a restaurant. My husband had the most beautiful bacon bleu cheese burger I've ever seen. It was huge with no less than four thick slices of bacon and plenty of bleu cheese crumbles. I honestly don't know how he got his mouth around it, but he managed and it was gone (every last crumb) in no time flat. My older son had a chicken cheese steak, which he said was good, and I had a crab cake sandwich, which was good and filled with crab, but I was yearning for a bite of hubby's burger. My youngest, who just got braces put on a week before and had mouth sores, had potato soup. He told me that I HAD to learn to make it. The fries were great. They were all we had left at the end of our meal and we packed them all into a styrofoam container and took them back to the hotel with us. Service was great. The waitress seemed taken with my younger son (I'm sure it had nothing to do with him playing to her sympathies by refusing to talk and answering with a simple thumbs up or thumbs down) and gave him some extra bread and butter to take back along with some extra soup. We're craving that burger... I just wish it weren't so expensive! ($8 for the burger, $400 for the plane ticket!)

text: Having just returned from a week business trip laced with as much tourism as we could fit in, I feel so obligated to return the favor and provide my first "city review". I never thought to review a city, but I see that others have and I want to do so as well. We had a SPECTACULAR time in The Big Easy. We never had a bad meal, never received a rude comment, got loads of help with directions, and thoroughly enjoyed our very reasonably-priced rooms at the Iberville Suites. It feels as though we ate our way through the city at several restaurants (which I will later review as time permits) including Bourbon House and the Palace Cafe, and ate beignets at Cafe du Monde. And the seafood....well, talk about heaven!! Delish! The people here are warm and friendly and eager to please. Granted, there is as much insanity here as any other large city, but we walked when we could and always felt safe. Bourbon Street is certainly to be experienced...maybe only once, and we did have a great time at Pat O'Brien's. Visiting New Orleans is a must. The Gulf Coast certainly needs visitors now more than ever as they rely so much on tourism. If you haven't been....you should go. If you have been...go back. You won't be disappointed. There is so much to do and see. It's not all about the beaches and the oil. Oh, and by the way, kudos to Gov. Jindal for taking the bull by the horns, as they say, and handling the situation! We will be going back....perhaps in October or March when, as our hotel doorman told us, the weather is so much better than the heat and humidity we experienced during our week.

text: The Hubbs surprised me with a quickie getaway to SB for our anniversary and he booked a room here.
