text: CAUTION. This agency screams scam. I can only tell you what I experienced. A friend recommended E&A as a way to get out and socialize in a new area, or with people who share common interests. I went to their site and found it locked down -with prompts to fill out a form. So I did, curious to see where it went. I got a call the very next day and was treated to the classic sales lure. I was asked a few questions about my age, job, etc. Although I answered them, I kept it generic enough to retain some privacy. However, I was beginning to *smell* the build up. And sure enough, I was flattered and promised impossible things. I was told I would meet QUALITY people, like myself. I was advised that they weren't like other social groups - which let ANYONE join. ?? really? What type of screening do they perform? I was advised that they liked to meet people and interview them to see if they are the type of people that should join their club. I asked what the qualifications are, but they dodged the answer, assuring me I was clearly their type of people and I wasn't going to have any problems joining their club. I kept getting that odd sense of elitist. I wasn't sure if the "special" nature of the members was racial, cultural, or financial. I asked what it would cost and got the next red flag: I wouldn't be told what the cost was to join. But I was assured it was affordable. I was told the fee was to help ensure that the members were QUALITY members. [Really? what exactly are "quality" members?] I was told that joining this group would open the calendar to me and expose me to lots of activities and fun! I asked if the events were free with the membership. NO. "most of the events do not cost more than $25". So if I understand this offer, I have to pay a membership fee in order to even SEE THE CALENDAR of events. And this fee is, according to the agent, a method of deterring some element of the populace. And so I must assume it is a financial deterrent, which means the ones who can pay are clearly QUALITY people. Then you get to pay for each event in addition. I started to hesitate about attending, and was treated again to a special courtesy... my agent moved other appointments around to accommodate my schedule. [Why?] I agreed to the appointment and ended the call. I received the email. This is the copied/pasted quote exactly out of the email: But people love Events and Adventures for the QUALITY of our members. Note the emphasis. It is bolded and underlined in my email. Something is wrong. I then googled this agency and checked with the BBB in other states (PA is fairly new). Everyone cautions that this agency requires a contract (never told to me over the phone), that it costs more than 1.5k to join (again, no details provided over the phone), and there is even a monthly fee on top of the event fees. I emailed my agent to cancel my appointment. I encourage everyone to research this agency/club/group before signing a single piece of paper. They used the classic 'flattery / special' statements to boost your ego and QUALITY, while insisting on a face to face interview. Which, if you know about sales pitches, is the best method of intimidating and pressuring you into signing paperwork and giving over money.
label: NEG

text: This place darn near ruined my perfectly good trip to the East Coast with my Dad. If there were a prize for the worst service, worst value and the worst overall customer experience, Harry the K's would win the triple crown. My dad and I walked into the ballpark right as the gates opened, 90 minutes before the 7:05 pm game. After a leisurely stroll around the ballpark we made it to Harry the K's by about 5:50. The place was pretty full, but the hostess showed us to our table. It was a tiny, slanted, wobbly, cramped table with no view of the field. We didn't mind, however, because it wasn't a 5-star establishment; it was a place to get some food before the game. At a place like this, I only expect two things: cold drinks and fast service. We sat and sat there, and the only interaction we've had with the waitstaff was a semi-polite "excuse me, could you move up a little bit, please - I can't get through" from a waitress serving other customers. After 12-15 minutes of waiting, we flagged down the waitress and asked her if we could place an order. "Not my table," she said, "but let me get your waiter, Steve." Steve showed up 3 minutes later. He was a gentleman in his 50s with a gray ponytail. He reluctantly took our order (drinks and food), then went over to two of his other tables and took their orders as well. 5 minutes later, the other two tables had their drinks and one - even appetizers. We had nothing, except for 2 plates with ketchup stains on them. 10 minutes later, I called the same waitress who had located Steve for us. I asked her if I could please speak to the manager, because it is absolutely unacceptable. She, being the nice woman she was, told us that "Steve has had an awful day, and his boss yelled at him in the morning. Some people can take it, but Steve can't. Let me get the drinks for you." I sure hope Steve is reading this, and he appreciates the coworker that he has. Otherwise, Steve might have been fired that day. She brought our drinks and our appetizer which was NOT worth $16, not even by the ballpark standards. 2 small rolls, 4 chicken wings a couple of celery sticks and 4 other tiny things for $16!!! Steve walked by our table with the look of disgust on his face. I am not sure what my father or I had done to him, or anyone, to deserve that. He continued bringing food to all the tables but ours. He deliberately ignored our table to the point that I felt I was being discriminated against. We complained to the same waitress one more time, and she got Steve to bring us the food. My dad had the brisket, while I ordered the cheesesteak. The food was average, but pretty decent by ballpark standards. Steve brought my dad a fork and a knife, but nothing for me. I asked him for the utensils, and he asked me "you want a fork and a knife, too?" Dude, it's not like you donated a kidney to my dad and I asked you for the second one. Unbelievable. After a couple more requests, he brought me another diet coke ("on the house") and a check. The check for our meal (a brisket, a cheesesteak, a $16 crappy appetizer, a diet coke and a glass of Yuengling) was $50.09. I left him exactly $50.10 and walked out in disgust. Anyone can have a bad day--heck, I am having one right now--but there's no excuse for not doing your job and disrespecting fellow human beings. We did nothing to deserve this, and his behavior was uncalled for. I would have, and should have, complained to the manager. Fortunately for Steve, the game was about to start. Besides, I didn't want to make a scene with my Dad in attendance.

In order to try and be as kill-free as they possibly can be some of their animals are often transfered to "rescues" such as greyhound rescues throughout PA and the Jersey area. It just bothers me every time I'm dropping off food to see the irresponsible low lifes turning over their animals because they just don't want them anymore. A lot of people prefer to go to Morris because they are somewhat of a no-kill shelter, but then at the same time a cat or dog from the SPCA will be put to sleep. text: The Hubby and I enjoy going out on culinary adventures to find new and fresh food whenever we go out of town. Just a couple of weeks ago, we went down to St. Petersburg for the day and we found this cute cafe tucked away in a beautiful neighborhood in the downtown area. Its "fresh bread" signs posted up on the display window were so inviting that we did not hesitate to go in at all. Like many reviews here state, the inside decor was very welcoming and " homey". It really did make us feel as if we had just gone to grandma's for Sunday brunch. We were very much entertained looking at the antique collection throughout the restaurant while we waited on our food. Although the service was great, it was not enough to make up for the food itself, which I considered well below average. For starters, I ordered "traditional" eggs Benedict, which are supposed to be poached eggs on a toasted English muffin. My eggs were fried, on an English muffin that had become soggy from the heaping amount of hollandaise poured on top of it. The breakfast included "fresh fruit", and considering the name of the restaurant, this seemed like a safe item to order, and yet i got a small ramekin with fruit medley from a can. At this point I looked forward to my "soup of the day" in hopes it could make my breakfast a little more enjoyable. Unfortunately, the cream of corn soup was not very good either. It simply tasted like canned corn mixed with evaporated canned milk and thrown together without any additional seasoning. The hubby ordered a veggie sandwich with pesto and that tasted ok. I ended up eating his food. On a good note, the pesto was very tasty and it really added a kick to what would have otherwise been an ordinary leafy greens veggie sandwich with carrots and sprouts. After our breakfast was served, the waiter asked us how everything was and I did let him know that I did not enjoy my eggs benedict. I believe he told the owner,"Angie", because she came to our table and offered up some dessert on the house. Let me be very clear, from the moment I walked into this little place, I was charmed by the decor and the service. I can tell that the owners have a passion for food and they really want to bring something fresh and original to the community, for that they should be commended. However, I hope that they work on their food and make sure that they serve what is promised in the menu. If they do that, I have no doubt that this place will be around for many years to come.

text: Sotto Varalli serves southern Italian restaurant on the Avenue of the Arts. It lies beneath Upstares [sic] at Varalli, owned by the same folks. True to its name, "sotto" is Italian for "under" (or beneath, rather) and Varalli is a proper noun, I think. Get it? The decor is very 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea. Water was streaming down the walls, there was a giant squid looking down upon the bar, "S" door handles and light fixtures about the interior - the underwater theme was unusual. There was an absence of music which I found refreshing. The clink of glasses, the noise of traffic and the murmur of conversations accompanied our meals. There were young and attractive servers, the exception our OWN waiter, who was neither young or attractive. His personality was flamboyant (he was a toucher!) but he paid attention to his customers. The service was exemplary for lunch! Our table was served by more than one person and as soon as my water became low the hostess came by with a pitcher. If only the food was as good as the service! We started with the complimentary Foccia bread with a slice of ridged butter. We ordered entree sizes for our dishes which was a mistake - a small portion would have been enough for lunch. Lunch came in less than 15 minutes. The black linguini was cooked with chunks of crab meat (tasted slightly raw... ick!), mushrooms, strong basil, and cheese. I didn't finish it...(!) The risotto (with sausage and peas) had plenty of meat, was tender and slightly seasoned. A wholesome, simple meal and not overpowering, it's not enough to excite the palate but it filled us up. If you like southern Italian food, you can do better in South Philadelphia! If you're not an Italian food junkie (like me), approach with caution. If you're looking for pre-theatre food, I've yet to find a place in that area that I would recommend. Since that lunch, I have eaten here twice (both for dinner) - once as recently as last October - and I still stand by two stars.
label: NEG

text: OK, for those not from Tucson (or the SW), or for those new to town, there's a fascinating tradition of shrines around the area that were new to this NY native when I moved here. A (morbid?) curiosity overcomes me as I travel along Hwy 86 and see the shrines along the way, marking tragedy in the lives of some unknown-to-me soul. But here at El Tiradito Shrine, you can easily walk up to the location and visit for as long as you wish. And unlike so many of the other shrines located around the Old Pueblo, this one has a story you can learn (I won't bother to repost the historic info, just check other reviews). And while, like the other shrines, this one has a personal origin, it really has evolved into a remembrance for all sinners--all of us who are, well, humans. Located so close to the TCC, Cushing Street, and El Minuto, you don't necessarily even have to make a specific trip to visit the shrine. text: This was a great place, but you can't appreciate it without the timeline of events... We get through the forest area, into an open grassland, and still no butterflies... We made it all the way to the beach, a most beautiful view of the islands. On the way back from the cliffs, we made it back to the preserve, and saw two butterflies.... Wow, and then another one, and another one... We started seeing more of the sun come out and then suddenly the handful of butterflies turned into 10's and hundreds, then we saw clusters... What is a cluster? So imagine looking up and seeing what you think is a branch with a bunch of leaves on it, and then realizing that the leaves are moving... When you zoom in to the 'leaves' you realize that every single one of them is a set of orange monarch butterfly wings. Very cool place, very fun for kids to run around, but the butterfly experience was amazing, you just have to wait for it.

What I got was a pile of baby carrots, frozen broccoli and cauliflower on top of some penne and a literal oil slick. Huh?! It's The freaking HIll, ground zero for the Italians in St. Louis! My husband had the filet mignon with a twice-baked potato which was better, but not Italian. We had ice cream pie with amaretto/chocolate sauce on top which I thought was pretty good, but it was probably because the pasta was so disturbingly bad... Good wine, though. And shit, the whole thing was free, so I guess I shouldn't be bitching that much...
label: NEG

text: The only reason I can even give Kopperman's two stars is because the location is great. The place is filthy, the waiters are crabby and rude, I don't think the mimosas had any champagne in them, and the food is boring and below average. Sticky tables, no elbow room and grumpy staff? No thanks.
label: NEG

text: I called in a takeout order this past Sunday. They forgot to put spicy mustard, lettuce, AND tomato on my friend's grilled chicken sandwich. Additionally, the chicken had a fair amount of gristle and fat attached to it making it less than appetizing. I was given the wrong sandwich. Hymie's was nice enough to deliver two fresh sandwiches - correctly done this time (my friend did name drop so this could have had something to do with their being SO nice about correcting the snafu). My fresh sandwich did have the avocado that was promised but it was all centralized on about a third of the sandwich. Eh, needless to say, I wasn't that crazy about the food. There is a new place, Katz's that just opened two weeks ago over in Bala Cynwyd but they aren't staying open on weekends until September - I'll give them a try then.
label: NEG

text: This is a great place in a great neighborhood. We came here one Saturday evening for a date night. The weather was lovely so we sat outside on their patio (enchanting). There was live music being played (a little twang country for my tastes, but charming none-the-less). We ordered their quesadilla to share and each had a house salad. Their house salad is scrumptious--fresh and crisp with varied veggies (much better than the iceberg/hothouse tomato standby that many places seem to serve). The quesadilla was delish. I enjoyed a glass of wine (can't remember which, but it was solid). And, my husband ordered one of the 15 beers they have on tap. Overall a lovely place for a date. We enjoyed our light meal, and then headed across the street to Goody's to top it off with some ice cream. Love life in Hyde!
label: POS

text: Having never visited Philly before I had to stop and try from both Geno's and Pat's. I ordered the exact same at both--cheesesteak wit onions and cheese whiz. Since I had already eaten my Pat's first and loving every bite (at Pat's with no evidence of me being there) I approached Geno's for an order to take back on the plane. The woman behind the counter was rude and not pleasant at all. The food was okay but the service at Pat's was overwhelmingly positive compared to this place.
label: NEG

text: These guys are top notch. I used Don's Pharmacy before Sierra compounders opened because they were the only compounders in the area. Thank god for Sierra Compounders because now I never have to deal with Don's again... not to mention they are on my side of town!! Sierra Compounders is everything Don's isn't. Polite. Prompt. Professional. Clean. Don's had knick knacks and products all over their store and you could barely weave your way to the counter. Sierra's is clean and has a great layout. They are EXTREMELY prompt (24 hour turn around even when refill permission was needed from Dr). They always call as soon as the medicine is ready instead of waiting for me to call and "double check" as Don's used to do. I've only used them for medicine for my cat so far but with their excellent service I may switch my own medications to them. They always supply extra syringes for my cats meds and put the medicine inside an outer bag filled with ice to ensure there are no temperature fluctuations as I travel home. I trust them and feel they are a top notch pharmacy and will continue to give them my business.
label: POS

text: I went to this place for breakfast with a girlfriend on a Friday morning while we were in town for the CMA Music Fest. With the crowd in town that week, I figured we would have long lines but it was no wait at all. I ordered an omelet and it was really good. The biscuits were also very tasty and the service was great. My favorite thing was the blackberry jam. I have never really liked blackberry jam because of the seeds but this was so good I bought a jar for myself and 4 others to give away for Father's Day. I have hear from each person I gave a jar to and they liked it as well. I also bought biscuit mix to make at home, and while they were not exactly like the restaurant, they were pretty good.
label: POS

text: What is it that makes a place great? Is is the atmosphere, the food, the service, a combination of all of these? I wasn't sure after I ate here. I had heard, to quote, that La Strada was "Named one of the top 10 Italian restaurants in the nation." That seems impressive, and in fact, I had thought that all of the elements that I listed above would be great, and really, only the atmosphere was. Perhaps the key here is to stress this point about its "top ten" status (in whose poll, BTW? As named in the "Favorite non-Olive Garden Italian restaurant for people who mainly eat at the Olive Garden?" poll) and then you will BELIEVE that you are eating the finest food in the country. An experiment in mind control?
label: NEG

text: Seriously, this is not delicious food. I had the Blackened Salmon over Succotash, and it was just so obviously not fresh it was sad. Pathetic, wrinkly lima beans and shriveled corn kernels. It looked like cafeteria food. Maybe it's my fault for ordering summer vegetables in the wintertime, but really it's their fault for serving it.
label: NEG

text: These folks went above and beyond in taking care of my mother-in-laws vehicle and I cannot say enough good things about their professional service. The car broke down going through Nashville and they worked closely with me (I sorta manage all things car related for my mother-in-law) to make sure the issues were solved and we were taken care of. Great above-expectation service. Jimmy in service is a rockstar and his manager, Cameron, is top notch. If you have a GMC or Pontiac, these are your guys!

text: Went twice in the 48 hours we were in Nashville. Sure, everyone says it's touristy, but everyone who told us that in the bar was a Nashville local. So... does not compute, I guess. I didn't actually meet many other tourists. Yes, it was busy, but I'd rather be in a busy bar than an empty one. The music was excellent. We had a blast dancing upstairs, both on and off the stage. The drinks were ridiculous. They were SUPER expensive, but at least they were also SUPER strong. I was irritated when one not-so-helpful bartender charged me $2 for a water "ever since the flood." I would happily go back today. Alas, I'm back in KC...
label: POS

text: I was tipped off to Jacques-Imo's Cafe by my sister. She said it was one of the best meals she'd ever had, and she was right. A short wait in the crazy (in a good way) bar allowed us to down a Abita Turbo Dog and take in the wonderful smells from the kitchen. As we were escorted through the kitchen to our table we got our first glimpse of the wonderful food that awaited us. The Alligator cheesecake, a house specialty, was delicious. That was followed by the Drum with crawfish etouffee cooked perfectly. The waiter was pushing desserts but we declined as we were stuffed. As a nice gesture, the waiter brought bite-sized pieces of chocolate cheesecake for the table. One taste made me wish I'd saved room for dessert. There's always next time...
label: POS

text: PJs iced coffee is delicious and this location is no exception. Service was surly and disinterested. Very small location with just a few uncomfortable tables and harsh track lighting. Definitely not a study spot - better for to-go coffee.
label: NEG

text: Vino 100 Reno is under new ownership and has a great new look. There is seating for you to enjoy a glass of wine at the bar or in a quite corner in the store. A great place to meet others and enjoy a glass of wine. There are more changes to follow. Be sure to check Vino 100 out
label: POS

text: My visit to the Olive Garden was my last. Call me ignorant, but am I supposed to know that the salad is free? When my friend and I were seated, we were asked if we would like salad. We didn't have a lot of money, and we didn't know it was free, so we said no. Then I starting thinking that it must be free, so I asked the waiter if we could have the salad. He said no and that it was too late, because the food was about to be served. Well, we both felt embarrassed and actually felt like leaving. I mean, why wouldn't he tell us it was free and why would be then refuse it to us? Apparently, there are bread sticks too? We didn't get those either. Anyway, when the food came, I wasn't impressed anyway. I got the fettuccine alfredo, and it seriously tasted like someone had just plopped a bunch of pasta on a plate and then pour a bunch of sauce on. Is this restaurant food? It tasted like something from a package that I could make at home. I've had better at Boston Pizza. Overall, a bad experience, and I just got the sense that this place is somewhat snobby and overrated. I won't be back.
label: NEG

text: Walked into this place psyched by the rock n roll spirit it exuded - although in retrospect I was also slightly disturbed by its weird fanaticism - and left with a residue of too much pomade and a general feeling of awkwardness. The proprietor of Twist told me at the beginning of our weird hour-long exchange that my cut would cost only 35 and I left paying 45 (not including tip). My attempts to make small talk, "where ya from, what do you like to do for fun?", were rebuffed with, "listen babe, my business is my business and I like to keep it that way. You wanna talk rock n' roll, let's talk about the kinks or the stones, but I like to keep my business private." Uh...what? *crickets chirping* ------------------------------------------------------ Top that off with being overcharged by ten dollars for a haircut that really wasn't what I wanted you can bet I vented about to two different friends...their response? One had a friend or two and other the personal experience to vindicate my claims. Butchered hair and uncomfortable interaction.

text: Yum. Went in today for a wrap at lunch. I ordered the Bourbon Salmon Wrap and it was fantastic. Plenty of salad, salmon, walnuts and dressing. If you can eat one of these things and not be filled up then you are a stud. As always, the ordering line at the salads/wrap station at 12:30 was long. Beware if you have a time-restricted lunch break. There was nobody in line at the sandwich station.

text: Seriously people, read the reviews below! I mean READ IT. Most come from the "late night drunk people". Nothing against them because I am one of them too but when you are drunk, EVERYTHING tastes good. This time, I was sober. Yelped this place while I was at Sand Bar [another crap establishment]. Had the Bratwurst and wow, it tasted like well.... I could get 5 Bratwursts on sale at Safeway/Vons for the same price and tastes 10x better. To add to this, every single hot dog stand in the middle of the street I have tried tasted better than Mad Dogs. I guess I'll give this place 1 star for opening up business in a college town where 90% of the people that come eat will be drunk.

text: John has surely re-invented the 'dive' bar. Coining the very name itself it caters to both locals, hipsters, and probably some sea captains. This place is too hard to describe that you literally just have to walk in and see for yourself. There's an upstairs area now open again where sometimes djs spin and a third floor hidden pool table. The bonus of getting some booze and chatting it up with some friends is the wonderful free pizza provided for your service. Though don't be greedy, two slices per person, but after 7pm it's up for grabs. Where else will you get beer with free pizza? John, usually the bartender most nights, will greet you and have some very amazing stories to share for you or just listen to the stories he's already shouting as he runs up and down the walk tapping glasses and exchanging smiles. So if you're feeling like a rogue pirate or um not... just pop inside and get ready to watch 'The Simpsons' on the big screen as your sipping down a cold one with PIZZA!

text: The first (and only) time I've ever sent food back. I wanted to like this place so badly. I loved the kitchy decor, loved the outdoor seating, thought the waitstaff was friendly and attentive . . . but the food! My ground beef taco was mostly luke-warm gray slop that seemed to have been put through a blender. The queso looked like it was 80% lard and didn't taste any better. I don't drink alcohol, and that seems to be a key to this place -- a friend has since told me that everyone goes here for drinks & atmosphere. I am a picky eater, I'm often served things that I'm not able to appreciate properly, and I always assume the problem is *me*. This food was so gross, there was no way for me to take the blame. Seriously. Gross.

text: I live in S.F., enjoy Thai, and was visiting St Louis so my mom suggested Blue Elephant for lunch. The chicken Phad Thai and Pad See-U were great but not spicy at all. They would be a great way to introduce someone to Thai. Friendly, quick service!
label: POS

text: As a local, I've visited Miller's Ale House frequently with friends and coworkers when there's a big sporting event. Go Eagles! If the beer/drink specials, big screen TV's and bar food was may main goal of visiting, they'd probably get 4 stars. Unfortunately, there's also sit down dining... I've eaten here three times and chalked up my first two below-average visits to the restaurant being busy or understaffed. Sadly, they appear to be always understaffed and the quality of the food and preparation is below average. My most recent (and last) sit-down visit was on St. Patrick's Day. I was excited to see Irish specials such as corned beef ruebens, corned beef and cabbage, and Irish stew. The Guinness ($4.95) was also flowing, which is a wonderful thing. Within 10 minutes, my party was seated. So far so good. We ordered the Zingers (boneless buffalo chicken) and the spinich dip with chips. This is a very safe start since it's essentially bar food. Sadly, it took about 15 minutes for what should be prepared spinach dip and some tortilla chips. My corned beef rueben (side of fries) arrived about 20 minutes later. Although tiny in size by NY deli standards, it looked delicious. Then I took a bite in to the fattiest corned beef I had ever eaten... or attempted to eat. I looked over at my eating companions' plate and saw that their corned beef and cabbage meal was lined with thick, white fat, which was probably what my baby Rueben contained as well. I spent the next few minutes, deconstructing my sandwich, in an attempt to carve off as much fat as possible. I'll spare you the details of what the little pile of blubber on my plate looked like. The grand finale of this awesomely bad meal was the Irish coffee that I ordered. It came to me about 15 minutes after ordered in a clear coffee mug with no whipped cream on top. Seriously? It's St. Patrick's Day and you can't get a simple Irish coffee right? The waitress offered to bring out a cup of whipped cream on the side, but at that point, I was defeated and didn't want to wait another 15 minutes for that, too. In summary, if you're going to Miller's to drink and watch the game on their many big screens, go for it. The two stars that I gave Miller's is for that alone. If you're looking for a quality sit-down meal with friends or family, I'd think twice. There are many, many reasonably priced establishments in a 1 mile radius that will do a far better job.
label: NEG

text: I had just moved to Philly and was looking for a salon. I randomly picked Luna because it seemed trendy without being overpriced. I have gone twice for a hair cut and was extremely happy with the results! I have thick hair, which most people don't know how to deal with, but Mae is an expert. I barely have to describe what I want and she understands and also puts her creative spin on it. Around $50 per cut is a small price to pay when you know you're going to get great results! I would definitely recommend Luna (ask for Mae) to a friend.
